knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Model Adequacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order fidelity of a smooth trust-region model, measured by the ratio of actual to predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(x\). Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and define \(m(p)=f(x)+\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Bp\). For every \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(m(0)-m(p)>0\), define
\[
\rho(p)=\frac{f(x)-f(x+p)}{m(0)-m(p)}.
\]
Let \((p_j)_{j\ge1}\) be a sequence of nonzero vectors such that \(p_j\to0\) and \(m(0)-m(p_j)\ge c\lVert p_j\rVert\) for every \(j\ge1\) and some \(c>0\). Then \(\rho(p_j)\to1\). Consequently, for every fixed \(\eta\in\mathbb{R}\) with \(\eta<1\), the inequality \(\rho(p_j)\ge\eta\) holds eventually; thus any acceptance rule that accepts whenever this inequality holds eventually accepts these steps. Values of \(\rho\) far below one signal inadequate local prediction under this ratio diagnostic and motivate reducing the trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonzero steps converging to zero whose predicted decrease is bounded below proportionally to their length, the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio approaches one. Therefore, any rule that accepts a step when this ratio exceeds a fixed threshold below one eventually accepts such steps; ratios far below one signal poor local prediction and motivate a smaller trust region.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(f\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(x\).
\((p_j)_{j\ge1}\) is a sequence of nonzero vectors satisfying \(p_j\to0\) and \(m(0)-m(p_j)\ge c\lVert p_j\rVert\) for every \(j\ge1\) and some \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(p_j)\to1\), and consequently \(\rho(p_j)\ge\eta\) eventually for every fixed \(\eta\in\mathbb{R}\) with \(\eta<1\).

Ratio of actual objective reduction to model-predicted reduction.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the objective. At iteration \(k\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\Delta_k>0\), let \(\|\cdot\|_k\) be a norm, and let \(m_k\) be a model defined on \(\mathcal B_k=\{x:\|x-x_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, model-based unconstrained minimization; the definition permits iteration-dependent norms and general smooth models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathfrak T=\bigl(\{x_k\},\{m_k\},\{\|\cdot\|_k\},\{\Delta_k\},\{s_k\},\{\rho_k\}\bigr)\] is a trust-region framework if, for every \(k\), \(\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\), \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\), \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)},\qquad x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&\rho_k\geq\eta_1,\\x_k,&\rho_k<\eta_1,\end{cases}\] for a fixed \(0<\eta_1<1\), and \(\Delta_{k+1}\) is selected from a prescribed control map depending on the agreement class of \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region framework consists of iterates, local models, trust-region norms and radii, feasible model-decreasing trial steps, an actual-to-predicted reduction ratio, an acceptance rule, and a radius-control rule. Each trial step lies in the current region. It is accepted when its ratio reaches the acceptance threshold; otherwise the iterate is retained. The next radius is selected according to the observed agreement between model and objective.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is defined on \(\mathcal B_k\), and the chosen trial step has strictly positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak T\) is precisely the restricted-model, agreement-tested, accept-or-reject, radius-controlled iteration specified above.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(q_k(s)=m_k(x_k+s)\), the region and predicted reduction become \(\{s:\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}\) and \(q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\), respectively.
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic model, \(m_k(x_k+s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\) with \(B_k=B_k^T\).
For the Euclidean geometry, \(\|s\|_k=\|s\|_2\) and \(\mathcal B_k\) is a ball.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\rho_k<0\), then \(f(x_k+s_k)>f(x_k)\), so any positive-threshold rule rejects the trial point.
The framework separates step quality, acceptance, and radius management into distinct mathematical components.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require exact minimization of the model.
Constrained, stochastic, derivative-free, and inexact-evaluation variants require additional feasibility or error conditions.

children.top_down_role: The basic restricted-step method family and the roles assigned to models, trial steps, acceptance, and region control.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\). Given \(x_k\), form \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k=B_k^T\), and choose \(0<\Delta_k\leq\widehat\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth, deterministic, unconstrained trust-region iteration with a quadratic model and Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[s_k\approx\arg\min_{\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k}m_k(s),\qquad \rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\] Given \(0\leq\eta<\tfrac14\), define \[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&\rho_k>\eta,\\x_k,&\rho_k\leq\eta,\end{cases}\quad \Delta_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\Delta_k/4,&\rho_k<1/4,\\\min\{2\Delta_k,\widehat\Delta\},&\rho_k>3/4\text{ and }\|s_k\|_2=\Delta_k,\\\Delta_k,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\] A sequence generated by these relations, with every \(s_k\) feasible and model decreasing, is a classical trust-region method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical method approximately minimizes a local quadratic model inside a Euclidean ball, compares actual and predicted objective reduction, accepts sufficiently reliable trial points, and contracts, retains, or expands the ball according to fixed ratio thresholds. Expansion is allowed only when agreement is strong and the computed step reaches the current boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at every generated iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed subproblem, ratio, iterate recurrence, and radius recurrence define the classical trust-region method.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The subproblem may be written \(\min_s g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\) subject to \(s^Ts\leq\Delta_k^2\), since the constant \(f(x_k)\) does not affect its minimizers.
special_cases_latex: Setting \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) gives the trust-region Newton method.
Setting \(B_k=0\) gives a radius-limited steepest-descent step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every radius satisfies \(0<\Delta_k\leq\widehat\Delta\).
A rejected step leaves the iterate unchanged but may change the radius.
boundary_notes: The constants \(1/4\), \(3/4\), \(1/4\), and \(2\) are canonical choices, not universal requirements.
Approximate subproblem solution requires a separate model-decrease condition for convergence analysis.

notation.meaning: Symmetric Hessian or Hessian approximation in the quadratic model.
Global upper bound on the trust-region radius.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model-decrease roles of trust-region trial steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(q(s)=q(0)+g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\) on \(\mathcal R(\Delta)=\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta\}\), define the predicted reduction \(D(s)=q(0)-q(s)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic, possibly nonconvex trust-region models; roles classify steps by the decrease certificate they provide, not by the numerical solver used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible step \(s\in\mathcal R(\Delta)\) has a Cauchy role if \(D(s)\geq\kappa_C D(s^C)\); a negative-curvature role if \(\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\) and \(D(s)\geq\kappa_E D(s^E)\); and a model-minimization role if \(D(s)\geq\kappa_M D(s^M)\), where \(s^C\) minimizes \(q\) on the feasible steepest-descent ray, \(s^E\) minimizes it on a feasible negative-curvature ray, \(s^M\in\arg\min_{\mathcal R(\Delta)}q\), and \(\kappa_C,\kappa_E,\kappa_M\in(0,1]\). A combined first/second-order role requires \[D(s)\geq\kappa\max\{D(s^C),D(s^E)\},\qquad \kappa\in(0,1].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trial-step roles are defined by which reference decrease the step matches. A Cauchy-role step captures a fixed fraction of steepest-descent decrease. A negative-curvature-role step captures a fixed fraction of eigenpoint decrease when the model is indefinite. A model-minimization-role step captures a fixed fraction of the globally best model decrease. A combined role must compare favorably with both first- and second-order references.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\), \(\Delta>0\), and the reference points exist in the closed region.
The negative-curvature role is invoked only when \(\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities above assign a trial step its model-decrease role independently of its construction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(D(s^M)\geq\max\{D(s^C),D(s^E)\}\), a model-minimization certificate with a sufficiently large fraction also supplies weaker reference-step certificates.
special_cases_latex: If \(H\succeq0\), the negative-curvature role is inactive.
An exact model minimizer has \(\kappa_M=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Role membership is invariant under adding a constant to \(q\).
A step can possess several roles simultaneously.
boundary_notes: The classification does not prescribe dogleg, conjugate-gradient, Lanczos, or factorization machinery.
A first-order role alone does not require exploitation of negative curvature.

notation.meaning: Predicted reduction produced by step s.
Cauchy, eigenpoint, and model-minimizer reference steps.

review_flags: The term “role” is formalized through the source's distinct Cauchy, eigenpoint, and model-minimizer decrease requirements.

children.title: Cauchy Reference-Step Family
children.top_down_role: First-order reference-step families used to calibrate acceptable model decrease.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(s)=q(0)+g^Ts+\tfrac12s^TBs\), with \(B=B^T\), \(g\neq0\), and Euclidean trust region \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\), \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic models in Euclidean geometry; the family includes exact and fraction-of-Cauchy reference steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Cauchy step is \[s^C=-\tau_C\frac{\Delta}{\|g\|_2}g,\qquad \tau_C=\begin{cases}1,&g^TBg\leq0,\\\min\left\{\dfrac{\|g\|_2^3}{\Delta g^TBg},1\right\},&g^TBg>0.\end{cases}\] Equivalently, \(s^C\in\arg\min\{q(-tg):t\geq0,\ t\|g\|_2\leq\Delta\}\). For \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\), the associated Cauchy reference-step family is \[\mathcal C_{\kappa_C}(q,\Delta)=\{s:\|s\|_2\leq\Delta,\ q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_C[q(0)-q(s^C)]\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Cauchy step minimizes the quadratic model along the feasible negative-gradient ray. It reaches the boundary when curvature along that ray is nonpositive or when the unconstrained ray minimizer lies outside the region; otherwise it stops at that ray minimizer. The corresponding reference-step family contains every feasible step whose predicted reduction is at least a fixed fraction of the Cauchy reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^C\) and \(\mathcal C_{\kappa_C}(q,\Delta)\) are defined by the displayed ray minimization and decrease comparison.
special_cases_latex: If \(B=0\), then \(s^C=-\Delta g/\|g\|_2\).
If \(g=0\), the conventional degenerate Cauchy step is \(s^C=0\); this case is excluded from the displayed quotient.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every \(s\in\mathcal C_{\kappa_C}\) has positive predicted reduction when \(g\neq0\).
boundary_notes: The Cauchy family supplies a first-order decrease baseline and need not exploit the most negative curvature direction.
For a non-Euclidean norm, the steepest feasible direction is determined by the corresponding dual-norm problem.

notation.meaning: Family of steps achieving a prescribed fraction of Cauchy decrease.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cauchy-Type Decrease from Standard Trust-Region Subproblem Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded decrease certificate for dogleg, two-dimensional subspace, and Steihaug trust-region steps, together with the Cauchy reference constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Steps \(p_k\) produced by the dogleg method, two-dimensional subspace minimization, or Steihaug's method satisfy, for some constant \(c_1\in(0,1]\),
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge c_1\lVert g_k\rVert\min\!\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\lVert g_k\rVert}{\lVert B_k\rVert}\right\}.
\]
The Cauchy point \(p_k^{\mathrm c}\) satisfies this estimate with \(c_1=\tfrac12\). A step obtaining a fixed positive fraction of the Cauchy reduction likewise retains a Cauchy-type decrease estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dogleg, two-dimensional subspace, and Steihaug subproblem solvers produce steps with a fixed Cauchy-type lower bound on model reduction. The Cauchy point has constant one half, and a fixed positive fraction of its reduction is sufficient for a corresponding bound.
assumptions_latex: p_k\text{ is produced by the dogleg, two-dimensional subspace, or Steihaug trust-region subproblem method}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c_1\in(0,1]:\ m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge c_1\lVert g_k\rVert\min\!\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\lVert g_k\rVert}{\lVert B_k\rVert}\right\};\qquad p_k=p_k^{\mathrm c}\Longrightarrow c_1=\tfrac12

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cauchy-Quality Reduction Suffices for Trust-Region Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative trust-region subproblem-accuracy principle. The extract states neither the quantitative decrease test nor the remaining global-convergence hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within a trust-region method satisfying the hypotheses of its global-convergence result, an exact solution of the trust-region subproblem is unnecessary: it is sufficient to choose a step \(p_k\) satisfying \(\lVert p_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\) and a sufficient model-reduction condition calibrated by the Cauchy point \(p_k^{\mathrm c}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subject to the applicable trust-region convergence assumptions, the model subproblem need not be solved exactly. A feasible approximate step with sufficient decrease measured against the Cauchy point is enough.
assumptions_latex: \(p_k\) is a trial step for a trust-region model \(m_k\) with radius \(\Delta_k\).
The model reduction satisfies the applicable Cauchy-point-based sufficient-reduction condition.
All other hypotheses of the applicable trust-region global-convergence result hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\arg\min_{\lVert p\rVert\leq\Delta_k}m_k(p)\) is not required for the stated global-convergence guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cauchy Point
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact Cauchy point minimizes the quadratic model along the feasible segment of the steepest-descent ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12 s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), where \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(\Delta>0\). The exact Cauchy point is \(s_C=-\alpha_C g\), with \(s_C=0\) when \(g=0\), and otherwise
\[
\alpha_C\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq\alpha\leq\Delta/\lVert g\rVert}q(-\alpha g).
\]
Equivalently, if \(g\neq0\), then
\[
\alpha_C=\begin{cases}
\Delta/\lVert g\rVert,&g^{\mathsf T}Bg\leq0,\\
\min\{\lVert g\rVert^2/(g^{\mathsf T}Bg),\,\Delta/\lVert g\rVert\},&g^{\mathsf T}Bg>0.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_C\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s=-\alpha g,\ 0\leq\alpha\lVert g\rVert\leq\Delta}q(s)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean trust-region Cauchy point for a quadratic model.

notation.meaning: Quadratic model without its irrelevant constant term.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form Cauchy point for the quadratic trust-region model in the nonzero-gradient regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), where \(\Delta_k>0\) and \(g_k\neq0\). Then
\[p_k^{\mathrm c}=-\tau_k\frac{\Delta_k}{\lVert g_k\rVert}g_k,\qquad
\tau_k=\begin{cases}
1,&g_k^TB_kg_k\leq0,\\
\min\!\left\{\dfrac{\lVert g_k\rVert^3}{\Delta_k g_k^TB_kg_k},1\right\},&g_k^TB_kg_k>0.
\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Cauchy point lies on the negative-gradient ray. It reaches the trust-region boundary when the directional curvature is nonpositive. With positive directional curvature, it is the earlier of the one-dimensional quadratic minimizer and the boundary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k^{\mathrm c}=-\tau_k(\Delta_k/\lVert g_k\rVert)g_k\) with \(\tau_k\) given by the stated curvature-dependent cases.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Limitation of Repeated Cauchy Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the Cauchy point's sufficient-decrease safeguard role from the curvature-sensitive step directions needed for rapid local convergence. The superlinear-rate language is an expectation, not a theorem in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Cauchy point satisfies \(p_k^{\mathrm c}\parallel-g_k\), with \(B_k\) affecting its length but not its direction. Consequently, always taking \(p_k^{\mathrm c}\) is a steepest-descent method with a particular step length and may perform poorly. Curvature-exploiting trust-region strategies are instead designed to select \(p_k^B=-B_k^{-1}g_k\) whenever \(B_k\succ0\) and \(\lVert p_k^B\rVert\leq\Delta_k\); when \(B_k\) is the exact Hessian or a suitable quasi-Newton approximation, the extract states that superlinear convergence can be expected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated Cauchy steps retain the negative-gradient direction, so curvature changes only their length and they inherit steepest descent's potential slowness. Improved trust-region steps use curvature in the direction and are designed to take the feasible full Newton-type step; the source presents superlinear convergence in the Hessian or quasi-Newton setting only as an expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(p_k^{\mathrm c}\) is the Cauchy point of the quadratic trust-region model.
For the full-step selection clause, \(B_k\succ0\) and \(p_k^B=-B_k^{-1}g_k\).
For the local-rate expectation, \(B_k\) is the exact Hessian or a suitable quasi-Newton approximation carrying valid curvature information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated Cauchy steps use the steepest-descent direction; curvature-sensitive improvement strategies select the feasible full step \(p_k^B\) and may thereby support faster local convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage construction of the exact Cauchy reference point for a trust-region model at a nonstationary iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose
\[p_k^{\mathrm s}\in\arg\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{f_k+g_k^Tp:\lVert p\rVert\leq\Delta_k\right\}.\]
Then choose
\[\tau_k\in\arg\min_{\tau\geq0}\left\{m_k(\tau p_k^{\mathrm s}):\lVert\tau p_k^{\mathrm s}\rVert\leq\Delta_k\right\},\]
and set \(p_k^{\mathrm c}=\tau_kp_k^{\mathrm s}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First minimize the linearized model over the trust-region ball. Then minimize the full model along the feasible portion of the resulting ray and scale the linearized-model step by that minimizing scalar.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a trust-region model whose linear term is \(g_k^Tp\).
\(g_k\neq0\), as required for the positive ray minimizer used in this construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k^{\mathrm c}=\tau_kp_k^{\mathrm s}\), where \(p_k^{\mathrm s}\) solves the linearized trust-region problem and \(\tau_k\) minimizes \(m_k\) along its feasible ray.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Cauchy Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Cauchy step is feasible and attains a fixed positive fraction of the exact Cauchy-point model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and exact Cauchy point \(s_C\), a vector \(s\) is an approximate Cauchy step with constant \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\) if
\[
\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta
\quad\text{and}\quad
q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_C\bigl(q(0)-q(s_C)\bigr).
\]
The constant \(\kappa_C\) is required to be bounded away from zero uniformly over the trust-region iterations in which this condition is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_C\bigl(q(0)-q(s_C)\bigr)\) with \(\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease condition for an inexact trial step.

knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy Decrease Comparisons
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cauchy reduction is bounded below by a gradient-radius term, limited by curvature; fractional Cauchy steps inherit the bound proportionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), with \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(s_C\) be the exact Cauchy point for radius \(\Delta>0\). Then
\[
q(0)-q(s_C)\geq\tfrac12\lVert g\rVert\min\left\{\Delta,\frac{\lVert g\rVert}{\lVert B\rVert_2}\right\},
\]
where the second argument is interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(\lVert B\rVert_2=0\). Consequently, every approximate Cauchy step \(s\) with fraction \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\) satisfies the same bound multiplied by \(\kappa_C\).
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta\) and \(q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_C(q(0)-q(s_C))\) for the approximate-step conclusion
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(s)\geq\tfrac{\kappa_C}{2}\lVert g\rVert\min\{\Delta,\lVert g\rVert/\lVert B\rVert_2\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard lower bound for exact and fractional Cauchy decrease.

notation.meaning: Spectral norm of the symmetric model matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative transfer from a Cauchy-relative decrease condition to the standard trust-region decrease certificate, including the exact-subproblem case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0<c_2\le1\), let \(\lVert p_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\), and suppose
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge c_2\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k^{\mathrm c})\bigr).
\]
Then
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge \frac{c_2}{2}\lVert g_k\rVert\min\!\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\lVert g_k\rVert}{\lVert B_k\rVert}\right\}.
\]
In particular, an exact solution \(p_k^*\) of the trust-region subproblem satisfies this estimate with \(c_1=\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible trust-region step attaining at least a fraction c2 of the Cauchy-point reduction satisfies the standard decrease estimate with constant c2 divided by two. An exact subproblem solution satisfies it with constant one half.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge \frac{c_2}{2}\lVert g_k\rVert\min\!\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\lVert g_k\rVert}{\lVert B_k\rVert}\right\};\qquad p_k=p_k^*\Longrightarrow c_1=\tfrac12

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dogleg path minimization and Cauchy decrease bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-decrease guarantee for the residual least-squares dogleg step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose $J_k$ is nonsingular and
\[
m_k(p)=\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal P_k=\bigl([0,p_k^{\mathrm c}]\cup[p_k^{\mathrm c},p_k^{\mathrm J}]\bigr)\cap\{p:\|p\|\leq\Delta_k\}.
\]
The classical dogleg step satisfies
\[
p_k\in\arg\min_{p\in\mathcal P_k}m_k(p).
\]
Consequently, it achieves at least Cauchy-point model reduction, and for some $c_1>0$,
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\geq c_1\|J_k^Tr_k\|\min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|J_k^Tr_k\|}{\|J_k^TJ_k\|}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the residual Jacobian is nonsingular, the dogleg step minimizes the least-squares model over the portion of the two-segment dogleg path lying inside the trust region. Its model reduction therefore matches or exceeds the Cauchy-point reduction and satisfies the stated lower bound for some positive c1.
assumptions_latex: p_k\text{ is selected by the classical dogleg procedure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k\in\arg\min_{p\in\mathcal P_k}m_k(p),\quad m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\geq c_1\|J_k^Tr_k\|\min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|J_k^Tr_k\|}{\|J_k^TJ_k\|}\right\}\text{ for some }c_1>0.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(s)=q(0)+g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\), where \(H=H^T\) has \(\tau=\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\), and let \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex quadratic trust-region models; second-order reference means explicit exploitation of negative model curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(u\) with \(\|u\|=\Delta\), \(g^Tu\leq0\), and \(u^THu\leq\kappa_{nc}\tau\Delta^2\), where \(0<\kappa_{nc}\leq1\). The eigenpoint reference step is \[s^E=t_Eu,\qquad t_E\in\arg\min_{0<t\leq1}q(tu).\] For a quadratic model these sign and curvature conditions imply \(t_E=1\). For \(0<\kappa_E\leq1\), the second-order reference-step family is \[\mathcal E_{\kappa_E}(q,\Delta)=\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta,\ q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_E[q(0)-q(s^E)]\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order reference direction has trust-region length, is oriented so its linear contribution is nonincreasing, and captures a fixed fraction of the model's most negative curvature. Minimizing the quadratic along that ray produces the eigenpoint, which lies on the boundary. The associated family contains feasible trial steps attaining a prescribed fraction of the eigenpoint's predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: The sign of \(u\) is selected so that \(g^Tu\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^E\) and \(\mathcal E_{\kappa_E}(q,\Delta)\) constitute the negative-curvature second-order reference family.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an exact unit eigenvector \(v\) of \(H\) for \(\tau\), one may take \(u=\pm\Delta v\), choosing the sign so that \(g^Tu\leq0\), with \(\kappa_{nc}=1\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g=0\), either sign is admissible and the decrease is purely curvature-driven.
If \(H\succeq0\), this negative-curvature family is inactive.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(q(0)-q(s^E)\geq-\tfrac12\kappa_{nc}\tau\Delta^2>0\).
A step satisfying both Cauchy and eigenpoint comparisons carries combined first- and second-order model-decrease information.
boundary_notes: The definition concerns model curvature, which need not equal objective curvature unless a Hessian-fidelity condition is imposed.
Convex-model Newton or dogleg references belong to a different second-order regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenpoint Reference Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eigenpoint minimizes the model along a signed leftmost-eigenvector segment and reaches the boundary when negative curvature is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), where \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\), and choose a unit eigenvector \(u\) satisfying \(Bu=\lambda_{\min}(B)u\). Select its sign so that \(g^{\mathsf T}u\leq0\). An eigenpoint reference step is
\[
s_E=\alpha_Eu,
\qquad
\alpha_E\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq\alpha\leq\Delta}q(\alpha u).
\]
If \(\lambda_{\min}(B)<0\), the univariate quadratic is concave, so its minimum over the segment occurs at \(\alpha_E=\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(s_E)=\min_{0\leq\alpha\leq\Delta}q(\alpha u)\) and \(\lVert s_E\rVert\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary reference step along a leftmost-eigenvector direction.

notation.meaning: Smallest eigenvalue of the symmetric model matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Reference Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signed approximate leftmost-eigenvector boundary step guarantees model decrease proportional to the magnitude of negative curvature and the squared radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(B)<0\). For \(\kappa_{nc}\in(0,1]\), choose a unit vector \(u\) such that
\[
u^{\mathsf T}Bu\leq-\kappa_{nc}\lvert\lambda_{\min}(B)\rvert
\quad\text{and}\quad
g^{\mathsf T}u\leq0.
\]
Then \(s_{nc}=\Delta u\) is a negative-curvature reference step. It is feasible and satisfies
\[
q(0)-q(s_{nc})\geq\tfrac12\kappa_{nc}\Delta^2\lvert\lambda_{\min}(B)\rvert.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert s_{nc}\rVert=\Delta\) and \(q(0)-q(s_{nc})\geq\tfrac12\kappa_{nc}\Delta^2\lvert\lambda_{\min}(B)\rvert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable model-decrease condition based on approximate negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Reference-Step Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated quadratic trust-region model, compute a Cauchy reference candidate and, when negative curvature exists, a negative-curvature candidate; return whichever feasible candidate produces the larger model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), where \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let \(\Delta>0\). Compute a feasible Cauchy reference candidate \(s_C\), either the exact Cauchy point or an approximate Cauchy step satisfying the prescribed Cauchy-decrease condition. If \(\lambda_{\min}(B)<0\), compute a feasible eigenpoint or admissible negative-curvature candidate \(s_{nc}\); otherwise set \(s_{nc}=0\). Select
\[
s_R\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in\{s_C,s_{nc}\}}\bigl(q(0)-q(v)\bigr).
\]
Return \(s_R\). It is feasible and realizes the larger of the two candidate model reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert s_R\rVert\leq\Delta\) and \(q(0)-q(s_R)=\max\{q(0)-q(s_C),q(0)-q(s_{nc})\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection between first-order and negative-curvature reference decreases for a quadratic trust-region model.

notation.meaning: Quadratic model without its irrelevant constant term.
Exact or admissible approximate Cauchy reference candidate.
Negative-curvature reference candidate, or zero when no negative-curvature candidate is used.

children.title: Model-Step Quality Classes
children.top_down_role: Trial-step families providing stronger model improvement than the reference-step baseline.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a continuous model \(q\) on the compact region \(\mathcal R(\Delta)=\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta\}\), let \(D(s)=q(0)-q(s)\), let \(s^C\) be a Cauchy reference, and let \(s^M\in\arg\min_{\mathcal R(\Delta)}q\). If the model is indefinite, also let \(s^E\) be an eigenpoint reference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic trust-region subproblems; quality is ordered by certified predicted reduction rather than by distance to an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constants in \((0,1]\), define \[\mathcal Q_C=\{s\in\mathcal R(\Delta):D(s)\geq\kappa_CD(s^C)\},\] \[\mathcal Q_{CE}=\{s\in\mathcal R(\Delta):D(s)\geq\kappa_{CE}\max[D(s^C),D(s^E)]\},\] and \[\mathcal Q_M=\{s\in\mathcal R(\Delta):D(s)\geq\kappa_MD(s^M)\}.\] These are respectively first-order adequate, first/second-order adequate, and approximate-model-minimizing steps. Exact model minimizers form \(\mathcal Q_*=\arg\max_{s\in\mathcal R(\Delta)}D(s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hierarchy compares a trial step with increasingly strong reference reductions. First-order adequacy requires a fraction of Cauchy decrease. First/second-order adequacy additionally requires a fraction of negative-curvature decrease. Approximate model minimization requires a fraction of the globally maximal predicted reduction, while the top class consists of exact model minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The trust region is compact and \(q\) is continuous, so a model minimizer exists.
\(\mathcal Q_{CE}\) is used only when an eigenpoint reference is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four displayed classes define a model-step quality hierarchy from reference decrease to exact model minimization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(D(s^M)\geq D(s^C)\) and, when defined, \(D(s^M)\geq D(s^E)\), exact model minimization dominates both reference baselines.
special_cases_latex: For \(\kappa_M=1\), \(\mathcal Q_M=\mathcal Q_*\).
When the model is convex, the hierarchy reduces to Cauchy adequacy, approximate model minimization, and exact model minimization.
immediate_consequences_latex: A solver can be compared across implementations solely through the achieved value \(D(s)\).
Stronger decrease certificates can support faster local behavior while the Cauchy certificate supplies the standard global baseline.
boundary_notes: Set inclusion between fractional classes depends on the chosen constants; the conceptual ordering does not imply unconditional inclusion for arbitrary fractions.
Residual-based or distance-based subproblem tolerances are not equivalent without additional conditioning assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Enhanced Model Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enhanced step obtains a fixed fraction of the better reduction supplied by the Cauchy and negative-curvature reference steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_C\) be a Cauchy reference step and \(s_{nc}\) a negative-curvature reference step for the same quadratic model \(q\) and radius \(\Delta\). A feasible vector \(s\) is an enhanced model step with constant \(\kappa_E\in(0,1]\) if
\[
q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_E\max\{q(0)-q(s_C),\ q(0)-q(s_{nc})\}.
\]
When no negative-curvature reference is required, take \(s_{nc}=0\). Thus enhancement retains Cauchy decrease while additionally exploiting detectable negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_E\max\{q(0)-q(s_C),q(0)-q(s_{nc})\}\).

notation.meaning: Uniform fraction of the best reference decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Exact Model Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearly exact step realizes a prescribed fraction, close to one, of the globally maximal trust-region model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
q_*:=\min_{\lVert v\rVert\leq\Delta}q(v)
\]
and let \(\theta\in(0,1]\). A feasible vector \(s\) is a \(\theta\)-nearly exact model step if
\[
q(0)-q(s)\geq\theta\bigl(q(0)-q_*\bigr).
\]
The case \(\theta=1\) is an exact global solution of the trust-region subproblem. A sequence is uniformly nearly exact when one constant \(\theta>0\), conventionally chosen close to one, applies at every relevant iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(s)\geq\theta\max_{\lVert v\rVert\leq\Delta}\bigl(q(0)-q(v)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-accuracy approximation to the globally optimal trust-region model step.

notation.meaning: Global minimum model value over the trust region.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Step Quality Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact steps are precisely the one-nearly-exact steps. With matching factors, nearly exact steps are enhanced and enhanced steps satisfy the approximate Cauchy condition; the latter inclusions can be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a quadratic model \(q\) and radius \(\Delta>0\). Let an exact step globally minimize \(q\) over \(\{s:\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta\}\); let a \(\theta\)-nearly exact step attain at least the fraction \(\theta\in(0,1]\) of the globally maximal model reduction; and let a \(\kappa_E\)-enhanced step attain at least the fraction \(\kappa_E\in(0,1]\) of the larger Cauchy and negative-curvature reference reductions. Then
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{exact}}=\mathcal S_{\mathrm{near}}(1),
\qquad
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{near}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathrm{enh}}(\theta)
\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathrm{Cauchy}}(\theta).
\]
The first inclusion holds because the globally maximal reduction is at least either feasible reference reduction; the second holds because the larger reference reduction is at least the Cauchy reference reduction. For \(\theta<1\), a nearly exact step need not be exact, and the latter two inclusions need not be equalities in general.
assumptions_latex: All compared steps use the same quadratic model \(q\) and radius \(\Delta>0\)
The Cauchy and negative-curvature reference steps are feasible

children.title: Model-Agreement Acceptance Calculus
children.top_down_role: Model-to-objective agreement diagnostics and the resulting iteration classifications.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(s_k\) be a feasible trial step for model \(m_k\), with predicted reduction \(P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\), and actual reduction \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic objective evaluations and a strictly model-decreasing trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\rho_k=\frac{A_k}{P_k}=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)}.\] For thresholds \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\), define the acceptance map \[\mathcal A(\rho_k)=\begin{cases}\text{reject},&\rho_k<\eta_1,\\\text{accept},&\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2,\\\text{accept with strong agreement},&\rho_k\geq\eta_2.\end{cases}\] The iterate is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) in either accepted class and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) in the rejected class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The agreement calculus divides actual objective reduction by the reduction predicted by the model. A positive denominator is required. Ratios below the lower threshold cause rejection; ratios between the thresholds cause ordinary acceptance; ratios at or above the upper threshold indicate strong agreement and also cause acceptance. Radius management may use the same classes but is a separate rule.
assumptions_latex: Both objective values in \(A_k\) are evaluated without an explicit error allowance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\) and \(\mathcal A\) define the model-agreement acceptance calculus and its iterate update.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\rho_k=1+[m_k(x_k+s_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/P_k\) whenever \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), so \(\rho_k-1\) is normalized endpoint model error.
special_cases_latex: If \(\rho_k<0\), the objective increased and the trial point is rejected.
If \(\rho_k=1\), actual and predicted reductions coincide exactly.
immediate_consequences_latex: Acceptance with \(\eta_1>0\) implies \(A_k\geq\eta_1P_k>0\).
Strong agreement does not by itself imply that the radius must expand; expansion belongs to the radius policy.
boundary_notes: The ratio is undefined when \(P_k=0\); such a trial step requires a separate convention.
Nonmonotone references and inexact objective evaluations require modified numerators or uncertainty tests.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Adequacy Ratio
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The adequacy ratio divides the actual objective reduction by the model-predicted reduction and diagnoses their agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x\) be the current iterate, and let \(m\) be a local model satisfying \(m(0)=f(x)\). For a trial step \(s\) with positive predicted reduction \(m(0)-m(s)>0\), the model adequacy ratio is
\[
\rho=\frac{f(x)-f(x+s)}{m(0)-m(s)}.
\]
Values near one indicate agreement between actual and predicted reduction; \(\rho<0\) means that the objective increased despite a predicted decrease. The ratio is undefined when the predicted reduction is zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Successful, very successful, and unsuccessful iterations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\rho_k\) be a well-defined actual-to-predicted reduction ratio, and fix \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical two-threshold trust-region classification; the classes govern acceptance and constrain subsequent radius management.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the index sets \[\mathcal S=\{k\geq0:\rho_k\geq\eta_1\},\qquad \mathcal V=\{k\geq0:\rho_k\geq\eta_2\},\qquad \mathcal U=\{k\geq0:\rho_k<\eta_1\}.\] An iteration is successful when \(k\in\mathcal S\), very successful when \(k\in\mathcal V\), and unsuccessful when \(k\in\mathcal U\). Thus \(\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal S\), \(\mathcal U=\mathbb N_0\setminus\mathcal S\), and \[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&k\in\mathcal S,\\x_k,&k\in\mathcal U.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iteration is successful if its agreement ratio reaches the acceptance threshold, very successful if it reaches the higher strong-agreement threshold, and unsuccessful otherwise. Very successful iterations are therefore a subset of successful ones. Successful and very successful iterations accept the trial step; unsuccessful iterations retain the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_k\in\mathbb R\) is defined for each classified iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S\), \(\mathcal V\), and \(\mathcal U\) form the stated trust-region iteration taxonomy.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The disjoint partition is \(\mathcal U\), \(\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal V=\{k:\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2\}\), and \(\mathcal V\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\eta_1=\eta_2\), every successful iteration is very successful; the source permits equality, although implementations commonly use distinct thresholds.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only successful indices can change the accepted iterate.
A radius policy may require nonincrease on \(\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal V\), contraction on \(\mathcal U\), and nondecrease on \(\mathcal V\).
boundary_notes: Some texts add labels such as acceptable or extremely successful; those refinements are outside this three-class taxonomy.
The taxonomy classifies iterations, not the intrinsic accuracy of the model over the entire region.

knowledge_statements.title: Successful Iterations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region iteration is successful when its agreement ratio meets the acceptance threshold, so the trial point is accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an acceptance threshold \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\). At iteration \(k\), suppose the trial step \(s_k\) has positive predicted reduction and adequacy ratio \(\rho_k\). The iteration is successful when
\[
\rho_k\geq\eta_1.
\]
The standard acceptance action is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). The radius \(\Delta_{k+1}\) is then maintained or enlarged according to the algorithm's update rule; success alone does not require enlargement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted trust-region iterations under the standard ratio threshold.

notation.meaning: Model adequacy ratio at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsuccessful Iterations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated ratio convention, an iteration is unsuccessful when agreement falls below the acceptance threshold. Under the additionally stated update rule, the trial point is rejected and the trust-region radius is contracted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an acceptance threshold \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\). At iteration \(k\), suppose the trial step \(s_k\) has positive predicted reduction and model adequacy ratio \(\rho_k\). Under the convention that a trial point is rejected when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), the iteration is unsuccessful precisely when
\[
\rho_k<\eta_1.
\]
If the algorithm additionally uses a contraction factor \(\gamma_{dec}\in(0,1)\) and requires an unsuccessful iteration to choose \(0<\Delta_{k+1}\leq\gamma_{dec}\Delta_k\), then its rejection update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) together with that radius contraction.
assumptions_latex: For the radius-update conclusion, \(0<\gamma_{dec}<1\) and the algorithm prescribes \(0<\Delta_{k+1}\leq\gamma_{dec}\Delta_k\) after rejection
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); under the stated rejection-and-contraction rule, \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(0<\Delta_{k+1}\leq\gamma_{dec}\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected trust-region iterations under a specified ratio-threshold and contraction convention.

notation.meaning: Trust-region contraction factor used by the specified update rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Very Successful Iterations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iteration is very successful when its actual reduction is at least an \(\eta_2\) fraction of the model-predicted reduction; acceptance and possible radius expansion follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be a model of \(f\) at \(x_k\), let \(s_k\) satisfy \(\lVert s_k\rVert\leq \Delta_k\), and suppose the predicted reduction \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\) is positive. Define the agreement ratio by \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/p_k\). Given a threshold \(\eta_2\in(0,1)\), iteration \(k\) is very successful exactly when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\). In the classical update policy, the trial point is accepted and the next radius is permitted to increase, commonly subject to the step being sufficiently close to the trust-region boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite at the evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\), so iteration \(k\) is very successful and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) under the classical acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical trust-region classification using the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.

children.title: Generalized Agreement Variant Family
children.top_down_role: Agreement families adapted to reference histories or imperfect evaluations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(R_k\) be an admissible reference value, let \(\widetilde f_k\) and \(\widetilde f_k^+\) approximate \(f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k+s_k)\), and let \(P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate umbrella definition for nonmonotone reference histories and imperfect deterministic evaluations; exact admissibility and error budgets are variant-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative error bounds \(\epsilon_k,\epsilon_k^+\) satisfying \(|\widetilde f_k-f(x_k)|\leq\epsilon_k\) and \(|\widetilde f_k^+-f(x_k+s_k)|\leq\epsilon_k^+\), define \[\widetilde\rho_k(R_k)=\frac{R_k-\widetilde f_k^+}{P_k}.\] The reference-value agreement family consists of choices \(R_k=\Phi_k(f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_k))\) for a prescribed history functional \(\Phi_k\). A robust acceptance certificate at threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\) is \[R_k-\widetilde f_k^+-(\epsilon_k+\epsilon_k^+)\geq\eta P_k.\] The exact monotone ratio is recovered when \(R_k=f(x_k)\) and both error bounds vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized agreement ratio may compare predicted reduction with reduction from a history-dependent reference value rather than only the current objective. When evaluations are imperfect, acceptance can be certified by subtracting an error allowance from the measured reduction. The ordinary monotone, exact-evaluation ratio is the zero-error current-value member of this family.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation errors satisfy the displayed deterministic bounds.
The history functional \(\Phi_k\) and admissibility conditions on \(R_k\) are fixed by the selected variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed generalized ratio and robust inequality define a candidate family encompassing reference-history and bounded-evaluation-error agreement tests.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The robust test is equivalent to \(\widetilde\rho_k(R_k)\geq\eta+(\epsilon_k+\epsilon_k^+)/P_k\).
special_cases_latex: \(R_k=f(x_k)\), \(\epsilon_k=\epsilon_k^+=0\) gives the classical ratio.
A finite-window nonmonotone candidate may take \(R_k=\max_{k-M_k\leq j\leq k}f(x_j)\), subject to a source-specific rule.
immediate_consequences_latex: The robust certificate implies \(R_k-f(x_k+s_k)\geq\eta P_k\) under the stated error bounds.
boundary_notes: No inspected source locator in the supplied evidence set established this entire umbrella family with these exact hypotheses.
Stochastic confidence bounds, relative-error tests, and probabilistic acceptance require separate definitions.
review_flags: A precise authoritative source is required for the combined reference-history and imperfect-evaluation umbrella definition.
The finite-window special case is retained only as a candidate and must not be promoted without direct evidence.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference-value and evaluation-error agreement family
Nonmonotone Agreement Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonmonotone variant compares the trial objective with a reference no smaller than the current value, allowing controlled objective increases while retaining ratio-based acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\) be a reference value satisfying \(R_k\geq f(x_k)\), for example the maximum of finitely many recent objective values. For a trial step \(s_k\) with positive predicted reduction \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\), define \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}=[R_k-f(x_k+s_k)]/p_k\). A nonmonotone agreement variant accepts the trial point when \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}\geq\eta_1\), where \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\). Consequently, an accepted step may satisfy \(f(x_k+s_k)>f(x_k)\), but it must produce sufficient reduction relative to the chosen reference value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point is accepted when \(R_k-f(x_k+s_k)\geq\eta_1p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-value generalization of the ordinary trust-region agreement ratio.
review_flags: authoritative locator for the selected reference-value formulation is missing
variant family admits multiple reference sequences

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The reference-value ratio is mathematically coherent and fits the nonmonotone-variant container, but no source is supplied for this particular reference condition, denominator, and acceptance rule. Nonmonotone trust-region methods use materially different reference sequences and normalizations, so an authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Agreement Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified error bounds yield a conservative computable test whose satisfaction guarantees that the exact actual-to-predicted reduction ratio meets the acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\) and \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Suppose computed reductions \(\widetilde a_k\) and \(\widetilde p_k\) have certified errors \(|\widetilde a_k-a_k|\leq\varepsilon_k^a\) and \(|\widetilde p_k-p_k|\leq\varepsilon_k^p\), with \(\widetilde p_k-\varepsilon_k^p>0\). For \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\), the conservative inexact agreement condition is \(\widetilde a_k-\varepsilon_k^a\geq\eta_1(\widetilde p_k+\varepsilon_k^p)\). Satisfaction of this computable condition guarantees the exact acceptance inequality \(a_k\geq\eta_1p_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde a_k-\varepsilon_k^a\geq\eta_1(\widetilde p_k+\varepsilon_k^p)\) implies \(a_k/p_k\geq\eta_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust acceptance test when actual or predicted reductions are known only approximately.
review_flags: authoritative locator for this certified-error formulation is missing
inexact trust-region variants use differing error models

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The conservative implication is mathematically valid under the displayed absolute-error bounds and the condition content kind fits the leaf. However, the selected two-sided certified-error model is only one possible inexact agreement regime and has no supporting citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Agreement Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The combined test uses a nonmonotone reference and certified evaluation errors; its conservative inequality guarantees sufficient exact reduction relative to that reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\geq f(x_k)\), define \(a_k^R=R_k-f(x_k+s_k)\), and let \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Suppose computed values satisfy \(|\widetilde a_k^R-a_k^R|\leq\varepsilon_k^a\) and \(|\widetilde p_k-p_k|\leq\varepsilon_k^p\), with \(\widetilde p_k-\varepsilon_k^p>0\). A combined nonmonotone-inexact regime accepts whenever \(\widetilde a_k^R-\varepsilon_k^a\geq\eta_1(\widetilde p_k+\varepsilon_k^p)\), where \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\). This condition guarantees \(a_k^R\geq\eta_1p_k\), while monotonic decrease from \(f(x_k)\) need not occur.
assumptions_latex: The computed reductions obey the displayed certified error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable conservative test implies \([R_k-f(x_k+s_k)]/p_k\geq\eta_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative agreement test combining nonmonotone references and inexact reduction evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An acceptance-radius control policy is the pair \((A,U)\) with \[A(\rho,s)=\begin{cases}s,&\rho\geq\eta_1,\\0,&\rho<\eta_1,\end{cases}\] and \[U(\Delta,\rho)=\begin{cases}[\Delta,\infty),&\rho\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta,\Delta],&\eta_1\leq\rho<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta,\gamma_2\Delta],&\rho<\eta_1.\end{cases}\] The controlled recurrence is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+A(\rho_k,s_k)\) and \(\Delta_{k+1}\in U(\Delta_k,\rho_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy maps a ratio and trial step to either the step or zero, and maps the current radius and ratio to an admissible interval for the next radius. Strong agreement permits a nondecreasing radius, ordinary acceptance permits retention or limited contraction, and rejection forces contraction by bounded factors.
assumptions_latex: The trial step has a well-defined agreement ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A,U)\) and the two recurrences define the acceptance-radius control policy.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The policy may be expressed as a state transition on \((x_k,\Delta_k)\) driven by \((s_k,\rho_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing a single point from each interval gives a deterministic radius-update rule.
Adding \(\Delta_{k+1}\leq\Delta_{\max}\) yields a globally capped policy.
immediate_consequences_latex: An unsuccessful iteration satisfies \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(\Delta_{k+1}<\Delta_k\).
A very successful iteration never forces contraction under this policy.
boundary_notes: The source's upper interval is unbounded; implementations commonly add a maximum radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Based Radius Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The radius contracts below the lower ratio threshold, expands up to its cap for very good boundary-active steps, and is retained otherwise; the lower threshold also determines trial-point acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose thresholds \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), factors \(0<\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}<1<\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}\), and a maximum radius \(\Delta_{\max}>0\). Given \(\Delta_k\), an agreement ratio \(\rho_k\), and a trial step \(s_k\), set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\Delta_k\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}\}\) if \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\) and the trial step is boundary-active; and set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\Delta_k\) otherwise. Accept the trial point exactly when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); otherwise retain \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces \(0<\Delta_{k+1}\leq\Delta_{\max}\), with contraction for poor agreement, capped expansion for very good boundary-active steps, and retention in all remaining cases.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical three-way contraction, retention, and expansion rule.
review_flags: specific numerical thresholds and factors are implementation parameters

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Delta_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\gamma_c\Delta_k,&\rho_k<\eta_c,\\\Delta_k,&\eta_c\leq\rho_k\leq\eta_e\text{ or }\|s_k\|_2<\Delta_k,\\\min\{\gamma_e\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}\},&\rho_k>\eta_e\text{ and }\|s_k\|_2=\Delta_k,\end{cases}\] where \(0<\gamma_c<1<\gamma_e\) and \(0<\eta_c<\eta_e<1\). The Nocedal-Wright canonical instance is \((\gamma_c,\gamma_e,\eta_c,\eta_e)=(1/4,2,1/4,3/4)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold-based update contracts the radius after poor agreement, retains it after intermediate agreement, and expands it after strong agreement only when the step is boundary-limited. Expansion is capped by a maximum radius. The canonical numerical factors are one-quarter for contraction and two for expansion, with ratio thresholds one-quarter and three-quarters.

special_cases_latex: With \(\gamma_c=1/4\), \(\gamma_e=2\), \(\eta_c=1/4\), and \(\eta_e=3/4\), the recurrence is Algorithm 4.1's radius rule.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the trial step lies strictly inside the region, the radius is not expanded.
The cap preserves \(\Delta_{k+1}\leq\Delta_{\max}\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Delta>0\), let \(\rho\) be an agreement ratio, and fix \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\) and \(0<\gamma_1\leq\gamma_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: BTR-style graded control using ranges of admissible updates rather than one fixed multiplier per class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graded radius-update family is the set-valued map \[\mathcal U(\Delta,\rho)=\begin{cases}[\Delta,\infty),&\rho\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta,\Delta],&\eta_1\leq\rho<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta,\gamma_2\Delta],&\rho<\eta_1.\end{cases}\] A radius sequence belongs to this family if \(\Delta_{k+1}\in\mathcal U(\Delta_k,\rho_k)\) for every \(k\). With a cap \(\Delta_{\max}\), replace each interval by its intersection with \((0,\Delta_{\max}]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graded update does not prescribe one contraction or expansion factor. It permits a range of next radii based on the quality class: nondecrease after strong agreement, limited contraction or retention after ordinary acceptance, and mandatory bounded contraction after rejection. Any selection from the corresponding interval is a member of the family.
assumptions_latex: When a finite cap is imposed, the selected interval must remain nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U\) defines the graded radius-update family and \(\Delta_{k+1}\in\mathcal U(\Delta_k,\rho_k)\) defines its admissible sequences.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For unsuccessful iterations, the multiplier \(\Delta_{k+1}/\Delta_k\) belongs to \([\gamma_1,\gamma_2]\); for ordinary successful iterations it belongs to \([\gamma_2,1]\); for very successful iterations it belongs to \([1,\infty)\).
special_cases_latex: Selecting interval endpoints yields discrete update variants.
Choosing \(\gamma_1=\gamma_2\) forces a single contraction multiplier after rejection.
immediate_consequences_latex: Rejection gives \(\Delta_{k+1}<\Delta_k\).
Strong agreement gives \(\Delta_{k+1}\geq\Delta_k\) before application of any external cap.
boundary_notes: The cited family does not require a boundary-active step before allowing radius increase.
Additional lower and upper safeguards can narrow the admissible intervals.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolated Radius Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Piecewise-affine interpolation maps agreement ratios to radius multipliers, after which multiplier and absolute-radius safeguards are applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose knots \(-\infty<r_0<r_1<\cdots<r_q<\infty\) and positive multipliers \(g_0,\ldots,g_q\). Let \(g:\mathbb{R}\to(0,\infty)\) be piecewise affine with \(g(r_i)=g_i\), constant outside \([r_0,r_q]\), and clipped to \([\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\), where \(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq1\leq\gamma_{\max}\). Given the agreement statistic \(\rho_k\), update \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\Delta_{\max},\max\{\Delta_{\min},g(\rho_k)\Delta_k\}\}\). Thus neighboring target multipliers are interpolated continuously while explicit radius and multiplier safeguards are enforced.
assumptions_latex: The knot sequence is strictly increasing and all target multipliers are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{k+1}\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\) and \(g(\rho_k)\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Radius Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous safeguarded function converts agreement into contraction, retention, or expansion multipliers and then clips the resulting radius to fixed bounds.

Given agreement statistic \(\rho_k\), set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\Delta_{\max},\max\{\Delta_{\min},g(\rho_k)\Delta_k\}\}\). The update varies continuously with \(\rho_k\) except where the absolute radius bounds become active.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is continuous and takes values in \([\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\).
The stated contraction, retention, and expansion sign conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The radius update is safeguarded and is continuous in \(\rho_k\) wherever neither absolute bound is active.

knowledge_statements.title: Graded-Update Safeguards
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graded policy is safeguarded by bounded multipliers and clipping to positive finite radius limits, preventing unbounded one-step changes or radius collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a graded radius policy propose \(\widehat\Delta_{k+1}=g(\rho_k)\Delta_k\). It is safeguarded when constants \(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq1\leq\gamma_{\max}<\infty\) and \(0<\Delta_{\min}<\Delta_{\max}<\infty\) are fixed, \(g(r)\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\) for every admissible agreement value \(r\), and the implemented update is \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\Delta_{\max},\max\{\Delta_{\min},\widehat\Delta_{k+1}\}\}\). These conditions prevent a single update from changing the radius by an unbounded factor and keep every implemented radius positive and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{k+1}\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\) and the unclipped multiplier is uniformly bounded.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\widehat\Delta>0\), \(0<\Delta_0\leq\widehat\Delta\), and suppose an unsafeguarded radius proposal is \(\widetilde\Delta_{k+1}>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional radius management with positivity, a global upper cap, and a boundary-activity condition for expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A radius safeguard system consists of \[0<\Delta_k\leq\widehat\Delta,\qquad \Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\widehat\Delta,\widetilde\Delta_{k+1}\},\] together with the expansion gate \[\Delta_{k+1}>\Delta_k\ \Longrightarrow\ \rho_k>\eta_e\ \text{ and }\ \|s_k\|_k=\Delta_k.\] For a contraction proposal \(\widetilde\Delta_{k+1}=\gamma_k\Delta_k\), require \(0<\underline\gamma\leq\gamma_k\leq\overline\gamma<1\). These conditions preserve a positive finite scale, prevent unbounded expansion, and allow expansion only when the current region constrained a strongly agreeing step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded radius remains positive and no larger than a prescribed maximum. Contraction factors are bounded away from zero and one, so one update neither annihilates the radius nor fails to contract. Expansion is gated by both strong model agreement and an active trust-region boundary, because an interior step does not show that a larger region would have permitted more progress.
assumptions_latex: The boundary condition uses the norm defining the current trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cap, contraction-factor bounds, and expansion gate define the radius safeguard system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The cap is the projection \(\Delta_{k+1}=\Pi_{(0,\widehat\Delta]}(\widetilde\Delta_{k+1})\) for positive proposals, with the upper endpoint included.
special_cases_latex: Algorithm 4.1 uses \(\gamma_k=1/4\), expansion proposal \(2\Delta_k\), and cap \(\widehat\Delta\).
immediate_consequences_latex: By induction, \(0<\Delta_k\leq\widehat\Delta\) for every finite \(k\).
No interior trial step triggers expansion.
boundary_notes: A strictly positive numerical floor is an implementation safeguard but changes asymptotic behavior and is not imposed here.
Approximate boundary tests should use a stated tolerance in finite precision.

If a characteristic problem scale \(d_0>0\) is available, a scale-aware initialization may use \(\Delta_0=\min\{\Delta_{\max},\max\{\Delta_{\min},\tau d_0\}\}\) for a prescribed dimensionless \(\tau>0\). knowledge_statements.title: Radius Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping every proposed radius to fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds preserves the radius invariant, although theoretical analyses often omit a positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose constants \(0<\Delta_{\min}<\Delta_{\max}<\infty\). A radius sequence is bounded by the safeguard system when \(\Delta_k\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\) for every implemented iteration \(k\). For any proposed radius \(\widehat\Delta_{k+1}>0\), the projection update \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\Delta_{\max},\max\{\Delta_{\min},\widehat\Delta_{k+1}\}\}\) preserves this invariant. The upper bound limits excessively large local models, while the optional positive lower implementation bound prevents numerical underflow; convergence analyses may instead permit radii to approach zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{k+1}\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant lower and upper safeguards for implemented trust-region radii.

knowledge_statements.title: Radius Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invalid radius proposal is discarded, replaced by a contracted safeguarded radius, and followed by recomputation of the trial step before acceptance is considered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\Delta_{\min}<\Delta_{\max}<\infty\), a recovery factor \(\gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}\in(0,1)\), and a valid previous radius \(\Delta_k\). If a proposed \(\widehat\Delta_{k+1}\) is finite and positive, use its projection onto \([\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\). Otherwise reject the invalid proposal and set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\max\{\Delta_{\min},\gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}\Delta_k\}\). Recompute the trial step within the recovered trust region before evaluating acceptance. This recovery rule restores a finite admissible radius without accepting a step generated under an invalid radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery yields \(\Delta_{k+1}\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\) and requires a new trial step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded restoration after an invalid, nonfinite, or numerically unusable radius proposal.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric geometry of a trust region
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(\|\cdot\|_k\) be a norm, possibly varying with \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional restricted-step geometry, including Euclidean, polyhedral, and ellipsoidal trust regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trust-region metric geometry at iteration \(k\) is the norm ball \[\mathcal B_k=\{x_k+s:\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}.\] If \(S_k\) is nonsingular and \(\|s\|_k=\|S_k^{-1}s\|_2\), then \[\mathcal B_k=x_k+\{s:s^TS_k^{-T}S_k^{-1}s\leq\Delta_k^2\}=x_k+S_k\{w:\|w\|_2\leq\Delta_k\}.\] Thus a Euclidean ball in scaled coordinates \(w=S_k^{-1}s\) is an ellipsoid in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region geometry is the ball of the chosen step norm centered at the current iterate. A nonsingular change of variables converts a Euclidean ball in scaled coordinates into an ellipsoid in the original coordinates, with metric matrix given by the inverse-transpose times the inverse of the scaling matrix. The norm therefore determines which directions count as long or short.
assumptions_latex: For the ellipsoidal representation, \(S_k\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_k\) and its scaled-coordinate representation define the trust-region metric geometry.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(M_k=S_k^{-T}S_k^{-1}\succ0\), the ellipsoidal norm is \(\|s\|_{M_k}=\sqrt{s^TM_ks}\).
special_cases_latex: \(S_k=I\) gives the Euclidean ball.
The \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_\infty\) norms give cross-polytope and box geometries rather than ellipsoids.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing the norm can change the Cauchy point, eigenpoint, and model minimizer even when the model and radius are fixed.
Variable rescaling and ellipsoidal trust-region geometry are mathematically equivalent.
boundary_notes: A positive-semidefinite singular metric defines a seminorm and an unbounded cylinder, not a norm-bounded trust region.
Metric choice alone does not guarantee model fidelity in the resulting region.

notation.meaning: Nonsingular scaling map from scaled to original steps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed and iteration-dependent trust-region scaling regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, let \(s=S_kw\), and let \(m_k(x_k+s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear variable scalings for quadratic trust-region models; both preselected and iteration-dependent regimes are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scaling regime is a sequence \(\{S_k\}\) defining \[\|s\|_k=\|S_k^{-1}s\|_2,\qquad \|S_k^{-1}s\|_2\leq\Delta_k.\] In scaled coordinates, \[g_k^{(s)}=S_k^Tg_k,\qquad H_k^{(s)}=S_k^TH_kS_k,\] and \[m_k(x_k+S_kw)=f(x_k)+(g_k^{(s)})^Tw+\tfrac12w^TH_k^{(s)}w.\] The regime is fixed when \(S_k=S\) for all \(k\), diagonal when every \(S_k\) is diagonal, and adaptive when \(S_k\) depends on the current iterate, model, or preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaling regime is a fixed or varying sequence of nonsingular coordinate transformations. It defines the trust-region norm through the inverse scaling. Gradients transform by the transpose scaling and model Hessians by congruence. A fixed scaling uses one transformation throughout; a diagonal scaling changes variable units independently; an adaptive scaling may follow current curvature or preconditioning information.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic model uses a symmetric \(H_k\).
The same \(S_k\) is used consistently in the coordinate transformation, model, and trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed norm and transformed model quantities define the family of fixed, diagonal, and adaptive scaling regimes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The original-variable constraint is \(s^TS_k^{-T}S_k^{-1}s\leq\Delta_k^2\).
special_cases_latex: \(S_k=I\) is the unscaled regime.
A constant diagonal \(S\) represents preselected typical variable sizes.
A preconditioner-derived \(S_k\) gives an iteration-dependent regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: Model values are invariant under the consistent substitution \(s=S_kw\).
Scaling changes the feasible geometry without changing the represented original-space quadratic.
boundary_notes: Singular scalings are excluded.
Unboundedly ill-conditioned scaling sequences may destroy uniform metric equivalence even though each individual \(S_k\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Gradient and Hessian representation in scaled coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Scaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed scaling uses one nonsingular matrix at every iteration, producing ellipsoidal trust regions whose size changes with the radius but whose metric geometry remains constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and fixed for all iterations. The fixed-scaled trust region at iteration \(k\) is \(\mathcal{T}_k=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lVert Ds\rVert_2\leq\Delta_k\}\). Equivalently, with \(M=D^{\mathsf T}D\succ0\), it is the ellipsoid \(\mathcal{T}_k=\{s:s^{\mathsf T}Ms\leq\Delta_k^2\}\). Because \(D\) is independent of \(k\), only the scalar radius changes the region between iterations; the metric orientation and relative axis lengths remain fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and independent of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Ds\rVert_2\leq\Delta_k\) is equivalent to \(s^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}Ds\leq\Delta_k^2\), with a fixed positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region geometry induced by one iteration-independent positive-definite scaling matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimizes the linear model over the current diagonally scaled trust region and then minimizes the quadratic model along the resulting feasible ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), first choose
\[
p_k^{\mathrm s}\in\arg\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\{f_k+g_k^Tp:\|Dp\|\leq\Delta_k\}.

Next choose
\[
\tau_k\in\arg\min_{\tau>0}\{m_k(\tau p_k^{\mathrm s}):\|\tau Dp_k^{\mathrm s}\|\leq\Delta_k\},
\]
and set \(p_k^{\mathrm c}=\tau_kp_k^{\mathrm s}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Scaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive scaling chooses the trust-region metric from current iteration information while imposing iteration-independent lower and upper spectral bounds that prevent the metric from degenerating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(D_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be a symmetric positive-definite scaling matrix chosen using information available at iteration \(k\). An adaptively scaled trust region is \[\mathcal T_k=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|D_ks\|_2\leq\Delta_k\}.\] To prevent degeneration of the changing geometry, require constants \(0<d_-\leq d_+<\infty\), independent of \(k\), such that \[d_-I\preceq D_k\preceq d_+I\qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.\] The rule producing \(D_{k+1}\) may use current derivative or curvature information, but it must preserve these uniform bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
The scaling rule preserves \(d_-I\preceq D_k\preceq d_+I\) for fixed constants \(0<d_-\leq d_+<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regions \(\mathcal T_k=\{s:\|D_ks\|_2\leq\Delta_k\}\) use an adaptive metric that remains uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent metric scaling for smooth trust-region models.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Transition Safeguards
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded transition bounds the change between consecutive scaled norms by fixed factors, preventing a single metric update from abruptly collapsing or enlarging the measured size of a step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k,D_{k+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive-definite scaling matrices. A safeguarded scaling transition satisfies fixed constants \(0<\sigma_-\leq1\leq\sigma_+<\infty\) such that, for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\sigma_-\|D_ks\|_2\leq\|D_{k+1}s\|_2\leq\sigma_+\|D_ks\|_2.\] Equivalently, \[\sigma_-^2D_k^2\preceq D_{k+1}^2\preceq\sigma_+^2D_k^2.\] Thus one transition cannot make the measured norm of any step arbitrarily smaller or larger relative to the preceding metric.
assumptions_latex: The constants \(\sigma_-\) and \(\sigma_+\) are positive and independent of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_-\|D_ks\|_2\leq\|D_{k+1}s\|_2\leq\sigma_+\|D_ks\|_2\) for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform safeguards for transitions between consecutive trust-region metrics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform equivalence class of changing trust-region metrics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{\|\cdot\|_k\}_{k\geq0}\) be norms on \(\mathbb R^n\). For ellipsoidal metrics, write \(\|x\|_k=\|S_k^{-1}x\|_2\) with nonsingular \(S_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional changing metrics used in convergence analysis; equivalence constants must be uniform over iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \(\{\|\cdot\|_k\}\) belongs to a uniformly Euclidean-equivalent changing-metric class if there exists \(\kappa_{une}\geq1\), independent of \(k\), such that \[\frac1{\kappa_{une}}\|x\|_k\leq\|x\|_2\leq\kappa_{une}\|x\|_k\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n\text{ and }k\geq0.\] For \(\|x\|_k=\|S_k^{-1}x\|_2\), a sufficient class condition is \[\frac1{\kappa_{scb}}\leq\sigma_{\min}(S_k)\leq\sigma_{\max}(S_k)\leq\kappa_{scb}\qquad\text{for every }k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing trust-region norms are uniformly equivalent when one iteration-independent constant compares every one of them with the Euclidean norm in both directions. For ellipsoidal norms generated by scaling matrices, uniform lower and upper singular-value bounds are sufficient. This prevents trust regions from flattening without bound in one direction or expanding without bound in another as iterations proceed.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\|\cdot\|_k\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The constants \(\kappa_{une}\) and \(\kappa_{scb}\), when used, do not depend on \(k\).
Every ellipsoidal scaling matrix \(S_k\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed two-sided norm comparison defines the changing-metric equivalence class, and the singular-value bounds give a sufficient membership condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exist constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) independent of \(k\) such that \(c\|x\|_2\leq\|x\|_k\leq C\|x\|_2\) for all \(x,k\).
For metric matrices \(M_k=S_k^{-T}S_k^{-1}\), uniform equivalence is equivalent to uniform positive lower and finite upper spectral bounds on \(M_k\).
special_cases_latex: Any fixed norm sequence \(\|\cdot\|_k\equiv\|\cdot\|_*\) is uniformly equivalent in finite dimension.
Uniformly bounded diagonal scalings with diagonal entries bounded away from zero satisfy the condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: Trust regions cannot asymptotically collapse or become unbounded in a direction relative to their stated radii.
Euclidean step lengths and metric step lengths control each other uniformly over all iterations.
boundary_notes: Individual norm equivalence at each iteration is insufficient if its constants diverge with \(k\).
The condition is sufficient for the cited convergence framework but may be relaxable along only the generated gradient, step, and negative-curvature directions.
