knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Equivalent Norms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A changing family of norms is uniformly equivalent to a reference norm when common positive comparison constants work for every vector and every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a fixed norm on \(X\), and let \(\{\|\cdot\|_k\}_{k\geq0}\) be norms on \(X\). The family is uniformly equivalent to \(\|\cdot\|\) if there exist constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\), independent of \(k\), such that \[c\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq C\|s\|\qquad\text{for every }s\in X\text{ and }k\geq0.\] Consequently, the balls satisfy \(\{s:\|s\|\leq r/C\}\subseteq\{s:\|s\|_k\leq r\}\subseteq\{s:\|s\|\leq r/c\}\) for every \(r>0\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq C\|s\|\) uniformly in \(s\) and \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform equivalence of an iteration-indexed norm family to a reference norm.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Vector and Matrix Norms p. 20

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Equivalent Norms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each changing norm is equivalent to the reference norm separately, but its comparison constants may deteriorate without any iteration-independent bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with reference norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and let \(\|\cdot\|_k\) be a norm for every \(k\geq0\). The family is weakly equivalent to the reference norm if, for each \(k\), there exist numbers \(0<c_k\leq C_k<\infty\) satisfying \[c_k\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq C_k\|s\|\qquad\text{for every }s\in X,\] without requiring \(\inf_k c_k>0\) or \(\sup_k C_k<\infty\). Hence each individual metric has the same topology as the reference metric, although the comparison may degenerate along the iteration sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_k\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq C_k\|s\|\) for each fixed \(k\), with no uniform bound required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise, but not necessarily uniform, equivalence of changing norms.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: In finite dimensions, the displayed comparison holds separately for every norm automatically. The label “weakly equivalent norms” is not sufficiently standard to infer that this nonuniform notion is the intended definition, and the cited general norms section has not been shown to use or support this terminology.

knowledge_statements.title: Changing-Metric Consequences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform norm equivalence transfers vanishing-step statements and traps every changing-metric trust region between fixed multiples of reference-norm balls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\{\|\cdot\|_k\}\) is uniformly equivalent to a reference norm \(\|\cdot\|\), with \(c\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq C\|s\|\). For every sequence \(s_k\in X\), \[\|s_k\|_k\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\|s_k\|\to0.\] Moreover, if \(\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\), then \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k/c\); conversely, \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k/C\) implies \(\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\). Therefore shrinking trust-region radii force shrinking steps in the reference geometry, and metric trust-region balls admit uniform inner and outer reference-norm bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(c\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq C\|s\|\) for all \(s\in X\) and \(k\), with \(0<c\leq C<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s_k\|_k\to0\iff\|s_k\|\to0\), with the stated uniform ball inclusions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of step-size and convergence statements under uniform metric equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Geometry-Reflecting Trust Regions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem-geometry-reflecting trust region is a scaled unit ball of a norm chosen to represent weighted, block, or polyhedral structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(P_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact, convex, centrally symmetric, and contain \(0\) in its interior. Its Minkowski functional \(\gamma_{P_k}:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)\), defined by \[\gamma_{P_k}(s)=\inf\{t>0:s\in tP_k\},\] is a norm, and the corresponding trust region satisfies \[\mathcal T_k=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\gamma_{P_k}(s)\leq\Delta_k\}=\Delta_kP_k.\] Examples include \(\gamma_{P_k}(s)=\|D_ks\|_1\) for an invertible \(D_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\); \(\gamma_{P_k}(s)=\max_{1\leq j\leq q}\|D_{k,j}s_j\|_{p_j}\) for a fixed block decomposition \(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_q)\), exponents \(1\leq p_j\leq\infty\), and injective block maps \(D_{k,j}\); and \(\gamma_{P_k}(s)=\|A_ks\|_\infty\) for a matrix \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\) with trivial nullspace.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact, convex, centrally symmetric, and contains \(0\) in its interior.
Every linear map used in a displayed norm representation is injective on its stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_k=\{s:\gamma_{P_k}(s)\leq\Delta_k\}=\Delta_kP_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust regions induced by norms whose unit balls reflect weighted, block, or polyhedral problem structure.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) is the current iterate, \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) is a trial step, \(\Delta_k>0\), and \(D_k\) is a nonsingular scaling matrix chosen from problem structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic trust regions defined by scaled polyhedral norms; more general gauges require separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A problem-geometry-reflecting trust region is a set \[\mathcal T_k(\Delta_k)=\{p\in\mathbb R^n:\|D_kp\|_{\mathsf s}\leq\Delta_k\},\qquad \mathsf s\in\{1,\infty\},\] where the scaling \(D_k\) and norm are selected to represent known anisotropy, block scaling, or coordinatewise step restrictions. Its unit set is centrally symmetric, convex, closed, bounded, and contains the origin in its interior. Equivalently, it is the inverse image under \(D_k\) of a scaled cross-polytope when \(\mathsf s=1\), or a scaled box when \(\mathsf s=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem-geometry-reflecting trust region consists of all steps \(p\) whose scaled \(\ell_1\) or \(\ell_\infty\) norm is at most \(\Delta_k\). The nonsingular scaling \(D_k\) encodes known coordinate or block anisotropy. Thus the region is a cross-polytope or box in scaled coordinates and is a closed, bounded, centrally symmetric convex neighborhood of zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_k(\Delta_k)=\{p:\|D_kp\|_{\mathsf s}\leq\Delta_k\}\) is the structure-sensitive trust region used to restrict the local-model step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(z=D_kp\), \(\mathcal T_k(\Delta_k)=D_k^{-1}\{z:\|z\|_{\mathsf s}\leq\Delta_k\}\).
For \(\mathsf s=\infty\), membership is equivalent to \(|(D_kp)_i|\leq\Delta_k\) for every \(i\).
special_cases_latex: \(D_k=I\) gives the ordinary \(\ell_1\) or \(\ell_\infty\) trust region.
Diagonal \(D_k\) gives coordinate-scaled absolute-value bounds.
immediate_consequences_latex: The region is compact, so every continuous local model attains a minimum on it.
Nonsingular scaling makes its induced norm equivalent to the Euclidean norm in finite dimensions.
boundary_notes: This definition does not cover asymmetric regions or unbounded gauges.
Uniform conditioning of a changing scaling sequence is an additional convergence assumption, not part of the set definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an ellipsoidal trust region for a quadratic local model and records the source's sufficient boundedness condition for iteration-dependent diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), with \(\|\cdot\|\) the Euclidean norm. A positive diagonal matrix \(D_k=\operatorname{diag}(d_{k,1},\ldots,d_{k,n})\) defines the scaled trust-region subproblem
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}m_k(p)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \|D_kp\|\leq\Delta_k.
\]
Large \(d_{k,i}\) shorten the ellipsoid in sensitive coordinate directions, whereas smaller entries permit longer steps in less-sensitive directions. The scaling may vary with \(k\); the source states that most of the chapter's trust-region theory continues to apply, with minor modifications, provided
\[
0<d_{\mathrm{lo}}\leq d_{k,i}\leq d_{\mathrm{hi}}<\infty\qquad\forall k,i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal scaling changes a Euclidean trust region into an ellipsoid. Larger diagonal entries restrict movement in sensitive coordinates. If the scaling changes between iterations, the source qualifies its theoretical transfer by requiring all diagonal entries to remain uniformly bounded above and away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the stated variable-scaling transfer: }0<d_{\mathrm{lo}}\leq d_{k,i}\leq d_{\mathrm{hi}}<\infty\quad\forall k,i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T_k=\{p:\|D_kp\|_2\leq\Delta_k\};\quad \text{under uniform positive bounds on }D_k,\text{ most of the referenced trust-region theory applies with minor modifications.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Form and Spherical Rescaling of the Diagonal-Metric Cauchy Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the scaled linear-model solution and feasible ray length, then records the equivalent spherical trust-region model under a diagonal change of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(g_k\neq0\), \(D\succ0\) is diagonal, \(\Delta_k>0\), and \(\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_2\). Then
\[
p_k^{\mathrm s}=-\frac{\Delta_k}{\|D^{-1}g_k\|_2}D^{-2}g_k,
\]
and
\[
\tau_k=\begin{cases}
1,&g_k^TD^{-2}B_kD^{-2}g_k\leq0,\\[2mm]
\min\!\left\{\dfrac{\|D^{-1}g_k\|_2^3}{\Delta_k g_k^TD^{-2}B_kD^{-2}g_k},1\right\},&g_k^TD^{-2}B_kD^{-2}g_k>0.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus \(p_k^{\mathrm c}=\tau_kp_k^{\mathrm s}\). With \(\widetilde p=Dp\), the scaled subproblem is equivalently
\[
\min_{\|\widetilde p\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\left[f_k+(D^{-1}g_k)^T\widetilde p+\tfrac12\widetilde p^T(D^{-1}B_kD^{-1})\widetilde p\right].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero gradient and a positive diagonal metric, the scaled linear-model solution and its optimal feasible quadratic-model ray length have explicit formulas. The substitution p-tilde = Dp converts the ellipsoidal subproblem into a Euclidean-ball trust-region subproblem with transformed gradient D inverse g and transformed Hessian D inverse B D inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k^{\mathrm c}=\tau_kp_k^{\mathrm s}\text{ with the displayed closed forms, and }\widetilde p=Dp\text{ yields }\widetilde g_k=D^{-1}g_k,\quad\widetilde B_k=D^{-1}B_kD^{-1},\quad\|\widetilde p\|_2\leq\Delta_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Non-Euclidean Trust Regions and the Infinity-Norm Box Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records common non-Euclidean trust-region geometries and the box form induced by the infinity norm in a bound-constrained quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Trust regions may be defined by \(\|p\|_1\leq\Delta_k\), \(\|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta_k\), or, for positive diagonal \(D\), by \(\|Dp\|_1\leq\Delta_k\) or \(\|Dp\|_\infty\leq\Delta_k\). For a feasible iterate \(x_k\geq0\), the infinity-norm bound-constrained subproblem
\[
\min_p m_k(p)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_k+p\geq0,\quad \|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta_k
\]
has the equivalent box constraints
\[
x_k+p\geq0,\qquad -\Delta_ke\leq p\leq\Delta_ke.
\]
Hence it is a bound-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust regions can use the 1-norm or infinity norm, with or without positive diagonal scaling. For a nonnegativity-constrained problem, an infinity-norm trust region combines with feasibility to give coordinatewise lower and upper bounds, making the model subproblem a bound-constrained quadratic program.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ is positive diagonal when a scaled norm is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{p:x_k+p\geq0,\ \|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta_k\}=\{p:x_k+p\geq0,\ -\Delta_ke\leq p\leq\Delta_ke\},\quad\text{so the model subproblem is a bound-constrained QP.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First- and second-order trust-region fidelity hierarchy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(x\in S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\), and \(B(x;\Delta)=\{y:\|y-x\|_2\leq\Delta\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth finite-dimensional models, organized into the fully linear and fully quadratic accuracy levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The trust-region model fidelity hierarchy consists of two nested accuracy specifications. A \(C^1\) model is first-order faithful on \(B(x;\Delta)\) when constants independent of \(x\) and \(\Delta\) satisfy \[|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^2,\qquad \|
abla f(y)-
abla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta.\] A \(C^2\) model is second-order faithful when \[|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^3,\quad \|
abla f(y)-
abla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta^2,\quad \|
abla^2f(y)-
abla^2m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eh}\Delta\] for every \(y\in B(x;\Delta)\). A model class occupies a level when an appropriate model exists uniformly for every admissible center and radius and can be certified or produced by a uniformly finite model-improvement procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fidelity hierarchy has a first-order level, with function and gradient errors of orders \(\Delta^2\) and \(\Delta\), and a second-order level, with function, gradient, and Hessian errors of orders \(\Delta^3\), \(\Delta^2\), and \(\Delta\). The constants are uniform over admissible centers and radii, and the model class must admit a uniformly finite certification or improvement procedure.
assumptions_latex: For the first-order level, \(f\in C^1\) and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz on a neighborhood of the relevant balls.
For the second-order level, \(f\in C^2\) and \(\nabla^2 f\) is Lipschitz on that neighborhood.
The constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},\kappa_{eh}>0\) do not depend on \(x\), \(\Delta\), or \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed scale-dependent inequalities define the fully linear and fully quadratic levels of the model-fidelity hierarchy.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The order-two level strengthens the order-one level by controlling one additional derivative and improving the powers of \(\Delta\) in the lower-order errors.
special_cases_latex: Exact first- or second-order Taylor models satisfy the corresponding local orders under Lipschitz derivative assumptions.
Well-poised polynomial interpolation and regression models can furnish these fidelity classes.
immediate_consequences_latex: Shrinking \(\Delta\) forces the model derivatives to approach the corresponding objective derivatives at the stated rates.
boundary_notes: Membership of a model class does not imply that every member is accurate at every center and radius.
Stochastic or probabilistic fidelity is outside this deterministic hierarchy.

notation.meaning: Uniform function, gradient, and Hessian error constants.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), current point \(x_k\), step \(p\in\mathbb R^n\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), vector \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and symmetric \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth optimization with a quadratic model expressed in step coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local quadratic model of \(f\) at \(x_k\) is the map \[m_k(p)=c_k+g_k^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp,\qquad \|p\|\leq\Delta_k,\] where \(c_k\) approximates \(f(x_k)\), \(g_k\) approximates \(
abla f(x_k)\), and the symmetric matrix \(B_k\) represents exact or approximate curvature. The model is interpolatory at the center when \(c_k=f(x_k)\), first-order consistent when additionally \(g_k=
abla f(x_k)\), and a second-order Taylor model when also \(B_k=
abla^2f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local trust-region representation is a quadratic function of the step \(p\), consisting of a constant, a linear term \(g_k^Tp\), and a symmetric curvature term \(p^TB_kp/2\), used only for steps inside the radius \(\Delta_k\). Center interpolation, first-order consistency, and exact second-order Taylor representation are obtained by successively matching the objective value, gradient, and Hessian at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(p)=c_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) is the canonical local quadratic representation used by a trust-region method.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(y=x_k+p\) gives \(\widehat m_k(y)=c_k+g_k^T(y-x_k)+\tfrac12(y-x_k)^TB_k(y-x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: \(B_k=0\) gives a linear model.
\(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) and \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) give the second-order Taylor model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The model gradient and Hessian in step coordinates are \(\nabla m_k(p)=g_k+B_kp\) and \(\nabla^2m_k(p)=B_k\).
boundary_notes: The definition itself imposes no accuracy rate on approximate coefficients.
Nonsmooth composite models need not have this quadratic form.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at \(x_k\), and twice differentiable there for the second-order level.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact differential models and quadratic models with approximate curvature in finite-dimensional smooth optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The smooth local-model hierarchy at \(x_k\) comprises \[m_k^{(0)}(p)=f(x_k),\qquad m_k^{(1)}(p)=f(x_k)+
abla f(x_k)^Tp,\] and, when second derivatives or a curvature approximation are available, \[m_k^{(2)}(p;B_k)=f(x_k)+
abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp,\qquad B_k=B_k^T.\] The exact second-order member has \(B_k=
abla^2f(x_k)\); otherwise it is an approximate-curvature quadratic member. The index records the highest differential order represented, not a convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hierarchy begins with the constant objective value, adds the exact gradient to obtain a first-order affine model, and then adds a symmetric quadratic curvature term. Using the exact Hessian yields the second-order Taylor member; using another symmetric matrix yields an approximate-curvature member. The level describes represented differential information rather than algorithmic convergence.
assumptions_latex: For the exact second-order member, \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed constant, affine, and quadratic models form the smooth local-model hierarchy by increasing represented differential order.
special_cases_latex: \(B_k=0\) collapses the quadratic member to the first-order member.
\(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) gives the second-order Taylor polynomial.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every higher displayed level preserves the center value and gradient of the lower differentiable level.
boundary_notes: Approximation orders require additional Lipschitz assumptions.
The hierarchy excludes nonsmooth models and cubic regularization terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Taylor Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-p Taylor model truncates the derivative expansion after degree p; if the p-th derivative is locally Lipschitz, its local value error is of order p+1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(p\)-times continuously differentiable near \(x_k\), where \(p\geq1\). The order-\(p\) Taylor model at \(x_k\) is \[T_{k,p}(s)=f(x_k)+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{1}{j!}\nabla^jf(x_k)[s]^j.\] If \(\nabla^pf\) is locally Lipschitz and the segment \(\{x_k+ts:0\leq t\leq1\}\) remains in that neighborhood, then \[f(x_k+s)-T_{k,p}(s)=O(\|s\|^{p+1})\qquad\text{as }s\to0.\] A trust-region method assesses or minimizes this model only over its prescribed region of trial steps.
assumptions_latex: The segment \(\{x_k+ts:0\leq t\leq1\}\) remains in that neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-p Taylor approximation used as a local trust-region model.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

abla f(x_k)\), since \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \(
abla m_k(0)=
abla f(x_k)\). If additionally \(B_k=

children.top_down_role: Models using updated, partial, sampled, or operator-access curvature information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X\) is a real Hilbert space, \(g_k\in X\), and \(\mathcal B_k:X\to X\) is a bounded self-adjoint linear operator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, updated, sampled, or implicit curvature represented through a self-adjoint operator; no matrix representation is required by the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An operator-curvature local model is \[m_k(p)=c_k+\langle g_k,p\rangle+\tfrac12\langle p,\mathcal B_kp\rangle,\qquad p\in X,\ \|p\|\leq\Delta_k,\] where \(\mathcal B_k\) is bounded and self-adjoint. The model interface is determined by the triple \((c_k,g_k,\mathcal B_k)\); implementations may expose \(\mathcal B_k\) explicitly or only through actions \(v\mapsto\mathcal B_kv\). Exact Hessian, quasi-Newton, sampled-curvature, and projected-curvature choices are members when their operators satisfy these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator-curvature model is a quadratic model on a Hilbert space whose curvature is a bounded self-adjoint linear operator. It is completely specified by its center value, linear coefficient, and curvature operator. The operator may be stored explicitly or accessed only through its action on vectors, and it may represent exact, updated, sampled, or projected curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B_k\) is linear, bounded, and self-adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed quadratic functional defines the operator-curvature model family on the trust region.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In \(X=\mathbb R^n\), self-adjointness is equivalent to a symmetric representing matrix \(B_k=B_k^T\).
special_cases_latex: \(\mathcal B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) gives exact Newton curvature.
A finite-rank \(\mathcal B_k\) gives a partial-curvature model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The model derivative is \(Dm_k(p)[v]=\langle g_k+\mathcal B_kp,v\rangle\).
boundary_notes: Unbounded operators require domain conditions not covered here.
A nonsymmetric operator contributes only through its self-adjoint part to the quadratic form.
review_flags: The available sources support symmetric matrix quadratic models and Hessian-vector products but do not supply this exact Hilbert-space family definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton trust-region model is a quadratic local model whose symmetric curvature approximation is updated from displacements and gradient differences, ordinarily through a safeguarded secant relation.

abla f(x_k)\). A quasi-Newton trust-region model has the form \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+	frac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks,\qquad \|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k,\] where \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}\) is symmetric and approximates Hessian curvature. For successive iterates, define \(p_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=

\(\Delta_k>0\) and \(\|\cdot\|_k\) is the chosen trust-region norm.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, \(s_{k-1}=x_k-x_{k-1}\), and \(y_{k-1}=\nabla f(x_k)-\nabla f(x_{k-1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization using a symmetric Hessian approximation in a quadratic trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quasi-Newton trust-region model is \[m_k(p)=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp,
\qquad \|p\|\leq\Delta_k,\] where \(B_k=B_k^T\) is an approximation to \(\nabla^2f(x_k)\) obtained from previous iterates and gradients by a quasi-Newton update. For an unmodified secant update based on the most recent displacement, the defining interpolation condition is \[B_ks_{k-1}=y_{k-1}.\] Positive definiteness is optional for a trust-region model; indefinite approximations, such as those produced by SR1, remain admissible because the step is restricted to a bounded region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton trust-region model replaces the exact Hessian in the quadratic model by a symmetric matrix updated from previous steps and gradient differences. A standard secant update makes the new approximation map the latest displacement \(s_{k-1}\) to the latest gradient change \(y_{k-1}\). Unlike a line-search direction matrix, the model matrix need not be positive definite because the trust-region subproblem remains bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at the points defining \(y_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic model with updated secant curvature \(B_k\) is a quasi-Newton trust-region model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An inverse update uses \(H_ky_{k-1}=s_{k-1}\) when \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) exists.
special_cases_latex: BFGS maintains positive definiteness when its curvature condition holds.
SR1 may produce an indefinite \(B_k\), which is admissible in a trust region.
immediate_consequences_latex: The model uses curvature information without evaluating the exact Hessian.
boundary_notes: The secant equation alone does not select a unique update.
Skipped or damped updates may replace the exact secant condition by a safeguarded variant.

notation.meaning: Latest iterate displacement and gradient displacement.

children.title: Matrix-Free Curvature Models
children.top_down_role: Models accessed through curvature actions rather than explicit matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Curvature Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature is represented by products with a self-adjoint linear operator, allowing model values, gradients, and Krylov trust-region computations without storing a Hessian matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(g_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\mathcal B_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a linear self-adjoint operator available through products \(v\mapsto\mathcal B_kv\). The matrix-free quadratic model is \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12\langle s,\mathcal B_ks\rangle.\] Its gradient with respect to \(s\) is \[\nabla m_k(s)=g_k+\mathcal B_ks.\] Consequently, model values, gradient actions, and Krylov subproblem iterations can be computed without assembling a curvature matrix. If \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(x_k\) and \(\mathcal B_kv=\nabla^2f(x_k)v\) for every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), this is the exact-Hessian quadratic model in operator form.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with its Euclidean inner product.
The oracle returns \(\mathcal B_kv\) for every requested \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12\langle s,\mathcal B_ks\rangle\) and \(\nabla m_k(s)=g_k+\mathcal B_ks\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic models represented through a symmetric curvature-action oracle.

notation.meaning: model gradient vector at the current point

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Matrix Norms p. 22; II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and an oracle returns \(\mathcal O_k(v)=B_kv\) for requested vectors \(v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale finite-dimensional trust-region models evaluated and minimized through matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A matrix-free curvature model is the quadratic \[m_k(p)=c_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp,
\qquad \|p\|\leq\Delta_k,\] together with an access contract that supplies \(B_kv\) for arbitrary requested \(v\) without requiring assembly or storage of the entries of \(B_k\). The quadratic term is evaluated as \(p^T\mathcal O_k(p)/2\), and Krylov iterations generate their residuals and search directions using only calls to \(\mathcal O_k\), vector operations, and inner products. For Newton curvature, an action may be exact or approximated by a gradient difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free curvature model is an ordinary symmetric quadratic trust-region model equipped only with a vector-product oracle for its curvature matrix. Model values and Krylov subproblem iterations use products \(B_kv\), inner products, and vector operations, so the matrix entries need not be formed or stored. With Newton curvature, the products can be exact Hessian-vector products or gradient-difference approximations.
assumptions_latex: The oracle satisfies \(\mathcal O_k(v)=B_kv\) for every vector requested by the subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((m_k,\mathcal O_k)\) defines a matrix-free curvature model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(p^TB_kp=\langle p,\mathcal O_k(p)\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: For Newton-CG, \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
A finite-difference action is \(\mathcal O_k(v)\approx[\nabla f(x_k+hv)-\nabla f(x_k)]/h\).
immediate_consequences_latex: CG-Steihaug iterations require curvature actions but not an explicit factorization.
boundary_notes: An inaccurate action defines an inexact model and requires separate error control.
Matrix-free access does not by itself reduce the number of oracle calls.

children.title: Subspace-Restricted Models
children.top_down_role: Local models represented and assessed on selected search subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace-Restricted Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal basis parameterizes the selected search subspace, projects the quadratic model into reduced coordinates, and preserves the Euclidean trust-region radius when the reduced step is lifted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k,g_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(\Delta_k>0\). Choose an integer \(r_k\) with \(1\leq r_k\leq n\), and let \(Q_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r_k}\) satisfy \(Q_k^{\mathsf T}Q_k=I_{r_k}\). Its columns span the search subspace \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{range}(Q_k)\), and every restricted step has the form \(s=Q_kz\) for \(z\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k}\). For \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks\), the restricted model is \[\widehat m_k(z)=m_k(Q_kz)=f(x_k)+(Q_k^{\mathsf T}g_k)^{\mathsf T}z+\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}(Q_k^{\mathsf T}B_kQ_k)z.\] Because \(Q_k\) has orthonormal columns, \(\|Q_kz\|_2=\|z\|_2\); hence the Euclidean constraint \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k\) is equivalent to \(\|z\|_2\leq\Delta_k\) on \(\mathcal S_k\).
assumptions_latex: The full-space trust region uses the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat m_k(z)=f(x_k)+(Q_k^{\mathsf T}g_k)^{\mathsf T}z+\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}(Q_k^{\mathsf T}B_kQ_k)z\), with \(\|Q_kz\|_2=\|z\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a quadratic local model and Euclidean trust region to a selected search subspace.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis matrix for the search subspace
reduced coordinates of a trial step
quadratic model restricted to reduced coordinates

If the columns of \(Q_k\) are orthonormal and the Euclidean norm is used, feasibility becomes \(\|z\|_2\leq\Delta_k\). Model adequacy is then assessed only for displacements in \(\mathcal S_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace-restricted model substitutes \(p=Q_kz\) into the full quadratic model. Its reduced gradient is \(Q_k^Tg_k\), its reduced curvature is \(Q_k^TB_kQ_k\), and the trust-region constraint is \(\|Q_kz\|\leq\Delta_k\). With an orthonormal basis and Euclidean norm, the reduced constraint is simply \(\|z\|_2\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat m_k(z)=m_k(Q_kz)\) is the model restricted to the selected search subspace.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reduced coefficients are \(\widehat g_k=Q_k^Tg_k\) and \(\widehat B_k=Q_k^TB_kQ_k\).
special_cases_latex: For positive definite \(B_k\), choosing \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{span}\{g_k,B_k^{-1}g_k\}\) gives two-dimensional subspace minimization.
Krylov subspaces give iteratively enlarged restricted models.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(-g_k\in\mathcal S_k\), the restricted feasible set contains the Cauchy direction.
boundary_notes: Accuracy outside \(\mathcal S_k\) is neither asserted nor assessed.

children.title: Structured Model Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Problem-derived local models whose complete method families belong to neighboring chapters.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(F:X\to Y\) is a problem map, \(\Phi:Y\to\mathbb R\), and the objective has the structured form \(f=\Phi\circ F\), possibly with constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface for importing problem-derived residual, constraint, or regularization structure into trust-region step computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured local-model interface at \(x_k\) is a tuple \[\mathfrak M_k=(m_k,\mathcal T_k,\mathcal E_k),\] where \(m_k\) is obtained from a local representation of the problem maps, \(\mathcal T_k\) is the admissible trust-region step set, and \(\mathcal E_k\) exposes the quantities required to evaluate \(m_k(p)\), its first-order action, and any curvature action for \(p\in\mathcal T_k\). Consistency at the center requires \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \(Dm_k(0)=Df(x_k)\) whenever these derivatives exist. The interface specifies the local object supplied to trust-region globalization, not the complete specialized algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured model interface packages a problem-derived local model, its admissible trust-region steps, and evaluation operations for values, first-order information, and curvature actions. It matches the objective value and derivative at the center when those quantities exist. The interface defines what a specialized model supplies to trust-region globalization, without defining the specialized method's full iteration.
assumptions_latex: The evaluator \(\mathcal E_k\) is defined for every \(p\in\mathcal T_k\).
When first-order consistency is claimed, \(f\) and \(m_k\) are differentiable at the center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak M_k=(m_k,\mathcal T_k,\mathcal E_k)\) is a structured model interface when it satisfies the stated domain and center-consistency conditions.
special_cases_latex: Residual linearization gives the Gauss-Newton interface.
Lagrangian quadratic approximation gives the SQP interface.
immediate_consequences_latex: A trust-region framework can consume different structured models through the same value and derivative-action contract.
boundary_notes: This abstraction does not prescribe acceptance ratios, multiplier updates, or regularization updates.
No single inspected source states this exact interface tuple.
review_flags: A precise authoritative source for this abstract interface formulation was not located.

children.title: Gauss-Newton Model Interface
children.top_down_role: Least-squares local models used within trust-region globalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauss-Newton Model Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the residual, square its norm, and expose the resulting gradient and positive-semidefinite Gauss–Newton curvature to the trust-region globalization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable and define \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\). At \(x_k\), with \(F_k=F(x_k)\) and Jacobian \(J_k=F'(x_k)\), the Gauss--Newton model is \[m_k^{\mathrm{GN}}(s)=\tfrac12\|F_k+J_ks\|_2^2=f(x_k)+(J_k^{\mathsf T}F_k)^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}J_k^{\mathsf T}J_ks.\] Thus the trust-region interface supplies model gradient \(g_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}F_k\), positive-semidefinite curvature \(B_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k\), and products with these quantities, while globalization restricts \(s\) to the chosen trust region and evaluates the actual residual at trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}F_k\) and \(B_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k\succeq0\) define the quadratic Gauss--Newton trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares linearization exposed as a quadratic trust-region model.

notation.meaning: residual vector at the current iterate
residual Jacobian at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is differentiable, \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\), \(r_k=r(x_k)\), and \(J_k=Dr(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear least squares, using residual linearization within a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Gauss-Newton model interface at \(x_k\) is \[m_k^{GN}(p)=\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2,
\qquad \|p\|\leq\Delta_k.\] Its expanded quadratic form is \[m_k^{GN}(p)=\tfrac12\|r_k\|_2^2+(J_k^Tr_k)^Tp+	frac12p^TJ_k^TJ_kp.\] Thus the interface supplies model gradient \(g_k=J_k^Tr_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and positive-semidefinite curvature \(B_k=J_k^TJ_k\), omitting the residual-weighted second-derivative term in the exact Hessian of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonlinear least squares, the Gauss-Newton interface linearizes the residual as \(r_k+J_kp\) and squares its Euclidean norm. The resulting quadratic has exact objective gradient \(J_k^Tr_k\) and positive-semidefinite curvature \(J_k^TJ_k\). It omits the part of the exact objective Hessian that contains second derivatives of the individual residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k^{GN}(p)=\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2\) is the Gauss-Newton local model supplied to trust-region globalization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An unconstrained stationary Gauss-Newton step satisfies \(J_k^TJ_kp=-J_k^Tr_k\) when the normal equations are solvable.
special_cases_latex: If every residual is affine, the Gauss-Newton model equals the objective exactly.
If \(r(x_*)=0\), the omitted residual-weighted Hessian term vanishes at \(x_*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(J_k^TJ_k\succeq0\).
Model products can be evaluated using successive actions by \(J_k\) and \(J_k^T\).
boundary_notes: Rank deficiency may make the unconstrained model minimizer nonunique.
Large residuals can make the omitted curvature significant.

notation.meaning: Residual vector and residual Jacobian at the current point.

children.title: Lagrangian Hessian Model Interface
children.top_down_role: Constrained second-order models entering trust-region SQP and related frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Hessian Model Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface provides an objective gradient, an explicitly oriented constraint Jacobian, and a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian approximation for a linearly constrained trust-region SQP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\). At an iterate \((x_k,\lambda_k)\), a Lagrangian-Hessian model interface supplies \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\in\mathbb R^n\), \(J_k=Dc(x_k)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and a symmetric matrix \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) approximating \(\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). The associated trust-region SQP subproblem is
\[
\min_{s\in\mathbb R^n,\,\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\; f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_ks=0.
\]
Thus, objective curvature is represented by the Lagrangian-Hessian approximation and feasibility by the linearized constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k\) supplies the second-order objective term, while \(c(x_k)+J_ks=0\) supplies the first-order feasibility interface.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP interface using the current Lagrangian Hessian approximation.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian with rows corresponding to constraint components

review_flags: Exact constrained trust-region SQP source locator is absent from the supplied inventory.

abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). The interface is exact-curvature when \(B_k=
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and quasi-Newton otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-constrained problem, the interface supplies a quadratic objective model whose curvature approximates the Hessian of the Lagrangian and a linearized constraint equation \(c(x_k)+A_kp=0\). A trust-region SQP method additionally bounds the step. Exact Lagrangian curvature or a symmetric quasi-Newton approximation may be used.
assumptions_latex: Exact curvature requires the relevant functions to be twice differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed linearly constrained quadratic is the Lagrangian Hessian model passed to a trust-region SQP framework.
equivalent_formulations_latex: On the linearized constraint, \(\nabla f(x_k)^Tp\) may be replaced by \(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)^Tp\) up to a constant determined by feasibility linearization.
special_cases_latex: With no constraints, the model reduces to the ordinary quadratic trust-region model.
A quasi-Newton \(B_k\) gives a quasi-Newton SQP model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only curvature on feasible tangent directions directly affects the tangential step.
boundary_notes: The definition does not specify a merit function or normal-tangential decomposition.
Inequality-constrained SQP requires additional slackness and active-set conditions.

children.top_down_role: Boundary between restricted quadratic models and adaptive cubic regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Cubic-Regularized Model Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic interface augments a quadratic local model by a positive cubic norm term, yielding a coercive unconstrained step model and explicit stationarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), a cubic-regularized model interface supplies \(f_k\in\mathbb R\), \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), a symmetric \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(\sigma_k>0\), and defines
\[
m_k(s)=f_k+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks+\tfrac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_2^3.
\]
Unlike a quadratic trust-region subproblem, the step need not satisfy an explicit radius constraint: coercivity of the positive cubic term ensures that \(m_k\) has a global minimizer. An exact global minimizer \(s_k\) satisfies \((B_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2I)s_k=-g_k\) and \(B_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2I\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) is coercive and possesses a global minimizer satisfying the displayed first- and second-order conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained adaptive cubic regularization with a Euclidean cubic term.

notation.meaning: global minimizer of the cubic model

review_flags: Supplied cubic-interpolation locators do not establish the adaptive cubic-regularization interface.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cubic representation and its mathematical role fit the leaf. The coercivity and exact global-minimizer characterization are nontrivial claims and have no supporting locator; the supplied cubic-interpolation sources concern a different construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cubic regularization of a quadratic local model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and \(\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth optimization using an isotropically cubic-regularized quadratic model, without a separate hard trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A cubic-regularized model interface is \[m_k^{C}(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp+	frac{\sigma_k}{3}\|p\|_2^3,
\qquad p\in\mathbb R^n,\] where \(g_k\) and \(B_k\) represent first- and second-order local information and \(\sigma_k>0\) is the regularization parameter. The cubic term makes the model coercive even when \(B_k\) is indefinite. The interface exposes the same linear and curvature data as a quadratic trust-region model together with \(\sigma_k\), but controls step size through the cubic penalty rather than the constraint \(\|p\|\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic-regularized model adds \(\sigma_k\|p\|_2^3/3\) to a quadratic local model. The positive regularization parameter makes the model grow without bound as the step norm grows, even if the quadratic curvature is indefinite. It therefore controls the step through a penalty rather than through a hard trust-region radius.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean norm is used in the cubic term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed coercive function is the cubic-regularized local-model interface.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(p\neq0\), stationarity is \(g_k+B_kp+\sigma_k\|p\|_2p=0\).
special_cases_latex: With exact data, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(\sigma_k>0\), \(m_k^C(p)\to+\infty\) as \(\|p\|_2\to\infty\), so a global minimizer exists.
boundary_notes: This is not a quadratic trust-region subproblem unless a separate radius constraint is imposed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Step Decrease for the Modified Accelerated Cubic Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional decrease estimate for the modified method; the extract invokes additional hypotheses of an earlier theorem that are not expanded here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex with \(x^*\in\arg\min f\). Assume all hypotheses required for the method \(\mathcal M'\), including constants \(\sigma_2,L_3>0\) and, for every \(k\ge0\), points \(\hat x_k,x_{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
f(x_k)\ge f(\hat x_k)\ge f(x_{k+1}),
\]
\[
f(\hat x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\sigma_2}{6}\|x_{k+1}-\hat x_k\|^3,
\]
and
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\hat x_k\|\ge\frac{\sqrt{2\sigma_2}}{L_3}[f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)]^{1/6}.
\]
If \(M=2L_3\), then for every \(k\ge0\),
\[
f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge f(\hat x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\sqrt2\,\sigma_2^{3/2}}{3L_3}[f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)]^{1/2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, if every modified accelerated cubic Newton step is monotone, satisfies the stated cubic decrease inequality, and has the stated suboptimality-controlled length, then choosing M equal to twice L3 gives the displayed square-root suboptimality lower bound on every one-step objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: \text{All other hypotheses invoked for }\mathcal M'\text{ hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge0:\quad f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge f(\hat x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\sqrt2\,\sigma_2^{3/2}}{3L_3}[f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)]^{1/2}

children.title: Model Accuracy Classes
children.top_down_role: Fidelity taxonomies relating local approximation quality to trust-region scale.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), model class \(\mathcal M\), centers \(x\in S\), and radii \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform deterministic accuracy classes indexed by the trust-region scale and derivative order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q\in\{1,2\}\), a model class \(\mathcal M\) is a deterministic order-\(q\) accuracy class for \(f\) if constants \(\kappa_0,\ldots,\kappa_q>0\), independent of \(x\) and \(\Delta\), exist such that for every admissible \((x,\Delta)\) one can select \(m\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \[\|D^jf(y)-D^jm(y)\|\leq\kappa_j\Delta^{q+1-j},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,q,
\quad y\in B(x;\Delta).\] For \(j=0\), the norm denotes absolute value. The class must also admit a uniformly finite procedure that certifies such a model or replaces it by one satisfying these bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-\(q\) model accuracy class provides, at every admissible center and radius, a model whose errors in derivatives of orders zero through \(q\) scale respectively as \(\Delta^{q+1-j}\). The constants are uniform, and a finite uniformly bounded procedure must be able to certify or construct an accurate member. Orders one and two correspond to fully linear and fully quadratic classes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and candidate models possess the derivatives appearing through order \(q\).
The corresponding highest derivative has the regularity needed for uniform Taylor-type bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The derivative-error inequalities and finite certification requirement define the deterministic model accuracy class of order \(q\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q=1\), the errors are \(O(\Delta^2)\) in value and \(O(\Delta)\) in gradient.
For \(q=2\), the errors are \(O(\Delta^3)\), \(O(\Delta^2)\), and \(O(\Delta)\) in value, gradient, and Hessian.
special_cases_latex: Fully linear and fully quadratic model classes are the \(q=1\) and \(q=2\) instances.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition compares accuracy at a common trust-region scale and permits different model constructions at different centers and radii.
boundary_notes: The definition is deterministic; probability-qualified models require separate quantifiers.
A class may contain inaccurate members, provided an accurate member can be selected or produced.

notation.meaning: Derivative of order j, with order zero interpreted as the function value.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Linear Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully linear model approximates function values to order radius squared and gradients to order radius throughout the trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\Delta>0\). A continuously differentiable model \(m\) is fully linear for \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)=\{y:\|y-x\|\leq\Delta\}\) with constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg}\geq0\) if, for every \(y\in B(x,\Delta)\),
\[
|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^2,
\qquad
\|\nabla f(y)-\nabla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta.
\]
For a model family, the constants are required to be independent of the center and radius over the algorithmically admitted collection of balls.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\) has uniform first-order fidelity to \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order fidelity on a closed trust-region ball.

notation.meaning: closed norm ball centered at x with radius Delta
uniform function and gradient error constants

children.top_down_role: Second-order model-fidelity family used in model-based trust-region analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully quadratic model approximates values, gradients, and Hessians to orders three, two, and one in the trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\Delta>0\). A twice continuously differentiable model \(m\) is fully quadratic for \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\) with constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},\kappa_{eh}\geq0\) if every \(y\in B(x,\Delta)\) satisfies
\[
|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^3,
\quad \|\nabla f(y)-\nabla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta^2,
\quad \|\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eh}\Delta.
\]
For a model family, these constants are uniform over the admitted centers and radii.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\) has uniform second-order fidelity to \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic second-order fidelity on a closed trust-region ball.

uniform value, gradient, and Hessian error constants

children.title: Imperfect Model Accuracy Classes
children.top_down_role: Model families whose accuracy is conditional, iteration-dependent, approximate, or probabilistic.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta_k>0\), and let the iteration-dependent model \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be defined on \(B_k=\{x:\|x-x_k\|\leq\Delta_k\}\). Let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) denote the information available before constructing \(m_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local models whose fidelity can be approximate, conditional, or random; no convergence assertion is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An imperfect model-accuracy specification is a sequence of events \(A_k(\delta)\), for \(0<\delta\leq\Delta_k\), and constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g\geq0\) such that on \(A_k(\delta)\), \[|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa_f\delta^2\quad(\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta),\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k)-\nabla m_k(x_k)\|\leq\kappa_g\delta.\] The specification is deterministic if \(A_k(\delta)\) always holds, conditional if an algorithmically testable predicate implies \(A_k(\delta)\), and probabilistic at level \(p\in(0,1]\) if \(\mathbb P(A_k(\delta)\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely. A model family is imperfectly accurate when it is assigned at least one of these non-unconditional qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an objective \(f\), center \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), and local model \(m_k\), an imperfect accuracy class is specified by events \(A_k(\delta)\). Whenever the event occurs, the function-value error throughout the radius-\(\delta\) ball is at most \(\kappa_f\delta^2\), and the gradient error at the center is at most \(\kappa_g\delta\). The qualification may be deterministic, triggered by a checkable condition, or probabilistic through a conditional-probability lower bound given past information. Thus the term denotes a fidelity requirement that need not hold unconditionally at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) belongs to the specified imperfect accuracy class exactly when the stated error bounds hold on the associated event \(A_k(\delta)\), with the declared deterministic, conditional, or probabilistic quantifier.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(e_k(x)=f(x)-m_k(x)\), the value condition is \(\sup_{\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta}|e_k(x)|/\delta^2\leq\kappa_f\) on \(A_k(\delta)\).
special_cases_latex: The conditional class is obtained when \(A_k(\delta)=\{C_k(\delta)=\mathrm{true}\}\) for a model-validity predicate \(C_k\).
The deterministic class corresponds to \(\mathbb P(A_k(\delta)\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition separates the magnitude of the required local error from the logical or probabilistic mechanism under which that error is guaranteed.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how an invalid model is repaired or how many repair steps are required.
The probabilistic branch requires an authoritative source matching the filtration and conditional-probability convention before promotion.

notation.meaning: Event on which the iteration-k model satisfies the radius-dependent fidelity bounds.
Past-information sigma-field available before constructing the current random model.

children.title: Conditional Models
children.top_down_role: Models required to satisfy fidelity conditions only in algorithmically relevant circumstances.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional model must meet a specified fidelity predicate whenever a predeclared algorithmic trigger is active; inactive iterations carry no fidelity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k\) be a model on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), let \(T_k\in\{0,1\}\) be an algorithmically specified trigger measurable from information available when the model is assessed, and let \(\mathcal A_k\) denote a chosen deterministic fidelity predicate, such as full linearity. The sequence is conditionally accurate relative to \((T_k)\) when
\[
T_k=1\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathcal A_k(m_k;f,x_k,\Delta_k)\text{ holds}
\]
for every iteration \(k\). No accuracy assertion is imposed when \(T_k=0\). The trigger must be fixed independently of whether the unobserved fidelity inequalities happen to hold, so the implication cannot be made vacuous by inspecting their failure.
assumptions_latex: \(T_k\) is determined by information available at model assessment.
\(\mathcal A_k\) is a precisely specified deterministic fidelity predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_k=1\) guarantees the required model-accuracy event \(\mathcal A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise fidelity imposed only when an algorithmic trigger is active.
review_flags: Conditional-model terminology is not uniquely standardized without a designated algorithmic framework.
A source is needed to confirm the intended trigger convention.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate knowledge kind, but this trigger-based meaning of “conditional models” is framework-dependent. A designated algorithmic framework and locator are needed to determine whether the trigger, measurability, and non-vacuity requirements match the intended leaf sense.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. For \(\delta>0\), set \(Q_k(\delta)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional conditional models with a checkable validity condition and finitely terminating model improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model \(m_k\) is valid in \(Q_k(\delta)\) if there is a constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}>0\), independent of \(x\), such that \[|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\delta^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in Q_k(\delta).\] It is a conditional model if this validity property is required only when a designated, algorithmically checkable condition \(C_k(\delta)\) holds, validity can be checked for every \(k\) and \(\delta>0\), and for every \(k,\delta\) a finite sequence of model-improvement operations can produce a model for which \(C_k(\delta)\) and hence the displayed bound hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model \(m_k\) is valid on the ball \(Q_k(\delta)\) when its error from \(f\) is uniformly bounded there by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\delta^2\). It is conditional when this error guarantee is attached to a designated condition that can be tested by the algorithm, rather than imposed at every construction, and when any failed condition can be made true after finitely many model-improvement operations for every positive radius. The definition therefore includes both the fidelity inequality and the finite repair requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) is conditionally valid on \(Q_k(\delta)\) precisely when the checkable condition \(C_k(\delta)\) certifies the uniform \(O(\delta^2)\) value error and failed validity can be restored in finitely many improvement steps.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The validity inequality is \(\sup_{x\in Q_k(\delta)}|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\delta^2\).
special_cases_latex: For interpolation models, \(C_k(\delta)\) may require an adequately poised interpolation set contained in \(Q_k(\delta)\).
An improvement operation may add a newly evaluated point in \(Q_k(\delta)\) and rebuild the model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Validity applies in particular at \(x_k\) and at every trial point lying in \(Q_k(\delta)\).
The finite-improvement condition excludes a model defect that persists forever at a fixed center and radius.
boundary_notes: Conditional validity is stronger than merely observing a good reduction ratio at one trial point because its error bound is uniform over the ball.
No probability qualification is part of this deterministic definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Models with Approximate Derivatives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient errors of order radius squared and Hessian errors of order radius make a centered quadratic model fully quadratic under Lipschitz-Hessian regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) have an \(L_H\)-Lipschitz Hessian on \(B(x,\Delta)\), and define
\[
m(x+s)=f(x)+\widetilde g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Hs.
\]
If \(\|\widetilde g-\nabla f(x)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta^2\) and \(\|\widetilde H-\nabla^2f(x)\|\leq\kappa_H\Delta\), then, for every \(s\) satisfying \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\),
\[
|f(x+s)-m(x+s)|\leq\left(\kappa_g+\tfrac12\kappa_H+\tfrac16L_H\right)\Delta^3.
\]
The same derivative-error scaling, together with Hessian Lipschitz continuity, yields gradient error of order \(\Delta^2\) and Hessian error of order \(\Delta\), and hence fully quadratic fidelity with suitable uniform constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(\nabla^2 f\) is \(L_H\)-Lipschitz on \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The approximate-derivative quadratic model is fully quadratic on \(B(x,\Delta)\), with constants determined by \(\kappa_g\), \(\kappa_H\), and \(L_H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radius-scaled derivative errors sufficient for quadratic-model fidelity.

notation.meaning: closed trust-region ball centered at x with radius Delta

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region model with controlled approximate derivatives
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and define \(m_k(x_k+s)=m_k(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), where \(H_k=H_k^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth trust-region models with inexact gradients and finite-difference or quasi-Newton curvature approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic model has controlled approximate derivatives if its gradient error \(v_k=\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\) satisfies \[\|v_k\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}\|g_k\|\quad\text{for every }k\] for a fixed admissible \(\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}\geq0\), and its symmetric curvature matrix \(H_k\) is generated by a declared approximation rule. Admissible rules include finite differences with a stated difference vector \(h_k\), or a secant update satisfying \[H_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k,\] whenever the update denominator required by the selected formula is nonzero. The model class records both the error control and the derivative-construction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic trust-region model with approximate derivatives uses a model gradient \(g_k\) and symmetric curvature approximation \(H_k\) in place of exact derivatives. The gradient discrepancy \(v_k=\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\) must be bounded relative to the model gradient by a fixed constant. The curvature approximation must come from an explicitly declared mechanism, such as finite differences or a symmetric quasi-Newton update satisfying the secant equation. Thus merely labeling derivatives approximate is insufficient: the approximation error and update domain must be specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model belongs to the controlled approximate-derivative class when \(\|\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}\|g_k\|\) and \(H_k\) is produced by its stated well-defined finite-difference or secant rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}<1\), then \((1-\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}})\|g_k\|\leq\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq(1+\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}})\|g_k\|\).
special_cases_latex: The BFGS rule is defined when \(y_k^Ts_k>0\).
The SR1 rule is defined when \((y_k-H_ks_k)^Ts_k\neq0\).
A forward finite-difference gradient uses \([g_k]_i=(f(x_k+[h_k]_ie_i)-f(x_k))/|[h_k]_i|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g_{k_j}\to0\) along a subsequence, the relative-error condition forces \(\nabla f(x_{k_j})\to0\).
boundary_notes: Finite-precision noise limits how far finite-difference steps can be reduced reliably.
First-order error control alone does not ensure that an approximate Hessian detects all negative curvature.

notation.meaning: Error of the model gradient relative to the objective gradient.
Difference of successive model gradients used in a secant equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-difference, automatic, and symbolic derivative calculation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes three derivative-acquisition approaches without asserting an error order or convergence guarantee for the finite-difference formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, a small scalar $\epsilon>0$, and the $i$th unit vector $e_i$, the partial derivative at $x$ may be approximated by the central difference
\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)\approx\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x-\epsilon e_i)}{2\epsilon}.
\]
Automatic differentiation obtains derivatives by decomposing function-evaluation code into elementary operations and applying the chain rule, either by generating derivative-evaluation code or by recording and processing the executed operations at the evaluation point. Symbolic differentiation instead manipulates an algebraic specification of $f$ to produce expressions for the components of $\nabla f$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth real-valued function on Euclidean space, the ith partial derivative at a point can be approximated from function values at small positive and negative perturbations along the ith coordinate direction. Automatic differentiation applies the chain rule to the elementary operations in evaluation code, while symbolic differentiation manipulates an algebraic function specification to produce gradient-component expressions.
assumptions_latex: e_i\text{ is the }i\text{th standard unit vector}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)\approx\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x-\epsilon e_i)}{2\epsilon}

children.title: Probabilistically Accurate Models

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistically Accurate Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random model is probabilistically accurate when, conditional on the past, its deterministic fidelity event has probability at least a fixed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_k\) be a random model, let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) contain the algorithmic history available before \(M_k\) is generated, and let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the event that \(M_k\) satisfies a specified deterministic fidelity predicate on \(B(X_k,\Delta_k)\). For \(p\in(0,1]\), the models are probabilistically \(p\)-accurate if
\[
\mathbb P(\mathcal A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p
\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.
\]
The event may encode fully linear or fully quadratic inequalities with constants fixed independently of \(k\); the conditioning permits adaptive centers and radii while requiring a uniform lower probability of accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\mathcal A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-probability formulation for random trust-region models.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers probabilistic trust-region model accuracy.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate for this leaf, and the conditional-probability formulation is coherent. The filtration timing and accuracy-event convention vary across stochastic trust-region frameworks, so a specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space with filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\). Let \(X_k\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and the random model \(M_k\) be measurable with the model constructed after observing \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional stochastic local models with conditional, iterationwise fidelity events; independence across iterations is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in(0,1]\) and constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g\geq0\). Define \[A_k=\left\{\sup_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}|f(X_k+s)-M_k(X_k+s)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\quad \|\nabla f(X_k)-\nabla M_k(X_k)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\right\}.\] The random model sequence is probabilistically accurate at level \(p\) if \[\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.\] The conditional bound, rather than an unconditional marginal probability, is part of the class definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random local model is probabilistically accurate at level \(p\) when, conditionally on all information available before the current model is generated, it has probability at least \(p\) of satisfying both a uniform \(O(\Delta_k^2)\) function-value error over the trust region and an \(O(\Delta_k)\) gradient error at its center. This requirement is imposed at every iteration and does not require the model events to be independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M_k)\) belongs to the probabilistically accurate class exactly when \(\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely for all \(k\), with \(A_k\) equal to the displayed fidelity event.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is \(\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{A_k}\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]\geq p\) almost surely.
special_cases_latex: For \(p=1\), the accuracy event holds conditionally almost surely.
If \(M_k\) is deterministic given \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\), the condition reduces to deterministic accuracy whenever \(p>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition permits temporally dependent model errors provided the iterationwise conditional success probability is maintained.
boundary_notes: An unconditional inequality \(\mathbb P(A_k)\geq p\) alone does not satisfy this definition.
The supplied sources do not establish the exact filtration convention or constants, so authoritative evidence is required.

notation.meaning: Event that the current random model satisfies both local accuracy inequalities.
Uniform lower bound on conditional model-accuracy probability.

review_flags: No inspected supplied source supports the probabilistically accurate model definition with the stated conditional filtration.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\). At iteration \(k\), let \(Z_k=(x_k,\Delta_k,m_k,D_k)\), where \(D_k\) is the derivative or sample information retained by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic model-management family covering construction, reuse, validation, improvement, and replacement; it is not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model-lifecycle system is a state-transition map \[Z_{k+1}\in\mathcal T(Z_k,o_k),\] where \(o_k\) contains newly observed function or derivative information, together with a validity predicate \(V(Z_k,\delta)\). Its transitions are partitioned into: construction, which creates \(m_k\) from \(D_k\); reuse, which retains prior model information; validation, which evaluates \(V\); improvement, which changes \(D_k\) or \(m_k\) after failed validity; and replacement, which discards designated stale information. For every fixed \((x_k,\delta)\), repeated improvement transitions must terminate after finitely many steps at a state satisfying \[V(Z_k,\delta)=1\implies\sup_{\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta}|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa\delta^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model lifecycle is a state-transition system whose state contains the current point, radius, model, and retained derivative or sample data. Its allowed transitions construct, reuse, validate, improve, or replace model information. A declared validity predicate connects the management state to a uniform local fidelity bound. The essential termination condition is that, at a fixed center and radius, repeated improvement cannot continue indefinitely without producing a valid model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transition family is a model-lifecycle system when it supplies the stated state components, typed transitions, validity implication, and finite termination of model improvement at every fixed center and positive radius.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The lifecycle may be represented as a directed state graph whose improvement-only subgraph has no infinite path at fixed \((x_k,\delta)\).
special_cases_latex: A conditional interpolation lifecycle adds or exchanges sample points until the interpolation set is sufficiently poised.
A quasi-Newton lifecycle reuses \(H_k\) and replaces it by a secant update when the update denominator is admissible.
A memory lifecycle forms \(m_k=(1-\alpha_k)q_k+\alpha_km_{k-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Validity and model construction are separate components: a syntactically defined model need not yet be certified adequate.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require every implementation to support every transition type.
The source supports the component mechanisms, but the unified state-transition packaging is a formal synthesis.

notation.meaning: Complete model-management state at iteration k.

children.title: Derivative-Model Lifecycle System
children.top_down_role: Curvature refresh, model reuse, replacement, and memory mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m_k(x_k+s)=f_k+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), with \(H_k=H_k^T\), and let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional quadratic models managed through exact refresh, finite differences, quasi-Newton reuse, or limited memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-model lifecycle state is \(D_k=(g_k,H_k,\mathcal M_k)\), where \(\mathcal M_k\) stores selected correction data. A lifecycle transition chooses exactly one declared operation: \[\text{refresh: }(g_{k+1},H_{k+1})=(\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\nabla^2f(x_{k+1}));\] \[\text{difference: }(g_{k+1},H_{k+1})=(\bar g(x_{k+1},h_{k+1}),\bar H(x_{k+1},h_{k+1}));\] or \[\text{secant reuse: }H_{k+1}=U(H_k,s_k,y_k),\qquad H_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\] provided the selected update \(U\) is well defined. Limited-memory reuse retains only a prescribed number of low-rank correction pairs, while replacement clears \(\mathcal M_k\) and initializes a new base matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-model lifecycle records the current gradient approximation, symmetric curvature approximation, and any retained correction pairs. Each transition is explicitly classified as an exact derivative refresh, finite-difference reconstruction, secant reuse, limited-memory update, or replacement. Secant reuse must satisfy the secant equation and may be performed only when the chosen formula is defined. A replacement discards the designated memory and installs a new base approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D_k)\) is a derivative-model lifecycle precisely when every derivative-state change follows one of the declared refresh, difference, secant, limited-memory, or replacement operations with its domain conditions enforced.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A dense quasi-Newton lifecycle takes \(\mathcal M_k=\varnothing\) and stores the complete matrix \(H_k\); a limited-memory lifecycle represents \(H_k\) implicitly from a base matrix and retained correction pairs.
special_cases_latex: BFGS reuse requires \(y_k^Ts_k>0\) and preserves positive definiteness when initialized positive definite.
SR1 reuse requires \((y_k-H_ks_k)^Ts_k\neq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Low-rank secant reuse separates information retention from a complete derivative recomputation.
boundary_notes: Skipping an undefined update is distinct from asserting that the secant equation holds.
No convergence property follows solely from the lifecycle definition.
