knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular, non-hard-case Euclidean trust-region multiplier computation. The bracket must remain in the positive-definite shifted domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A safeguarded secular root solver generates \(\lambda_j\in[L_j,U_j]\subset\mathcal D\) for the equation \[\phi(\lambda)=\frac1\Delta-\frac1{\|p(\lambda)\|_2}=0.\] Each trial shift is obtained from a Newton or rational-interpolation proposal and then projected or replaced so that \(\lambda_{j+1}\in[L_j,U_j]\) and \(B+\lambda_{j+1}I\succ0\). After evaluating \(\|p(\lambda_{j+1})\|_2-\Delta\), the bracket is reduced while retaining a root. The returned multiplier satisfies a stated secular residual or radial tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded secular solver computes the trust-region multiplier as a bracketed scalar root. It combines a fast local update with bounds that prevent a shift for which the Cholesky factorization fails. Every accepted iterate remains in the positive-definite shifted domain, and the bracket is updated from whether the corresponding step is longer or shorter than the target radius.
assumptions_latex: The regular secular equation has a root in an initial bracket \([L_0,U_0]\subset\mathcal D\).
Shifted systems are solved sufficiently accurately to evaluate the radial residual.
A termination tolerance is prescribed for \(|\phi(\lambda)|\) or \(|\|p(\lambda)\|_2-\Delta|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver returns \(\widehat\lambda\in\mathcal D\) with \(B+\widehat\lambda I\succ0\) and the prescribed secular or radial residual tolerance satisfied.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The same root may be written as \(\|p(\lambda)\|_2-\Delta=0\); the reciprocal form is typically closer to linear near the left spectral endpoint.
special_cases_latex: Without activation of a safeguard, the update is the Newton iteration applied to the reciprocal-norm secular function.
immediate_consequences_latex: All shifted Cholesky factorizations requested by the safeguarded iteration are well-defined.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), with dense symmetric \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense Euclidean trust-region solvers whose principal operation is factorization of a sequence of scalar shifts of the model Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A shifted factorization solver generates admissible shifts \(\lambda_j\) satisfying \(B+\lambda_jI\succ0\), factors \[B+\lambda_jI=R_j^TR_j,\] and computes \(p_j\) and optionally \(w_j\) from \[R_j^TR_jp_j=-g,\qquad R_j^Tw_j=p_j.\] The factorization-derived quantities determine a new shift, for example \[\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j+\left(\frac{\|p_j\|_2}{\|w_j\|_2}\right)^2\frac{\|p_j\|_2-\Delta}{\Delta},\] subject to safeguards. The returned step is the final \(p_j\) meeting the chosen radial or optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family solves the trust-region multiplier problem by repeatedly factoring matrices of the form \(B+\lambda I\). Each factorization supplies both the shifted-system step and derivative information for updating the shift. Admissible shifts keep the factorization positive definite, and iteration stops when the step has the required relation to the trust-region radius.
assumptions_latex: The update is safeguarded whenever its raw value leaves the positive-definite shift interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output has the form \(p=-(B+\widehat\lambda I)^{-1}g\) and satisfies the solver’s stated trust-region radial or multiplier tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The auxiliary solve gives derivative information for Newton iteration on \(1/\Delta-1/\|p(\lambda)\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(B\succ0\) and \(\|B^{-1}g\|_2\le\Delta\), a single unshifted factorization with \(\lambda=0\) suffices.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method avoids forming \((B+\lambda I)^{-1}\) explicitly; triangular solves determine the step.
boundary_notes: A singular endpoint in the hard case requires a modified factorization or eigenvector construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Shifted Factorization Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly factor the shifted Hessian, solve for the trial step, and update the multiplier until feasibility, positive semidefiniteness, and complementarity hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a safeguarded multiplier \(\lambda\geq\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(B)\}\). At each regular iteration, factor \(B+\lambda I=LL^{\mathsf T}\), solve \(LL^{\mathsf T}p=-g\), and test \(\lVert p\rVert\leq\Delta\) together with complementarity. If the boundary is active, use the factorization to evaluate a secular Newton correction, safeguard the new multiplier inside a valid bracket, and refactor at the new shift. Stop when \(B+\lambda I\succeq0\), \(\lVert p\rVert\leq\Delta\), and \(|\lambda(\Delta-\lVert p\rVert)|\) is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A separate hard-case correction is invoked if the shifted matrix becomes singular at the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \((B+\lambda I)p=-g\) and the trust-region optimality conditions hold to the prescribed tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Modification Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modify an indefinite shifted Hessian until it factors stably, then adjust the shift using the step norm and remove the modification before accepting the solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a trial shift \(\lambda\geq0\), attempt a stable factorization of \(B+\lambda I\). If a nonpositive or inadequately small pivot is encountered, increase \(\lambda\) or apply a symmetric modification \(E\succeq0\) so that \(B+\lambda I+E\succ0\). Solve \((B+\lambda I+E)p=-g\), use \(\lVert p\rVert-\Delta\) to update a safeguarded shift interval, and reduce the modification as regularity is approached. Return an unmodified step only after \(E=0\) and the trust-region optimality residuals meet tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The factorization reports loss of positive definiteness or unsafe pivots.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance with \(E=0\) yields a step satisfying the original, rather than modified, shifted trust-region equations to tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shift selection through positive-definiteness tests and stable matrix modification.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact numerical factors are reusable at the same shift; changing the shift generally requires refactorization or a specialized update, although symbolic structure remains reusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(B\), a numerical factorization of \(B+\lambda I\) may be reused without alteration for multiple right-hand sides at the same \(\lambda\). Its elimination ordering and symbolic structure may also be reused when \(\lambda\) changes. In general, however, a factorization at \(\lambda_1\) is not an exact factorization at \(\lambda_2\neq\lambda_1\), because \((\lambda_2-\lambda_1)I\) is a full-rank update. Thus shifted iterations require numerical refactorization, a specialized diagonal-shift update, or a previously computed eigendecomposition.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and fixed across the compared solves.
The statement concerns exact arithmetic identities; numerical stability may impose additional refactorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordinary factor reuse is exact for equal shifts, while unequal shifts require additional numerical work unless a shift-aware representation is maintained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid and limited forms of reuse across shifted dense solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Moré-Sorensen Hard-Case Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the hard case, solve with the singular optimal shift and add a minimum-eigenvector component that reaches the trust-region boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_1=\lambda_{\min}(B)<0\), set \(\lambda_*=-d_1\), and suppose \(g\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal E_1=\ker(B-d_1I)\). Compute the minimum-norm solution \(\widehat p=-(B-d_1I)^{\dagger}g\). If \(\lVert\widehat p\rVert<\Delta\), choose a unit vector \(z\in\mathcal E_1\) and a scalar \(\alpha\) satisfying \(\lVert\widehat p+\alpha z\rVert=\Delta\), selecting the sign that minimizes the model, and return \(p_*=
\widehat p+\alpha z\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B=Q\operatorname{diag}(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)Q^T\), where \(\theta_1=\lambda_{\min}(B)<0\), and let \(E_1=\ker(B-\theta_1I)\). Consider \(\min_{\|p\|_2\le\Delta}g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The exact Euclidean hard case caused by orthogonality of the gradient to the leftmost eigenspace; numerical near-hard variants replace exact tests by tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Moré–Sorensen hard case occurs when \(Q_1^Tg=0\), where the columns of \(Q_1\) span \(E_1\), and the regular shifted solution at the spectral endpoint has norm below \(\Delta\). Set \(\lambda_*=-\theta_1\) and let \[p_0=-(B-\theta_1I)^\dagger g.\] Choose a unit \(z\in E_1\) and a scalar \(\tau\) satisfying \[\|p_0+\tau z\|_2=\Delta.\] A hard-case step is \(p_*=p_0+\tau z\), with the sign of \(\tau\) chosen to minimize the model if the two boundary choices differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the hard case, the gradient has no component in the eigenspace of the most negative eigenvalue, so the regular secular equation may never reach the trust-region boundary. The multiplier is fixed at the singular spectral endpoint. A minimum-norm shifted-system solution is then augmented by a component in the leftmost eigenspace until the step reaches the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a suitable \(\tau\), \((B+\lambda_*I)p_*=-g\), \(B+\lambda_*I\succeq0\), and \(\|p_*\|_2=\Delta\), where \(\lambda_*=-\theta_1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In an eigenbasis, \(p_0=-\sum_{i:\theta_i\ne\theta_1}(q_i^Tg)/(\theta_i-\theta_1)\,q_i\), followed by an eigenspace component \(\tau z\).
special_cases_latex: If \(E_1\) is one-dimensional, \(|\tau|=\sqrt{\Delta^2-\|p_0\|_2^2}\).
For a multiple leftmost eigenvalue, any unit \(z\in E_1\) may be used subject to the model-minimizing choice.
immediate_consequences_latex: The completed step satisfies the global trust-region optimality conditions despite singularity of the shifted Hessian.
boundary_notes: If \(Q_1^Tg\ne0\), the ordinary regular secular root is used instead.
Near-hard numerical cases require tolerances for eigenspace orthogonality and singularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Based Subproblem Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonalize the Hessian, solve a scalar secular equation for the shift, reconstruct the step, and apply an eigenspace correction in the hard case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(B=Q\operatorname{diag}(d_i)Q^{\mathsf T}\) and \(h=Q^{\mathsf T}g\). In the regular case, find \(\lambda\geq\max\{0,-\min_i d_i\}\) such that \[\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{h_i^2}{(d_i+\lambda)^2}=\Delta^2,\] unless the unshifted minimizer is feasible. Set \(p=-Q\operatorname{diag}((d_i+\lambda)^{-1})h\). If a denominator vanishes and the corresponding \(h_i=0\), use the pseudoinverse components and add a vector from the minimum-eigenvalue eigenspace to attain norm \(\Delta\).
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean trust-region subproblem is solved in exact spectral coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstructed step and multiplier satisfy the global optimality conditions \((B+\lambda I)p=-g\), \(B+\lambda I\succeq0\), \(\lVert p\rVert\leq\Delta\), and \(\lambda(\lVert p\rVert-\Delta)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense trust-region solution using a spectral decomposition and scalar multiplier search.

notation.meaning: orthogonal eigenvector matrix of the Hessian

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral solver diagonalizes the symmetric model Hessian and performs the multiplier calculation in eigen-coordinates. The shifted-system step and its norm become scalar sums over eigenvalues. The multiplier is chosen to meet the trust-region optimality conditions, while a singular leftmost eigenspace is treated by a pseudoinverse and, when necessary, a boundary component.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \((p,\lambda)\) satisfies \((B+\lambda I)p=-g\), \(B+\lambda I\succeq0\), \(\|p\|_2\le\Delta\), and \(\lambda(\Delta-\|p\|_2)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The full subproblem is transformed by \(p=Qy\) into \(\min_{\|y\|_2\le\Delta}c^Ty+\tfrac12\sum_i\theta_i y_i^2\).
special_cases_latex: For diagonal \(B\), \(Q=I\) and no eigenvector transformation is required.
Partial spectral solvers may use the leftmost eigenpair to identify negative curvature while treating the remaining shifted system iteratively.
immediate_consequences_latex: The smallest eigenvalue directly supplies the lower admissible bound \(\lambda\ge-\theta_1\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) encode linear or convex step constraints, let \(D\) be nonsingular, and let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf G}\) be a specified norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional scaled, projected, or non-Euclidean trust-region geometry. The family is defined by exact or approximate minimization over the stated structured feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured-geometry trust-region solver returns an admissible approximate minimizer of \[\min_{p\in\mathcal F}\ q(p)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|Dp\|_{\mathsf G}\le\Delta.\] For an ellipsoidal Euclidean region, \(\|Dp\|_2\le\Delta\), the change of variables \(y=Dp\) gives the spherical reduced model \[(D^{-T}g)^Ty+\tfrac12y^T(D^{-T}BD^{-1})y,\qquad \|y\|_2\le\Delta.\] Projected variants additionally maintain \(p\in\mathcal F\); reduced-space variants parameterize feasible steps before solving the transformed subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured-geometry solver incorporates the actual geometry of the step set into the trust-region subproblem. Scaling produces ellipsoidal regions, other norms produce non-spherical regions, and constraints restrict steps to a feasible or tangent set. For an invertible Euclidean scaling, the problem is equivalent to a spherical trust-region problem in transformed variables.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is nonsingular for the stated change of variables.
The feasible set \(\mathcal F\) is nonempty and contains the zero step when a feasible current iterate is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver output satisfies \(p\in\mathcal F\) and \(\|Dp\|_{\mathsf G}\le\Delta\), and minimizes or meets a stated approximation condition for \(q\) on that structured region.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\mathcal F=\mathbb R^n\) and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf G}=\|\cdot\|_2\), solving in \(p\) is equivalent to solving the transformed spherical problem in \(y=Dp\).
special_cases_latex: \(D=I\) and the Euclidean norm give the standard spherical trust-region subproblem.
The infinity norm yields a box-shaped trust region.
A linear subspace \(\mathcal F=\ker A\) gives a projected or reduced-space trust-region problem.
immediate_consequences_latex: The transformed gradient is \(D^{-T}g\) and transformed Hessian is \(D^{-T}BD^{-1}\).
boundary_notes: Different norms generally require different subproblem algorithms; Euclidean multiplier formulas cannot be transferred unchanged.
If \(D\) is singular, the displayed variable transformation is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the quadratic model onto an orthonormal feasible basis, solve the reduced trust-region problem globally, and lift the reduced minimizer back to the original space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given symmetric \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) with orthonormal columns spanning the admissible subspace, form \(B_Z=Z^\top BZ\) and \(g_Z=Z^\top g\). Compute a global minimizer
\[u_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|u\|_2\leq\Delta}\left(g_Z^\top u+\tfrac12u^\top B_Zu\right),\]
and return \(s_*=Zu_*\). Then \(s_*\) globally minimizes \(g^\top s+\tfrac12s^\top Bs\) over \(s\in\operatorname{range}(Z)\) with \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_*=Zu_*\) is a global minimizer on \(\operatorname{range}(Z)\cap\{s:\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-space solver for an equality-constrained Euclidean trust-region quadratic model.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the admissible subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Norm Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a norm-ball linear minimization oracle and exact segment searches. The computable conditional-gradient gap certifies global objective error for the convex quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta\}\) and \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\). Initialize \(s_0\in K\). At iteration \(j\), obtain \(v_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in K}(g+Bs_j)^{\mathsf T}v\) from a linear minimization oracle and compute \(d_j=(g+Bs_j)^{\mathsf T}(s_j-v_j)\). If \(d_j\leq\varepsilon\), return \(s_j\). Otherwise choose \(\gamma_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}m(s_j+\gamma(v_j-s_j))\) and set \(s_{j+1}=s_j+\gamma_j(v_j-s_j)\). Every iterate is feasible, and termination certifies \(0\leq m(s_j)-\min_{s\in K}m(s)\leq d_j\leq\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is any norm on \(\mathbb R^n\), and linear minimization over its radius-\(\Delta\) ball is available.
The one-dimensional minimization defining \(\gamma_j\) is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_j\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow m(s_j)-\min_{\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta}m(s)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-gradient solver template for a convex quadratic trust-region subproblem under an arbitrary finite-dimensional norm.

notation.meaning: The trust-region ball under the chosen norm.
The conditional-gradient dual gap at iteration j.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Norm Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection is norm-compatible when it is nonexpansive in the trust-region norm, so projecting any feasible step preserves feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be a linear projector and let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal N}\) define the trust region. Projection and norm are compatible when
\[P^2=P,\qquad \|Ps\|_{\mathcal N}\leq\|s\|_{\mathcal N}\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb R^n.\]
Consequently, projection maps every trust-region ball into itself. For the weighted Euclidean norm \(\|s\|_M=(s^\top Ms)^{1/2}\), where \(M\succ0\), the \(M\)-orthogonal projector \(P=Z(Z^\top MZ)^{-1}Z^\top M\) satisfies this condition whenever \(Z\) has full column rank.
assumptions_latex: For the weighted formula, \(M\succ0\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s\|_{\mathcal N}\leq\Delta\Rightarrow\|Ps\|_{\mathcal N}\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring projection does not violate the trust-region radius.

notation.meaning: Norm induced by the positive-definite matrix M.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional problems large enough that dense storage or repeated dense factorization of the model Hessian is undesirable. Krylov, matrix-free, and preconditioned methods are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A large-scale trust-region solve produces \(p_j\) by restricting the quadratic model to a low-dimensional generated space \(\mathcal K_j\), typically \[\mathcal K_j(B,g)=\operatorname{span}\{g,Bg,\ldots,B^{j-1}g\},\] and approximately solving \[\min_{p\in\mathcal K_j,\ \|p\|\le\Delta}q(p).\] Its interface requires Hessian-vector products and vector operations, optionally applications of a positive-definite preconditioner, but not explicit dense formation or factorization of \(B\). Truncation may occur at a residual tolerance, the trust-region boundary, or detected nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large-scale trust-region solver works in successively generated low-dimensional spaces and accesses the Hessian through matrix-vector products. It returns an approximate step from a restricted trust-region problem and may use preconditioning. Boundary contact, negative curvature, or an accuracy test terminates the inner solve without dense factorization of the full Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(B=B^T\) defines a computable linear operator on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\).
The selected Krylov or reduced-space iteration has a stated truncation criterion.
Any preconditioner used is compatible with the trust-region norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output lies in a generated low-dimensional space, satisfies the trust-region constraint, and meets the solver’s stated model-decrease, curvature, or residual termination condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With an orthonormal basis \(Q_j\) of \(\mathcal K_j\), write \(p=Q_jy\) and solve the reduced problem with Hessian \(Q_j^TBQ_j\).
special_cases_latex: Truncated CG is the canonical short-recurrence member.
Lanczos methods explicitly maintain an orthogonal Krylov basis and a tridiagonal reduced Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage and principal operator cost can scale with the Krylov dimension rather than with a dense \(n\times n\) factorization.
boundary_notes: The definition does not imply that the full trust-region minimizer is obtained before truncation.

children.title: Truncated Conjugate-Gradient Trust-Region Method
children.top_down_role: Krylov subproblem family using truncation at curvature, boundary, or accuracy events.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\) subject to \(\|s\|_M\le\Delta\), where \(H=H^T\), \(M=M^T\succ0\), and \(\|s\|_M=(s^TMs)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional preconditioned CG applied to possibly nonconvex quadratic trust-region models. The definition allows truncation by curvature, boundary, or accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(s_0=0\), \(r_0=g\), \(v_0=M^{-1}r_0\), and \(d_0=-v_0\). While \(d_j^THd_j>0\), form \[\alpha_j=\frac{r_j^Tv_j}{d_j^THd_j},\qquad s_{j+1}=s_j+\alpha_jd_j.\] If \(d_j^THd_j\le0\), or if \(\|s_j+\alpha_jd_j\|_M\ge\Delta\), truncate to \(s_j+\sigma_jd_j\), where \(\sigma_j\ge0\) satisfies \(\|s_j+\sigma_jd_j\|_M=\Delta\), and stop. Otherwise update the preconditioned CG residual and direction, and stop when the prescribed accuracy condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated CG starts at the zero step and follows preconditioned conjugate-gradient directions. It terminates on the trust-region boundary if it detects nonpositive curvature or if the next ordinary CG iterate would leave the region. It may also terminate at an interior iterate when a residual or iteration accuracy condition is met.
assumptions_latex: Linear solves or operator applications defining \(M^{-1}r_j\) are available.
An interior accuracy termination rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step \(s_{\mathrm{TCG}}\) satisfies \(\|s_{\mathrm{TCG}}\|_M\le\Delta\); curvature or boundary truncation returns a point with \(\|s_{\mathrm{TCG}}\|_M=\Delta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(M=I\), the method is ordinary Euclidean truncated CG.
After the change of variables \(y=M^{1/2}s\), preconditioned truncated CG is ordinary truncated CG for the transformed model.
special_cases_latex: If \(H\succ0\) and the unconstrained minimizer is interior, exact-arithmetic CG may terminate at that minimizer.
If nonpositive curvature is detected in the first direction, the boundary point is the Cauchy step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Starting at zero makes the positive-curvature CG iterates increase in the \(M\)-norm, supporting immediate boundary truncation.
boundary_notes: The method need not identify the most negative curvature direction.
Residual-only stopping can be unreliable unless calibrated to the outer iteration.

notation.meaning: Boundary-intersection parameter on the current direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Steihaug-Toint Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run conjugate gradients from zero, stopping at convergence, at the first boundary crossing, or along a detected direction of nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(s)=g^\top s+\tfrac12s^\top Bs\) and \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\), initialize \(s_0=0\), \(r_0=g\), and \(p_0=-r_0\). At iteration \(j\), if \(p_j^\top Bp_j\leq0\), return the point \(s_j+\tau p_j\) on \(\|s_j+\tau p_j\|_2=\Delta\) that minimizes \(q\) along the feasible ray. Otherwise take the conjugate-gradient step \(\alpha_j=(r_j^\top r_j)/(p_j^\top Bp_j)\); truncate at the boundary if necessary. Set \(r_{j+1}=r_j+\alpha_jBp_j\), stop when the residual tolerance holds, and otherwise update the conjugate direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step is feasible and termination occurs at residual convergence, the trust-region boundary, or detected nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned truncated conjugate-gradient method for an indefinite Euclidean trust-region subproblem.

notation.meaning: Gradient of the quadratic model at the current CG iterate.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\), with \(H=H^T\), and impose \(\|s\|_M\le\Delta\) for \(M=M^T\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical preconditioned truncated-CG trust-region algorithm starting from the zero step, including its three defining termination outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Steihaug–Toint method is the truncated preconditioned-CG iteration initialized by \(s_0=0\), \(g_0=g\), \(v_0=M^{-1}g_0\), and \(p_0=-v_0\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\kappa_k=p_k^THp_k\). If \(\kappa_k\le0\), return the boundary point \(s_k+\sigma_kp_k\) minimizing the model along the feasible ray. If \(\kappa_k>0\), take the ordinary CG length \(\alpha_k=(g_k^Tv_k)/\kappa_k\); if it crosses the boundary, return \(s_k+\sigma_kp_k\) with \(\|s_k+\sigma_kp_k\|_M=\Delta\). Otherwise continue the CG recurrence until its accuracy test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Steihaug–Toint method is the canonical zero-start truncated-CG trust-region solver. It has three outcomes: an interior approximate solution, a boundary point reached because the ordinary CG path leaves the region, or a boundary point reached along a direction of nonpositive curvature.
assumptions_latex: The preconditioner used in CG is the same metric defining \(\|\cdot\|_M\).
A convergence test is specified for an interior return.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned Steihaug–Toint point \(s^{\mathrm{ST}}\) is feasible; boundary or nonpositive-curvature termination gives \(\|s^{\mathrm{ST}}\|_M=\Delta\), while interior termination satisfies the chosen CG accuracy test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(M=I\), this is the CG-Steihaug algorithm for the Euclidean trust-region subproblem.
special_cases_latex: The first generated point is the model’s Cauchy point.
For a positive-definite model with an interior minimizer and sufficiently strict tolerance, the method reduces to ordinary CG.
immediate_consequences_latex: Subsequent accepted CG iterates do not increase the model relative to the first Cauchy iterate.
The method requires Hessian-vector products rather than a factorization of \(H\).
boundary_notes: The first detected negative-curvature direction need not approximate the leftmost eigenvector.
Variants that retreat to the Cauchy point on negative curvature differ from the Steihaug boundary rule.

notation.meaning: Curvature of the quadratic along the current CG direction.
Positive parameter locating the trust-region boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Truncated CG
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply truncated CG with preconditioned residuals and an M-norm trust region, truncating on boundary crossing or nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\succ0\) and impose \(\|s\|_M=(s^\top Ms)^{1/2}\leq\Delta\). Initialize \(s_0=0\), \(r_0=g\), solve \(Mz_0=r_0\), and set \(p_0=-z_0\). While \(p_j^\top Bp_j>0\), use \(\alpha_j=(r_j^\top z_j)/(p_j^\top Bp_j)\); return the first intersection of \(s_j+\tau p_j\) with the boundary if the full step is infeasible. Otherwise update \(r_{j+1}=r_j+\alpha_jBp_j\), solve \(Mz_{j+1}=r_{j+1}\), and form the standard preconditioned conjugate direction. On nonpositive curvature, minimize along the feasible ray to the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step satisfies \(\|s\|_M\leq\Delta\) and respects the truncated-CG stopping rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned truncated CG in the metric induced by a positive-definite preconditioner.

notation.meaning: Symmetric positive-definite preconditioner and metric matrix.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2.6 Preconditioned Lanczos p. 102

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), where \(B=B^T\), and let \(D\) be nonsingular with \(M=D^TD\succ0\). The trust region is \(\|Dp\|_2=\|p\|_M\le\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional scaled Krylov trust-region solves. Preconditioning and the trust-region metric are required to be consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Preconditioned truncated CG is ordinary truncated CG applied after the variable transformation \(y=Dp\) to \[\min_{\|y\|_2\le\Delta}(D^{-T}g)^Ty+\tfrac12y^T(D^{-T}BD^{-1})y.\] Equivalently, in original variables it uses residual preconditioning \(z_j=M^{-1}r_j\), directions generated by the preconditioned CG recurrence, and truncates when \(d_j^TBd_j\le0\), when the next iterate reaches \(\|p\|_M=\Delta\), or when the prescribed accuracy test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned truncated CG rescales the quadratic so that its spectrum is more favorable, then applies the usual truncated-CG rules in the corresponding weighted norm. The same positive-definite matrix must define both the residual preconditioning and the trust-region geometry; otherwise the monotone-radius property used for truncation is not guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: A factorization \(M=D^TD\) or an operator for \(M^{-1}\) is available.
The preconditioner and trust-region norm use the same matrix \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step is feasible in the weighted norm, \(\|p\|_M\le\Delta\), and is obtained by curvature, boundary, or accuracy truncation of the preconditioned CG path.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The transformed Hessian is \(\widehat B=D^{-T}BD^{-1}\) and transformed gradient is \(\widehat g=D^{-T}g\).
Applying unpreconditioned truncated CG to \((\widehat B,\widehat g)\) is equivalent to the original-variable preconditioned recurrence.
special_cases_latex: \(M=I\) gives the unpreconditioned Steihaug–Toint method.
Incomplete Cholesky factors may define \(D\) for sparse models.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive-curvature iterates grow monotonically in \(\|\cdot\|_M\), so a boundary-crossing iterate need not be followed further.
boundary_notes: A preconditioner that is indefinite does not define the required norm.
Good preconditioning concerns spectral clustering; it does not change the exact transformed problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between a weighted trust-region subproblem and the standard Euclidean form, together with the stated sparse-factorization boundary for constructing a preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular scaling turns a weighted-norm trust-region quadratic into the standard Euclidean trust-region form. Standard Newton–CG in the transformed variables is therefore equivalent to preconditioned Newton–CG in the original variables, whose iterates grow monotonically in the weighted norm. Incomplete Cholesky can supply a sparse factor for a positive-definite matrix, but an indefinite Hessian requires an additional modification.

children.title: Projected Truncated CG
children.top_down_role: Projected and reduced-space Krylov variants for constrained settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Truncated CG
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run truncated CG in a feasible reduced space, then lift the feasible reduced step to the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning the admissible subspace. Apply truncated CG to the reduced model
\[\widehat q(u)=(Z^\top g)^\top u+\tfrac12u^\top(Z^\top BZ)u,
\qquad \|u\|_2\leq\Delta,\]
starting from \(u_0=0\). Terminate when the reduced residual meets tolerance; when a reduced direction has nonpositive curvature or its full CG step crosses the boundary, return the minimizing boundary point along that direction. Output \(s=Zu\). Equivalently, the iteration may use projected products \(PBPv\), where \(P=ZZ^\top\), without explicitly forming the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s=Zu\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}(Z)\), satisfies \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\), and obeys the reduced truncated-CG termination rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-space truncated CG for steps restricted to a linear feasible subspace.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the feasible subspace.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.4.1 Projected Preconditioned Conjugate Gradients p. 109

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, \(H=H^T\), \(M=M^T\succ0\), and consider \(\min g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\) subject to \(As=0\) and \(\|s\|_M\le\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linearly constrained or tangent-space trust-region subproblems. The iteration may be expressed in an explicit null-space basis or implicitly through projected preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projected truncated CG is truncated preconditioned CG restricted to \(\ker A\). With a basis \(N\) for \(\ker A\), it applies truncated CG to the reduced model with Hessian \(N^THN\), gradient \(N^Tg\), and steps \(s=Ny\). Implicitly, each preconditioned vector \(v_j\in\ker A\) is obtained from \[\begin{pmatrix}M&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}v_j\\w_j\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_j\\0\end{pmatrix}.\] The iteration truncates at nonpositive reduced curvature, the boundary \(\|s\|_M=\Delta\), or its accuracy test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected truncated CG performs the Krylov iteration entirely within a linear feasible or tangent subspace. It may explicitly reduce the problem with a null-space basis or implicitly project every preconditioned residual by solving an augmented system. Every generated step remains linearly feasible, and the ordinary truncated-CG curvature and boundary rules are applied in that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and the zero step is feasible.
The projected preconditioning systems are solved accurately enough to preserve \(Av_j=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step satisfies \(As=0\) and \(\|s\|_M\le\Delta\); boundary truncation gives equality in the norm constraint.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Explicit null-space CG and implicit projected CG solve the same reduced quadratic when projections and linear solves are exact.
special_cases_latex: With no linear constraints, \(A\) has zero rows and the method becomes preconditioned truncated CG.
For equality-constrained nonlinear optimization, \(A\) may be the current constraint Jacobian and \(\ker A\) the tangent space.
immediate_consequences_latex: All iterates and search directions remain in \(\ker A\).
Using the same \(M\) for preconditioning and the trust-region norm preserves monotonic growth in the weighted norm.
boundary_notes: Inexact augmented solves can destroy feasibility and CG conjugacy.
General inequalities require an active-set, interior, or projected-path mechanism beyond a fixed null space.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for the null space of the linear constraints.
Multiplier vector in the projected preconditioning system.

children.title: Lanczos Trust-Region Methods
children.top_down_role: Subproblem solver families based on orthogonal Krylov bases and reduced tridiagonal models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), with \(B=B^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\ne0\), and \(\Delta>0\). Let \(Q_j\) be the Lanczos basis generated from \(g/\|g\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale symmetric, possibly indefinite Euclidean trust-region models. Orthogonal Krylov bases and reduced tridiagonal models distinguish this family from short-recurrence truncation alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(j\) Lanczos steps, let \(Q_j^TQ_j=I\), \(\operatorname{range}(Q_j)=\mathcal K_j(B,g)\), and \(T_j=Q_j^TBQ_j\), where \(T_j\) is symmetric tridiagonal. A Lanczos trust-region step is \[p_j=Q_jy_j,\qquad y_j\in\arg\min_{\|y\|_2\le\Delta}\left(\|g\|_2e_1^Ty+\tfrac12y^TT_jy\right).\] The reduced subproblem may be solved nearly exactly by shifted tridiagonal factorization, and the Lanczos process is enlarged until a prescribed residual, model-decrease, or subspace-accuracy test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lanczos trust-region method builds an orthonormal basis for a Hessian-gradient Krylov space. In that basis the Hessian becomes tridiagonal, so the restricted trust-region problem is inexpensive to solve accurately. The reduced solution is lifted to the full space, and the basis may be expanded to capture additional negative curvature or improve the residual.
assumptions_latex: The implementation specifies treatment of Lanczos breakdown and its termination test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(p_j\in\mathcal K_j(B,g)\), \(\|p_j\|_2\le\Delta\), and globally minimizes the quadratic model over the current Krylov-space trust-region ball.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reduced Hessian relation is \(Q_j^TBQ_j=T_j\), so \(q(Q_jy)=\|g\|_2e_1^Ty+\tfrac12y^TT_jy\) up to the constant model term.
special_cases_latex: When the Krylov space reaches an invariant subspace containing a global solution, the lifted reduced solution solves the full subproblem.
For positive-definite models, Lanczos and CG generate the same Krylov spaces in exact arithmetic.
immediate_consequences_latex: Ritz values of \(T_j\) provide approximations to extreme eigenvalues and expose useful negative-curvature directions.
Only Hessian-vector products and basis storage are required for the full-space operation.
boundary_notes: Finite-precision loss of Lanczos orthogonality may require reorthogonalization.
A small Krylov space may miss curvature directions orthogonal to the starting gradient, including near-hard cases.

notation.meaning: Lanczos Krylov subspace generated by the Hessian and gradient.

children.title: Truncated Lanczos Method
children.top_down_role: Classical Lanczos reduction and truncation family for trust-region subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Lanczos Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a Lanczos Krylov basis, solve each small tridiagonal trust-region problem, and stop when the lifted step has sufficient accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Starting with \(v_1=g/\|g\|_2\) when \(g\neq0\), generate Lanczos bases \(V_k=[v_1,\ldots,v_k]\) and tridiagonal matrices \(T_k=V_k^\top BV_k\). At iteration \(k\), compute
\[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|y\|_2\leq\Delta}
\left(\|g\|_2e_1^\top y+\tfrac12y^\top T_ky\right),
\qquad s_k=V_ky_k.\]
Stop when the reduced optimality residual or prescribed model-accuracy test holds, when the Lanczos recurrence terminates, or when the iteration limit is reached; return the last \(s_k\). Only products of the form \(Bv\) are required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\in\mathcal K_k(B,g)\), \(\|s_k\|_2\leq\Delta\), and \(s_k\) globally minimizes the model over that Krylov-space ball.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lanczos reduction of a symmetric Euclidean trust-region quadratic model.

notation.meaning: Krylov space spanned by g through the first k powers of B.
Symmetric tridiagonal Lanczos projection of B.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 The Lanczos Method p. 91

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let \(\Delta>0\). Define \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\). Starting with \(q_1=g/\|g\|_2\) when \(g\ne0\), the Lanczos recurrence produces an orthonormal matrix \(Q_j=[q_1,\ldots,q_j]\) spanning \(\mathcal K_j(H,g)=\operatorname{span}\{g,Hg,\ldots,H^{j-1}g\}\) and a symmetric tridiagonal matrix \(T_j=Q_j^THQ_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, Euclidean-norm, symmetric quadratic trust-region subproblems; the Lanczos process is stopped before the full ambient dimension is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a chosen stopping index \(1\le j\le n\), a truncated Lanczos trust-region step is \[s_j=Q_jy_j,\qquad y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|y\|_2\le\Delta}\left\{\|g\|_2e_1^Ty+\tfrac12y^TT_jy\right\}.\] The method is truncated when \(j\) is selected by an inner accuracy, iteration, or resource rule rather than by completion of the full \(n\)-dimensional Lanczos reduction. The reduced problem is minimized globally, so indefiniteness of \(T_j\) is retained rather than discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The truncated Lanczos method builds only the first \(j\) vectors of the Krylov space generated by the symmetric curvature matrix \(H\) and gradient \(g\). It projects the quadratic trust-region problem into that space, globally minimizes the resulting tridiagonal trust-region problem, and lifts the reduced minimizer back as \(s_j=Q_jy_j\). Truncation refers to stopping the subspace expansion at a prescribed or adaptively chosen \(j<n\), not to replacing negative curvature by a positive-semidefinite approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathcal K_j(H,g),\ \|s\|_2\le\Delta}q(s).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(Q_j^TQ_j=I\), the reduced and full-space norms agree: \(\|Q_jy\|_2=\|y\|_2\).
The projected linear term is \(Q_j^Tg=\|g\|_2e_1\), so the displayed reduced objective equals \(q(Q_jy)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(j=n\) and the Lanczos basis spans \(\mathbb R^n\), the reduced problem is the original trust-region subproblem.
If \(T_j\succeq0\) and its unconstrained minimizer lies in the ball, \(y_j\) may be an interior reduced Newton step.
immediate_consequences_latex: A negative Ritz value of \(T_j\) remains available to the reduced global minimization.
Only products \(Hv\), vector operations, and a small tridiagonal trust-region solve are required.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes a rule that merely stops at the first detected negative-curvature direction without globally minimizing over the accumulated Krylov space.
When \(g=0\), a separate starting vector or eigenvalue-oriented Lanczos initialization is needed to reveal negative curvature.

notation.meaning: The order-\(j\) Krylov subspace generated by \(H\) and \(g\).

children.title: Trust-Region Newton-Lanczos Method
children.top_down_role: Newton trust-region methods using Lanczos-reduced curvature models.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Newton-Lanczos Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, build a symmetric quadratic model, approximately solve its radius-constrained subproblem by globally solving within expanding Lanczos spaces, accept the trial step when actual reduction sufficiently agrees with predicted reduction, and update the radius according to agreement and boundary activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable, choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(0<\Delta_0\leq\Delta_{\max}\), \(0\leq\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), \(0<\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}<1<\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}\), and \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^\top s+\tfrac12s^\top H_ks\), where \(H_k=H_k^\top\) is the exact Hessian or a symmetric model matrix. If \(\|g_k\|_2\leq\varepsilon\), stop. Otherwise use products \(H_kv\) to build a Lanczos space, solve the quadratic trust-region problem globally in the current Lanczos space, and expand that space until the prescribed reduced-residual tolerance is met, obtaining \(s_k\) with \(\|s_k\|_2\leq\Delta_k\) and \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Define
\[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) if \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise. Set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\Delta_k\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min\{\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}\}\) if \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\) and \(\|s_k\|_2=\Delta_k\); otherwise set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\Delta_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the iterates.
Every trial step used in the ratio has positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each trial step satisfies \(\|s_k\|_2\leq\Delta_k\); acceptance is determined by \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and the radius is updated by the declared agreement and boundary rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton trust-region iteration with Lanczos-reduced quadratic subproblems.

notation.meaning: Exact Hessian or symmetric model-curvature matrix at the current iterate.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115
5.2 The Lanczos Method p. 91

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. At outer iterate \(x_k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), and \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\). Let \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(Q_{k,j}\) be a Lanczos basis of \(\mathcal K_j(B_k,g_k)\) with \(T_{k,j}=Q_{k,j}^TB_kQ_{k,j}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale smooth unconstrained optimization with exact Hessian-vector actions and a Euclidean trust region; the inner Lanczos dimension may be truncated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region Newton-Lanczos iteration computes \[y_{k,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|y\|_2\le\Delta_k}\left\{\|g_k\|_2e_1^Ty+\tfrac12y^TT_{k,j}y\right\},\qquad s_k=Q_{k,j}y_{k,j},\] evaluates the agreement ratio \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)},\] and accepts or rejects \(s_k\) and updates \(\Delta_k\) by a trust-region rule based on \(\rho_k\). The Newton qualifier means that the curvature operator is the Hessian \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\); the Lanczos qualifier identifies the Krylov reduction used for the trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each nonlinear iteration, the trust-region Newton-Lanczos method forms no Hessian factorization. Instead it applies the current Hessian to Lanczos vectors, obtains a small symmetric tridiagonal projection, globally solves the projected trust-region problem, and lifts that solution to the original variables. The resulting trial step is assessed using the usual ratio of actual objective reduction to predicted quadratic-model reduction, after which the trust-region radius is updated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathcal K_j(\nabla^2f(x_k),\nabla f(x_k)),\ \|s\|_2\le\Delta_k}m_k(s).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inner method is Lanczos applied to \(B_ks=-g_k\), augmented by global minimization of the quadratic over the trust-region ball in the accumulated Krylov subspace.
The method accesses curvature through products \(v\mapsto\nabla^2f(x_k)v\) and does not require an explicitly stored Hessian.
special_cases_latex: With \(j=n\) and no Lanczos breakdown, the inner step solves the full Newton trust-region subproblem.
If \(B_k\succ0\) and the reduced Newton step is feasible, the reduced trust-region multiplier is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Indefinite Hessians can be handled because \(T_{k,j}\) may be indefinite.
The storage and factorization burden is shifted from an \(n\times n\) Hessian to Lanczos vectors and a \(j\times j\) tridiagonal matrix.
boundary_notes: A Newton-CG method that terminates immediately on negative curvature is not, by that fact alone, the Newton-Lanczos method defined here.
Finite-difference Hessian-vector products produce an inexact or Hessian-free variant and require separate error control.

notation.meaning: Ratio of actual to predicted reduction at outer iteration \(k\).
Lanczos basis constructed from the current Hessian and gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton–Lanczos reduced-space trust-region step and arbitrary-negative-curvature failure boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm statement for symmetric quadratic trust-region models in large-scale Newton methods, together with the motivating failure boundary showing that an arbitrary negative-curvature direction can give poor model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), where \(B_k\) is symmetric. An arbitrary negative-curvature direction need not provide a significant model reduction: for \(m(p)=10^{-3}p_1-10^{-4}p_1^2-p_2^2\) on \(\|p\|\le 1\), the steepest-descent direction from the origin followed to the boundary reduces the model by about \(10^{-3}\), whereas a boundary step along \(e_2\) reduces it by \(1\). After \(j\) Lanczos iterations, let \(Q_j\in\mathbb R^{n\times j}\) have orthonormal columns spanning the generated Krylov subspace and let \(T_j=Q_j^TB_kQ_j\) be tridiagonal. The reduced-space trust-region step is \(p_k=Q_jw_j\), where \[w_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|w\|\le\Delta_k}m_k(Q_jw)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|w\|\le\Delta_k}\left\{f_k+(Q_j^Tg_k)^Tw+\tfrac12w^TT_jw\right\}.\] Because \(T_j\) is tridiagonal, the reduced problem can be treated by nearly exact trust-region techniques using shifted factorizations of \(T_j+\lambda I\), while continued Lanczos iteration gathers information about indefinite curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Following an arbitrary negative-curvature direction can yield very little trust-region model improvement; the displayed example gives a reduction of about 0.001 along the steepest-descent boundary direction but a reduction of 1 along the second coordinate. Newton–Lanczos instead constructs an orthonormal Krylov basis, projects the symmetric model Hessian to a tridiagonal matrix, minimizes the quadratic trust-region model in that reduced subspace, and lifts the solution by p = Qw. Shifted factorizations of the tridiagonal matrix support a nearly exact reduced solve while retaining indefinite-curvature information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k=Q_jw_j,\qquad w_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|w\|\le\Delta_k}\left\{f_k+(Q_j^Tg_k)^Tw+\tfrac12w^TT_jw\right\}

children.top_down_role: Lanczos subproblem family retaining reduced-space global minimization capability.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Lanczos Trust-Region Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use an augmented Lanczos space, globally solve each reduced trust-region problem, and capture curvature directions that a gradient-only Krylov space may miss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a starting block whose span contains \(g\) and at least one auxiliary direction, and generate an orthonormal block-Lanczos basis \(V_k\) for the associated invariant Krylov space. Form \(T_k=V_k^\top BV_k\) and \(h_k=V_k^\top g\), solve
\[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|y\|_2\leq\Delta}
\left(h_k^\top y+\tfrac12y^\top T_ky\right),
\qquad s_k=V_ky_k,\]
and expand the basis until an accuracy test or invariant-subspace termination occurs. If \(\operatorname{range}(V_k)=\mathbb R^n\), the lifted step is a global solution of the original trust-region subproblem, including indefinite and hard cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\) globally minimizes the model over \(\operatorname{range}(V_k)\cap\{s:\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\}\), and is globally optimal in the full-space case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block or augmented Lanczos method retaining global reduced-subproblem minimization, including hard-case curvature.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-space minimization and full-space optimality statements are mathematically plausible, but the cited generic Lanczos section does not specifically identify the proposed block or augmented method, its starting-block requirements, or its claimed hard-case capability. A method-specific section, theorem, or paper is needed before the exact generalized variant can be reviewed reliably.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(M=M^T\succ0\), and \(\Delta>0\). Write \(\|s\|_M=(s^TMs)^{1/2}\) and \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\). Let \(\mathcal K_j\) be the nested preconditioned Krylov space generated by \(M^{-1}H\) and \(M^{-1}g\). Choose a basis \(Z_j\) satisfying \(Z_j^TMZ_j=I\), and set \(T_j=Z_j^THZ_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric, possibly indefinite quadratic models with an ellipsoidal trust region induced by a positive-definite preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generalized Lanczos trust-region step of order \(j\) is \[s_j=Z_jy_j,\qquad y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|y\|_2\le\Delta}\left\{(Z_j^Tg)^Ty+\tfrac12y^TT_jy\right\}.\] The method enlarges \(\mathcal K_j\) by the preconditioned Lanczos recurrence and, at selected dimensions, globally minimizes the reduced trust-region model. Thus it retains reduced-space global minimization, including reduced negative curvature and the reduced hard case, rather than selecting only a single conjugate-gradient path point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized Lanczos trust-region method is the preconditioned, variable-metric version of Lanczos trust-region minimization. An \(M\)-orthonormal basis represents a nested preconditioned Krylov space. At a chosen dimension, the method globally minimizes the quadratic over that entire space subject to the \(M\)-norm trust-region bound and maps the reduced minimizer back to the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathcal K_j,\ \|s\|_M\le\Delta}q(s).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(M=R^TR\), the change of variables \(u=Rs\) converts the problem to a Euclidean trust region with transformed Hessian \(R^{-T}HR^{-1}\).
The relation \(Z_j^TMZ_j=I\) gives \(\|Z_jy\|_M=\|y\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: For \(M=I\), the method reduces to the ordinary Lanczos trust-region reduction.
If the Krylov space reaches \(\mathbb R^n\), the lifted reduced minimizer is a global minimizer of the full trust-region subproblem.
immediate_consequences_latex: Each reduced problem is a small symmetric trust-region problem with tridiagonal projected curvature.
Preconditioning changes the geometry and Krylov space without requiring convexification of \(H\).
boundary_notes: The definition requires \(M\succ0\); an indefinite preconditioner does not define a norm or the displayed ball.
Lanczos breakdown can omit an eigenspace relevant to the full hard case; restarting with an additional vector is a nearby variant.

notation.meaning: An \(M\)-orthonormal basis for the preconditioned Krylov space.

children.title: Matrix-Free Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Curvature-action, preconditioner, inner-stopping, and workspace interfaces for large-scale solvers.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\mathbb R^n\) with inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\), let \(g\in V\), let \(A:V\to V\) be self-adjoint, and let \(\Delta>0\). A Krylov trust-region solver seeks a step for \(q(s)=\langle g,s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,As\rangle\) without receiving entries or a factorization of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional software-facing contract for deterministic matrix-free Krylov trust-region solvers; it specifies mathematical behavior, not a programming-language ABI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free solver interface is a tuple \[\mathfrak I=(\operatorname{apply}_A,\operatorname{apply}_{P^{-1}},\operatorname{stop},\mathcal W)\] where \(\operatorname{apply}_A(v)=Av\) for every requested \(v\in V\); \(P\succ0\) and \(\operatorname{apply}_{P^{-1}}(r)=P^{-1}r\), or this component is the identity; \(\operatorname{stop}\) is a predicate on observable inner state such as the residual, model decrease, boundary contact, curvature flag, iteration count, and action count; and \(\mathcal W\) stores only vectors, scalars, and reduced matrices generated by the iteration. The solver may depend on \(A\) only through calls to \(\operatorname{apply}_A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free solver interface supplies four coordinated capabilities: application of the curvature operator to arbitrary vectors, optional application of a positive-definite preconditioner inverse, a stopping policy based on observable Krylov quantities and resource limits, and workspace for vectors and small reduced matrices. The defining restriction is that the solver cannot inspect, assemble, or factor the full curvature matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A\text{ enters the Krylov solver only through }v\mapsto\operatorname{apply}_A(v)=Av.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The interface is matrix-free precisely when two self-adjoint operators agreeing on every queried vector are indistinguishable to the solver during that execution.
A Hessian-free specialization sets \(A=\nabla^2f(x)\) and implements \(\operatorname{apply}_A(v)\) without storing \(\nabla^2f(x)\).
special_cases_latex: With \(P=I\), no separate preconditioner callback is required.
A fixed maximum number of operator products is a valid component of \(\operatorname{stop}\), though it need not imply a prescribed residual accuracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: Krylov subspaces, Ritz values, residual norms, and projected trust-region models can be constructed from the interface.
Storage may scale with the retained Krylov dimension rather than with \(n^2\).
boundary_notes: The tuple is a formal synthesis of standard matrix-free solver requirements; the supplied sources discuss its components but do not present this exact tuple as a named canonical definition.
Approximate operator actions require an additional error contract not included here.

notation.meaning: The permitted vector and reduced-matrix workspace.

review_flags: No inspected source states the exact four-component interface tuple as a canonical mathematical definition; a source specific to solver-interface contracts is required.

children.title: Matrix-Free Operator Interface
children.top_down_role: Operator-access interfaces for matrix-free Krylov methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\mathbb R^n\), and let \(A:V\to V\) be the self-adjoint curvature operator used in a quadratic model. In a Newton specialization, \(A=\nabla^2f(x)\) at a fixed point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional matrix-free Krylov methods with exact linear operator actions; approximate finite-difference products are treated as a separate variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free operator interface for \(A\) is an oracle \[\operatorname{apply}_A:V\to V,\qquad \operatorname{apply}_A(v)=Av\quad\text{for every queried }v\in V,\] satisfying linearity and, for a symmetric Krylov method, self-adjointness \[\langle u,\operatorname{apply}_A(v)\rangle=\langle\operatorname{apply}_A(u),v\rangle\quad\text{for all }u,v\in V.\] The client is not supplied with matrix entries, a factorization, or unrestricted element access; all curvature information used by the iteration is obtained from returned products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free operator interface is a callable linear action that returns \(Av\) for each vector requested by the Krylov solver. For Lanczos, conjugate-gradient, and symmetric trust-region reductions, that action represents a self-adjoint operator. Matrix-free means that the algorithm obtains curvature only from these products and never requires the complete matrix or its factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{A\text{-information available to the solver}\}=\{(v,Av):v\text{ is queried}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(A=\nabla^2f(x)\), the oracle is a Hessian-vector product routine \(v\mapsto\nabla^2f(x)v\).
In exact arithmetic, repeated applications and vector operations generate \(\mathcal K_j(A,g)=\operatorname{span}\{g,Ag,\ldots,A^{j-1}g\}\).
special_cases_latex: Automatic differentiation may implement an exact Hessian-vector action to working precision.
The identity operator and sparse matrix multiplication are valid implementations even though the latter internally stores a matrix.
immediate_consequences_latex: A Lanczos tridiagonal projection can be generated without forming \(A\).
The interface separates the mathematical operator from its storage or evaluation mechanism.
boundary_notes: The forward-difference formula \((\nabla f(x+\epsilon v)-\nabla f(x))/\epsilon\) is generally an approximate, nonlinear-in-error action and is outside the exact oracle definition.
Self-adjointness is essential for the standard symmetric Lanczos recurrence.

notation.meaning: The oracle returning the action of \(A\) on a requested vector.

source_refs.locator: Section 7.1, discussion following the line-search Newton-CG method, p. 168: only Hessian-vector products are required; Section 8.2, formulas (8.19)–(8.20), pp. 195–196

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Vector Product Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface returns Hessian times a requested vector, enabling Krylov trust-region calculations without assembling or storing the Hessian matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a point \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), a Hessian-vector product interface exposes an operator \(\mathcal H_x:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[\mathcal H_x(v)=\nabla^2 f(x)v\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^n,\]
or \(\mathcal H_x(v)=Bv\) for a specified symmetric model matrix \(B\). A matrix-free trust-region solver may form residuals, Krylov bases, and projected curvature using calls to \(\mathcal H_x\) without storing \(B\). For a scalar twice-differentiable objective, the exact product is also the directional derivative \(\mathcal H_x(v)=D(\nabla f)(x)[v]\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(x\), or a symmetric model operator \(B\) is specified.
The interface is linear in \(v\) for fixed \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matrix-free solvers can obtain every required curvature product as \(\mathcal H_x(v)\) without explicit Hessian storage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free interface representing quadratic curvature through operator products.

notation.meaning: Hessian-vector or model-curvature operator at x.
Directional derivative of the gradient at x along v.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 The Lanczos Method p. 91

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian-Vector Product Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface applies a Jacobian and, when needed, its transpose to vectors, supporting matrix-free linearized constraints and Gauss-Newton curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a differentiable mapping \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) at \(x\), a Jacobian-vector interface supplies
\[\mathcal J_x(v)=J_c(x)v=Dc(x)[v],\qquad v\in\mathbb R^n.\]
When projected or normal-equation trust-region calculations require adjoint actions, the interface additionally supplies
\[\mathcal J_x^*(w)=J_c(x)^\top w,
\qquad w\in\mathbb R^m.\]
These two actions permit products such as \(J_c(x)^\top J_c(x)v=\mathcal J_x^*(\mathcal J_x(v))\), null-space residual calculations, and linearized constraint tests without explicitly assembling the Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: The adjoint is taken with respect to the Euclidean inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_c(x)^\top J_c(x)v=\mathcal J_x^*(\mathcal J_x(v))\) can be evaluated without forming \(J_c(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free interfaces for forward and adjoint actions of a constraint or residual Jacobian.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.4.1 Projected Preconditioned Conjugate Gradients p. 109

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Interface Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose interfaces that supply all products required by the solver, including adjoints or projections, while preserving the algebraic properties assumed by its Krylov recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select the smallest operator interface closed under every product required by the subproblem algorithm. A symmetric quadratic Krylov method requiring only \(Bv\) may use a Hessian-vector interface. A Gauss-Newton method requiring \(J^\top Jv\) must provide both \(v\mapsto Jv\) and \(w\mapsto J^\top w\). A projected method must additionally provide either a compatible projection \(P\), a feasible-space basis \(Z\), or the constraint operators needed to apply that projection. In every case, the implemented operator must preserve the declared dimensions, linearity, adjoint relation, and symmetry expected by the selected Krylov recurrence.
assumptions_latex: The trust-region solver's required operator products are specified.
Forward and adjoint spaces carry declared inner products.
Any solver-declared symmetry is mathematically valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected interface can evaluate every solver-required product while satisfying its dimension, adjoint, projection, and symmetry contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule matching matrix-free interfaces to the algebra required by a trust-region solver.

notation.meaning: Basis for a feasible or reduced subspace.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned residual and budget control for Krylov solves
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider an inner Krylov iteration for \(As=-g\) or a trust-region restriction of the associated quadratic. Let \(s_j\) be the current inner iterate, \(r_j=As_j+g\) its linear residual, \(P=P^T\succ0\) a preconditioner, and \(N_A(j)\) the number of curvature-operator actions used through iteration \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional inner iterations whose work is controlled jointly by conditioning, residual accuracy, trust-region events, and explicit resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Krylov effort-control interface is a pair \(\mathfrak E=(P^{-1},\mathsf S)\), where the preconditioner action \(r\mapsto P^{-1}r\) defines the monitored norm \(\|r\|_{P^{-1}}=(r^TP^{-1}r)^{1/2}\), and \(\mathsf S\) returns stop at the first index satisfying at least one declared condition, for example \[\|r_j\|_{P^{-1}}\le\eta\|r_0\|_{P^{-1}},\qquad N_A(j)\ge N_{\max},\qquad j\ge j_{\max},\] or a trust-region terminal event such as boundary contact, Lanczos breakdown, or attainment of the requested reduced-model accuracy. The parameters \(\eta\), \(N_{\max}\), and \(j_{\max}\) are inputs rather than implicit solver constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The effort-control interface combines a positive-definite preconditioner with explicit inner termination rules. The preconditioner changes the effective conditioning and supplies a residual norm. The stopping policy terminates on a requested residual tolerance, an operator-product or iteration budget, or a mathematically terminal trust-region event. Exposing these quantities lets an outer method trade inner accuracy against computational work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[j_{\mathrm{stop}}=\min\{j\ge0:\mathsf S(r_j,N_A(j),j,\text{events})=\mathrm{true}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A forcing sequence may replace the fixed tolerance by \(\eta=\eta_k\) at outer iteration \(k\).
If \(P=R^TR\), monitoring \(\|r_j\|_{P^{-1}}\) is equivalent to monitoring the Euclidean norm of \(R^{-T}r_j\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(P=I\) gives an unpreconditioned residual test.
Setting \(N_{\max}=j_{\max}=n\) permits, but does not require, a complete exact-arithmetic Krylov solve.
immediate_consequences_latex: The maximum number of expensive curvature actions is externally bounded.
Tighter residual tolerances generally increase inner work but can improve Newton-step accuracy.
boundary_notes: A residual tolerance alone does not certify global optimality of an indefinite trust-region subproblem.
The exact event set and tolerance scaling depend on the selected Krylov solver and outer convergence requirements.

notation.meaning: Number of curvature-operator actions consumed through inner iteration \(j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioning Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioner exposes inverse actions and an SPD inner product while leaving radius enforcement, boundary handling, and curvature detection to the trust-region solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the quadratic model \(m(s)=f+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), a preconditioning interface supplies an operator \(z=M^{-1}r\) without requiring either \(B\) or \(M\) to be formed. The operator \(M\) must be symmetric positive definite on the active Krylov space, thereby defining \(\langle u,v\rangle_M=u^{\mathsf T}Mv\) and \(\|u\|_M=(u^{\mathsf T}Mu)^{1/2}\). Each application accepts a residual \(r\), returns \(z\), and permits evaluation of \(r^{\mathsf T}z\). The trust-region solver remains responsible for enforcing \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\), detecting boundary intersection, and reacting to nonpositive curvature of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^{-1}r\) and \(r^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}r\) are well-defined for every Krylov residual \(r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface contract for SPD preconditioning of matrix-free Krylov trust-region subproblem solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Stopping Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface stops on a scaled residual or sufficient model decrease, and separately reports trust-region boundary or nonpositive-curvature termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(m(s)=f+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\), radius \(\Delta>0\), preconditioner \(M\succ0\), and inner iterate \(s_j\), an admissible inner-stopping interface may declare convergence only when \(\|s_j\|\leq\Delta\) and either \(\|g+Bs_j\|_{M^{-1}}\leq\eta_j\|g\|_{M^{-1}}\) or \(m(0)-m(s_j)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{cd}}\|g\|\min\{\|g\|/\|B\|,\Delta\}\). It must instead return a boundary or negative-curvature status when the Krylov recurrence first encounters \(\|s\|=\Delta\) or a direction \(d\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Bd\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step is feasible and is accompanied by a residual, sufficient-decrease, boundary, or negative-curvature status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-and-decrease stopping contract for an inexact Krylov trust-region solve.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The proposed disjunctive stopping rule is not reliably supported: attaining a Cauchy-decrease bound alone does not ordinarily constitute inner convergence, and the relationship between that condition and boundary or negative-curvature termination depends on the precise Krylov algorithm. The broad part-opening locator cannot confirm these choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner-Stopping Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral-equivalence constants determine how tightly a preconditioned residual must be controlled to achieve a prescribed Euclidean residual accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_j=g+Bs_j\), and suppose the preconditioner satisfies \(\alpha I\preceq M\preceq\beta I\) with \(0<\alpha\leq\beta<\infty\). Then \(\beta^{-1/2}\|r_j\|\leq\|r_j\|_{M^{-1}}\leq\alpha^{-1/2}\|r_j\|\). Consequently, the stopping test \(\|r_j\|_{M^{-1}}\leq\eta_j\|g\|_{M^{-1}}\) implies \(\|r_j\|\leq\eta_j\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}\,\|g\|\). Thus a Euclidean target \(\|r_j\|\leq\widehat\eta_j\|g\|\) is ensured by choosing \(\eta_j\leq\widehat\eta_j\sqrt{\alpha/\beta}\); deterioration of the spectral-equivalence ratio must tighten the preconditioned tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha I\preceq M\preceq\beta I\) for fixed positive \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_j\leq\widehat\eta_j\sqrt{\alpha/\beta}\) guarantees \(\|r_j\|\leq\widehat\eta_j\|g\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral equivalence converts preconditioned residual tolerances into Euclidean model-gradient tolerances.

children.title: Trust-Region Convergence and Complexity
children.top_down_role: Global convergence, local convergence, and worst-case complexity organized by criticality target and information regime.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Concise Complexity Analyses for Trust-Region Methods

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let an algorithm generate iterates \(x_k\), models \(m_k\), radii \(\Delta_k\), trial steps \(s_k\), and information \(\mathcal I_k\) while minimizing \(f\) on a specified problem class \(\mathcal F\). Let \(\chi_1(x)=\|
abla f(x)\|\) and, for twice differentiable unconstrained problems, \(\chi_2(x)=\max\{\|
abla f(x)\|,-\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A taxonomy of deterministic or explicitly specified stochastic trust-region analyses; each result must state its problem class, criticality target, information regime, and counted resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Trust-region convergence-complexity theory is the collection of quantified statements indexed by a descriptor \[\mathfrak C=(\mathcal F,\chi,\mathcal I,\mathcal G,\mathcal R),\] where \(\chi\) is the target criticality measure, \(\mathcal I\) specifies exact, inexact, conditional, or random model information, \(\mathcal G\) states whether the claim is global, local, subsequential, full-sequence, almost sure, or in expectation, and \(\mathcal R\) identifies the counted resource. A complexity statement has the form \[N_{\mathcal R}(\epsilon)=\inf\{N:\min_{0\le k\le N}\chi(x_k)\le\epsilon\}\le\Psi(\epsilon),\] while a convergence statement specifies a limit or limit-point property of \(\chi(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region convergence-complexity theory is not one convergence assertion. It is a structured family of assertions classified by the problem class, criticality measure, information quality, convergence mode, and resource being counted. Global and local convergence, first- and second-order targets, exact and imperfect models, and worst-case evaluation or iteration bounds therefore occupy distinct descriptors and must not be conflated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak C=(\mathcal F,\chi,\mathcal I,\mathcal G,\mathcal R)\quad\text{is the defining classification object.}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: First-order global convergence may be encoded by \(\mathcal G:\lim_k\chi_1(x_k)=0\).
Second-order evaluation complexity may use \(\chi=(\chi_1,-\lambda_{\min})\) and count objective, gradient, Hessian, or Hessian-vector evaluations separately.
special_cases_latex: A result with \(\liminf_k\chi_1(x_k)=0\) is subsequential rather than full-sequence convergence.
A local rate statement conditions on entry into a neighborhood of a specified solution and is distinct from global convergence.
