children.title: Imperfect-Evaluation Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity and attainable-accuracy families under controlled errors or intrinsic noise.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: The Impact of Noise on Evaluation Complexity: The Deterministic Trust-Region Case

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let available values satisfy \(\widetilde f_k=f(x_k)+e_k^f\), \(\widetilde g_k=\nabla f(x_k)+e_k^g\), and, when used, \(\widetilde H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)+E_k^H\). Let \(\Delta_k\) be the trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic controlled errors and irreducible bounded-noise floors; stochastic sampling costs require an additional probabilistic specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An imperfect-evaluation complexity regime is specified by error envelopes \[|e_k^f|\leq\delta_k^f,
0\qquad \|e_k^g\|\leq\delta_k^g,
0\qquad \|E_k^H\|\leq\delta_k^H\] and by a cost function for obtaining those envelopes. The regime is dynamically accurate of order \((2,1,0)\) when \(\delta_k^f=O(\Delta_k^2)\), \(\delta_k^g=O(\Delta_k)\), and \(\delta_k^H=O(1)\); stronger second-order regimes may require correspondingly tighter envelopes. It is an intrinsic-noise regime when fixed floors \((\bar\delta_f,ar\delta_g,ar\delta_H)\) prevent arbitrary tightening. A complexity statement must then specify both a bound \(N(\epsilon;\delta)
0\) and an attainable tolerance region, since requests below the induced criticality floor need not be achievable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An imperfect-evaluation complexity regime records bounds on errors in function, gradient, and Hessian information and the work required to achieve those bounds. Dynamically accurate regimes tighten errors relative to the current trust-region radius. Intrinsic-noise regimes have nonzero error floors. Their complexity statements must state not only the amount of work but also which stationarity tolerances remain attainable; a nominal bound below the noise-induced criticality floor is not meaningful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(\epsilon;\delta)<\infty\quad\text{is asserted only for }\epsilon\text{ in the declared attainable region determined by }(\delta_k^f,\delta_k^g,\delta_k^H).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A deterministic error envelope may be replaced by a high-probability or conditional-moment envelope, but the resulting complexity notion must state its probability mode.
special_cases_latex: Exact evaluation is the zero-envelope case.
Fixed bounded gradient error generally yields only convergence to a neighborhood measured at the scale of that error.
Adaptive sampling is represented by decreasing envelopes with an evaluation cost that increases as accuracy tightens.
immediate_consequences_latex: Evaluation accuracy and evaluation cost cannot be separated in a meaningful oracle-complexity comparison.
An algorithm may have finite complexity to a noise-dependent neighborhood but infinite complexity for smaller requested tolerances.
boundary_notes: The radius scalings given here define an information regime, not a universal convergence theorem.
No inspected source established the complete complexity-and-noise-floor interface.
review_flags: An authoritative source is required for exact attainable-accuracy and complexity bounds under each error model.
knowledge_statements.title: Complexity regimes under inexact evaluations
Inexact Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius-scaled deterministic errors preserve the usual first-order trust-region order of at most a constant times inverse accuracy squared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the computed values satisfy \( |\widetilde f_k-f(x_k)|\leq \kappa_f\Delta_k^2\) and \(\|\widetilde g_k-\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq \kappa_g\Delta_k\). Suppose \(f\) is bounded below with Lipschitz gradient, model Hessians are uniformly bounded, accepted steps achieve a fixed fraction of Cauchy decrease, and each iteration uses at most \(q\) inexact oracle calls. Then a standard trust-region method reaches an iterate with \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\) in at most \(C\varepsilon^{-2}\) iterations and at most \(qC\varepsilon^{-2}\) inexact oracle calls, where \(C\) is independent of \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is bounded below and has Lipschitz-continuous gradient.
The trust-region steps satisfy uniform Cauchy decrease and use at most \(q\) oracle calls per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{iter}}(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) and \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon)=O(q\varepsilon^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order trust-region complexity when evaluation errors are coupled to the current radius.

notation.meaning: number of inexact oracle calls before first-order accuracy epsilon

review_flags: Exact inexact-oracle complexity theorem and constants require an authoritative source.
Complexity counts oracle calls but not the internal cost of producing prescribed accuracy.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the terminal container, and the stated radius-scaled error orders are plausible. However, no citation is supplied, and the listed assumptions do not identify a precise inexact trust-region algorithm or theorem sufficient to establish the claimed iteration and oracle-call bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging noisy values to radius-squared accuracy can raise first-order complexity from inverse-square iterations to inverse-sixth function samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume each sampled function value is unbiased with conditionally sub-Gaussian noise of variance proxy \(\sigma^2\). To make a sample mean accurate to \(O(\Delta_k^2)\) with failure probability at most \(\delta_k\), it suffices to use \(m_k=O(\sigma^2\Delta_k^{-4}\log(1/\delta_k))\) samples. If the resulting probabilistically accurate trust-region method requires \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) iterations and relevant radii satisfy \(\Delta_k\geq c\varepsilon\) before termination, then its total function-sample complexity is \(O(\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1/\delta))\), up to algorithm-dependent constants and allocation of total failure probability \(\delta\).
assumptions_latex: Function noise is conditionally unbiased and sub-Gaussian with variance proxy \(\sigma^2\).
Sample means are allocated failure probabilities \(\delta_k\) with \(\sum_k\delta_k\leq\delta\).
Before termination, the analyzed trust-region radii obey \(\Delta_k\geq c\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{samples}}(\varepsilon,\delta)=O(\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1/\delta))\) under the stated representative regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative sample complexity for unbiased sub-Gaussian function noise controlled by adaptive averaging.

notation.meaning: number of noisy samples averaged at iteration k
overall allowed probability of inaccurate sampling events

review_flags: The bound is regime-specific rather than a universal noisy trust-region rate.
An authoritative stochastic trust-region complexity theorem is required.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the noisy-evaluation container, but the inverse-sixth sample bound is regime-specific and has no cited theorem. In particular, the stated logarithmic dependence does not transparently account for allocating failure probabilities across up to order inverse-square iterations, so an authoritative result or a more precise derivation framework is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainable Accuracy Floors
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed function and gradient errors impose a stationarity floor proportional to the larger of square-root function error and gradient error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose evaluations obey \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\leq\omega_f\) and \(\|\widetilde g(x)-\nabla f(x)\|\leq\omega_g\), with nonzero error levels independent of the trust-region radius. Fully linear adequacy at radius \(\Delta\) requires function error of order \(\Delta^2\) and gradient error of order \(\Delta\). Consequently, uniform adequacy cannot generally be guaranteed below \(\Delta_{\min}=c\max\{\sqrt{\omega_f},\omega_g\}\), where \(c>0\) depends on adequacy constants. A first-order method whose criticality scale is comparable to \(\Delta\) therefore cannot certify arbitrary accuracy below order \(\max\{\sqrt{\omega_f},\omega_g\}\) without reducing the evaluation errors.
assumptions_latex: Model adequacy requires function accuracy \(O(\Delta^2)\) and gradient accuracy \(O(\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{\min}=\Omega(\max\{\sqrt{\omega_f},\omega_g\})\) for certification based only on these evaluations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order accuracy obstruction created by nonvanishing absolute function and gradient errors.

notation.meaning: smallest radius at which adequacy can be guaranteed

review_flags: The scaling follows the fully linear error requirements, but a direct authoritative locator is absent.
The constant and precise certification floor depend on the algorithm and stationarity measure.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind correctly matches the accuracy-floor container, and the displayed scaling is plausible from fully linear error requirements. A source is nevertheless required because the conversion from a minimum reliable radius to a stationarity-certification floor depends on the algorithm, adequacy constants, and criticality measure.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Dependent Complexity Degradation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Errors decaying too slowly with radius create a minimum reliable radius and degrade or terminate the usual complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let function and gradient evaluation errors satisfy \(e_k^f\leq\omega_f\Delta_k^p\) and \(e_k^g\leq\omega_g\Delta_k^q\). Fully linear trust-region analysis requires \(e_k^f=O(\Delta_k^2)\) and \(e_k^g=O(\Delta_k)\). Thus \(p\geq2\) and \(q\geq1\) preserve these asymptotic orders. If \(p<2\), adequacy can fail below a radius of order \(\omega_f^{1/(2-p)}\); if \(q<1\), it can fail below a radius of order \(\omega_g^{1/(1-q)}\). Any complexity guarantee below the corresponding stationarity scale must therefore incorporate error reduction or an error-dependent degradation term.
assumptions_latex: The exact-evaluation analysis relies on fully linear function and gradient error orders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complexity-preserving thresholds are \(p\geq2\) and \(q\geq1\); smaller exponents induce positive reliability floors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radius-decay thresholds separating complexity preservation from error-induced stagnation.

notation.meaning: error-decay exponents relative to the radius

review_flags: A source is needed for a formal algorithm-specific degradation theorem.
Displayed floors suppress adequacy constants and describe scaling only.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container. The exponent thresholds and radius-floor scalings are plausible comparisons with fully linear accuracy orders, but no source supports the claimed consequences for complexity, and the conclusion is not tied to a specific trust-region method or degradation theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interface between model fidelity and complexity accounting
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m_k\) model \(f\) on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\). Let \(C_k\) denote the information cost of constructing or certifying \(m_k\), and let \(T_\epsilon\) be a criticality stopping time.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic fully linear and fully quadratic models, plus conditional probabilistic variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A model-information complexity interface is a pair \((\mathcal M,\mathcal C)\) consisting of a model-fidelity class and a cost rule. The fully linear class satisfies \[|f(y)-m_k(y)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,
0\qquad \|\nabla f(y)-\nabla m_k(y)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\quad(\forall y\in B(x_k,\Delta_k)).\] A fully quadratic class additionally controls function, gradient, and Hessian errors at orders \(\Delta_k^3\), \(\Delta_k^2\), and \(\Delta_k\), respectively. A probabilistic interface requires the relevant fidelity event to hold with a declared conditional probability. Its information complexity through tolerance \(\epsilon\) is \[I_\epsilon:=\sum_{k=0}^{T_\epsilon}C_k,\] and a valid complexity claim must state whether its bound is deterministic, expected, or high probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model-information interface couples a precise model-fidelity class with the cost of obtaining or certifying a model in that class. Fully linear models have second-order function error and first-order gradient error in the radius. Fully quadratic models have cubic function error, quadratic gradient error, and linear Hessian error. Probabilistic versions impose these properties conditionally with a stated success probability. Total information complexity is the cumulative model cost up to the criticality stopping time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I_\epsilon=\sum_{k=0}^{T_\epsilon}C_k\quad\text{with each }m_k\text{ classified by explicit radius-scaled fidelity conditions}.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(C_k\leq C\) uniformly, then \(I_\epsilon\leq C(T_\epsilon+1)\), so information and iteration complexity have the same order.
A probabilistic fidelity condition can be written \(\mathbb P(I_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\).
special_cases_latex: Derivative-based Taylor models may obtain fidelity from smoothness assumptions.
Derivative-free interpolation models charge sample evaluations to \(C_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Iteration bounds alone may conceal increasing model-construction costs.
Comparisons between exact and probabilistic models require a common information-cost unit.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how models are built.
The supplied sources did not provide a single exact locator for this combined interface.

notation.meaning: Information cost of the kth model.
Cumulative information cost to the requested tolerance.

review_flags: Sources are required for the exact fully linear, fully quadratic, and probabilistic complexity interfaces.

Derivative-Free Model Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine and full quadratic derivative-free interpolation models require linearly and quadratically many poised function values, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A determined affine interpolation model in \(n\) variables has \(n+1\) coefficients and can be constructed from \(n+1\) suitably poised function values. A determined quadratic model has \((n+1)(n+2)/2\) coefficients and requires that many suitably poised values. Hence rebuilding such models from scratch costs \(\Theta(n)\) and \(\Theta(n^2)\) function evaluations, respectively. If an interpolation set is updated by replacing one point while preserving poisedness, a subsequent model update may require only one new function evaluation, although maintaining geometry can require additional evaluations.
assumptions_latex: The interpolation set is poised for the selected polynomial space.
Only zeroth-order function evaluations are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{affine}}=n+1=\Theta(n)\) and \(N_{\mathrm{quadratic}}=(n+1)(n+2)/2=\Theta(n^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation counts for constructing determined polynomial interpolation models in dimension \(n\).

notation.meaning: values needed for determined affine interpolation
values needed for determined quadratic interpolation

review_flags: Standard dimension count, but no derivative-free interpolation source locator was supplied.
The update cost is conditional on preserving interpolation geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistically Accurate Model Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly more-likely-than-not accurate random models retain inverse-square expected first-order iteration complexity, with a probability-dependent constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) contain the algorithmic history before model \(m_k\) is generated, and let \(I_k\) denote the event that \(m_k\) is fully linear on the current trust region. Suppose \(\Pr(I_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\alpha\) almost surely for a fixed \(\alpha>1/2\), while successful accurate iterations provide standard Cauchy decrease and objective values are sufficiently accurate. Under the usual bounded-below and smoothness assumptions, the expected number of iterations before \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is at most \(C_\alpha\varepsilon^{-2}\), where \(C_\alpha\) is independent of \(\varepsilon\) and deteriorates as \(\alpha\downarrow1/2\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below and has Lipschitz-continuous gradient.
Accurate accepted models yield uniform Cauchy decrease and reliable acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[N_\varepsilon]\leq C_\alpha\varepsilon^{-2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected first-order complexity when model accuracy holds with uniformly positive conditional probability.

notation.meaning: event that the random model is fully linear at iteration k
history sigma-field before constructing the kth model
first iteration attaining gradient norm at most epsilon

review_flags: Probability thresholds and constants vary across stochastic trust-region frameworks.
A specific probabilistic-model complexity theorem must be sourced.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the container, but the threshold alpha greater than one half and the expected inverse-square conclusion depend on a particular stochastic trust-region framework. Terms such as sufficiently accurate objective values and reliable acceptance tests do not supply theorem-level hypotheses, and no authoritative theorem is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Linear Model Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully linear model approximates function values to radius squared and gradients to radius throughout the trust-region ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. The model \(m\) is fully linear for \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\) if constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\), independent of \(x\) and \(\Delta\) within the analyzed regime, satisfy \[|f(x+s)-m(s)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta^2,\qquad \|\nabla f(x+s)-\nabla m(s)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta\] for every \(s\) with \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\). An additive shift of \(m\) may be used so that its argument is the step \(s\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are continuously differentiable on the relevant ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\), value error is at most \(\kappa_f\Delta^2\) and gradient error at most \(\kappa_g\Delta\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Taxonomy of trust-region extensions, implementations, and failures
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: A basic trust-region architecture forms a model \(m_k\), computes \(s_k\in\{s:\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}\), evaluates an agreement ratio, accepts or rejects the trial point, and updates \(\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A navigation taxonomy, formalized through invariant algorithmic components rather than a convergence assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the trust-region architectural signature of a method as \[\mathcal A=(\mathcal X,F,\mathcal M,\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal U),\] where \(\mathcal X\) is the state space, \(F\) the objective or merit object, \(\mathcal M\) the model class, \(\mathcal R\) the radius-constrained admissible set, \(\mathcal S\) the step rule, and \(\mathcal U\) the acceptance-radius update. An extension changes \(\mathcal X\), \(F\), \(\mathcal M\), or \(\mathcal R\) while retaining an explicit model-agreement and radius-update architecture. An implementation variant changes the realization or approximation of \(\mathcal S\) or \(\mathcal U\) without changing the mathematical problem class. A failure regime is a set of states on which a required invariant—model adequacy, sufficient decrease, feasibility restoration, reliable agreement, or radius recovery—fails, so that the assumptions of the associated convergence statement are not satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy represents a trust-region method by its state space, objective or merit object, model, radius-constrained admissible region, step rule, and update rule. An extension changes the modeled problem or geometry while preserving the trust-region architecture. An implementation variant changes how a mathematical step or update is realized. A failure regime is a set of states where a required invariant such as model adequacy, sufficient decrease, feasibility progress, reliable agreement, or radius recovery does not hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{extension}\iff\mathcal A\text{ retains model agreement and radius control while changing the modeled domain, objective, model, or geometry}.
special_cases_latex: Composite, constrained, and infinite-dimensional methods are extension classes when they preserve the architectural signature.
Iterative subproblem solvers and preconditioners are implementation variants when they leave the mathematical step requirements unchanged.
immediate_consequences_latex: A computational symptom is not automatically a mathematical failure regime.
A method may belong to several extension classes but should be assigned one implementation description per concrete realization.
boundary_notes: The categories are interfaces and may overlap unless a finer navigation rule is imposed.
No inspected source defined this complete three-way taxonomy.
review_flags: The node is a synthesized taxonomy and lacks a source defining the exact formal partition.

children.title: Classical Trust-Region Extensions

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z_k\) be an algorithmic state, let \(m_k(s)\) be a local model, let \(\mathcal R_k(\Delta_k)\) be a radius-controlled admissible set, and let \(\operatorname{ared}_k\) and \(\operatorname{pred}_k\) denote actual and predicted improvement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensions of the basic smooth finite-dimensional unconstrained method that preserve its model-agreement-radius architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method is a classical trust-region extension when each iteration has the structural form \[s_k\in\mathcal R_k(\Delta_k),\qquad \operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0,\] \[\rho_k=\frac{\operatorname{ared}_k}{\operatorname{pred}_k},\qquad z_{k+1}\in\{z_k,z_k\oplus s_k\},\qquad \Delta_{k+1}=U(\Delta_k,\rho_k,s_k),\] while at least one of the state space, objective or merit function, local model, constraint geometry, or norm differs from the basic unconstrained smooth Euclidean formulation. Membership additionally requires a declared model-adequacy condition and a sufficient-decrease condition appropriate to the extension. Merely using a bounded step without an agreement test and radius update does not place a method in this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A classical trust-region extension preserves the basic cycle of radius-constrained model minimization, predicted and actual improvement comparison, step acceptance, and radius update, while changing the state space, merit function, model, constraints, or trust-region geometry. It must also state model-adequacy and sufficient-decrease conditions appropriate to the altered problem. A generic bounded-step method is not a trust-region extension unless it retains this architecture.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_k\in\mathcal R_k(\Delta_k),\quad \rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k,\quad (z_{k+1},\Delta_{k+1})\text{ are determined by an acceptance-radius rule}.
special_cases_latex: Ellipsoidal norms, constrained composite steps, and function-space trust regions fit the structural definition when their model and acceptance conditions are explicit.
A change only to the subproblem linear algebra is an implementation variant rather than a mathematical extension.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convergence claims for the basic method do not automatically transfer to an extension.
The acceptance ratio must compare improvement in mutually consistent merit and model quantities.
boundary_notes: Restoration phases and filters may require additional state beyond the displayed signature.
The inspected monograph sections support individual extensions but not this exact umbrella definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region model interface for composite objectives
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable and let \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Define the composite objective \(\Psi(x)=h(F(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite optimization; convexity of the outer function may be imposed by particular convergence theories but is not built into the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), a composite trust-region model interface consists of a model \(F_k(s)\) for \(F(x_k+s)\), the composite model \[M_k(s)=h(F_k(s)),\] and the subproblem \[\min_{\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k}M_k(s).\] For the first-order linearized interface, \(F_k(s)=F(x_k)+F'(x_k)s\). Given a computed step with positive predicted reduction \(M_k(0)-M_k(s_k)>0\), acceptance is governed by \[\rho_k=\frac{\Psi(x_k)-\Psi(x_k+s_k)}{M_k(0)-M_k(s_k)}.\] The interface is model-consistent on the current trust region when an explicitly declared error bound controls \(|\Psi(x_k+s)-M_k(s)|\) for all \(\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\), at the radius order required by the associated convergence result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite trust-region interface models an objective formed by applying an outer function h to a smooth mapping F. It first models F near the current point and then composes that model with h. The trial step approximately minimizes the composite model inside the radius. Acceptance compares the actual reduction in the composite objective with the predicted reduction in the composite model. A convergence theory must additionally state a uniform radius-scaled model-consistency bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_k(s)=h(F_k(s)),\qquad s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k}M_k(s)\ \text{approximately},\qquad \rho_k=\frac{\Psi(x_k)-\Psi(x_k+s_k)}{M_k(0)-M_k(s_k)}.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(h(u)=u\) and \(m=1\), the interface reduces to an ordinary smooth trust-region model.
An extended-valued \(h\) can encode constraints through its effective domain.
special_cases_latex: For \(h(u)=\|u\|_2^2/2\), the interface includes nonlinear least-squares trust-region models.
For \(h(u,v)=u+v\) with a nonsmooth modeled component, it represents a smooth-plus-nonsmooth composite objective when the component model is explicitly defined.
immediate_consequences_latex: Actual and predicted reductions are measured in the same composite objective scale.
The outer function can transmit nonsmoothness even when \(F\) is smooth.
boundary_notes: Exact solution of the generally nonsmooth subproblem is not part of the definition.
The supplied composite-step SQP source concerns constrained normal-tangential steps and does not directly support this composite-objective interface.

notation.meaning: Effective domain where the extended-valued outer function is finite.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-region model interface for composite objectives
Composite Objective Classes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite objective combines a smooth inner mapping, a convex outer loss, and an optional proper convex nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A composite objective on \(\mathbb R^n\) has the form \[F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x),\] where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable, \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is convex and locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(c(\operatorname{dom}g)\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. The feasible domain is \(\operatorname{dom}F=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}g:c(x)\in\operatorname{dom}h\}\). This class includes smooth objectives, nonlinear least squares, exact-penalty formulations, and smooth-plus-convex-nonsmooth problems.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is convex and locally Lipschitz on the relevant image.
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=h\circ c+g\) is defined on \(\{x\in\operatorname{dom}g:c(x)\in\operatorname{dom}h\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite objectives combining a smooth mapping with convex outer and nonsmooth terms.
review_flags: Several broader nonconvex composite classes exist; this record selects the convex-outer interface.
No supplied locator directly supports this composite class.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the objective-class container, and the record clearly selects a finite-dimensional convex-outer composite subclass. Because broader composite conventions exist and no cited definition supports this exact choice or the listed examples, a source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composite model linearizes the smooth inner map while retaining the outer and nonsmooth terms, optionally adding controlled quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\), the first-order composite trust-region model at \(x_k\) is \[M_k(s)=h\bigl(c(x_k)+J_k s\bigr)+g(x_k+s),\qquad \|s\|\leq\Delta_k,\] where \(J_k\) models \(\nabla c(x_k)\). A step \(s_k\) approximately minimizes \(M_k\) over the ball, and its predicted reduction is \(M_k(0)-M_k(s_k)\). When curvature information is included, a quadratic term \(\tfrac12s^TB_ks\) may be added, provided it is controlled so that the model remains a valid local approximation and the subproblem remains meaningfully solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k(s)=h(c(x_k)+J_ks)+g(x_k+s)\) supplies the trust-region predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prox-linear trust-region model obtained by linearizing the smooth inner mapping.

notation.meaning: exact or approximate Jacobian of the inner mapping

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports prox-linear composite trust-region models.
Conditions for adding an indefinite quadratic term depend on the chosen framework.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the composite-model container, and the prox-linear model formula is coherent. No source supports the representation, while the optional quadratic term is described without precise curvature, convexity, or solvability conditions; these framework-dependent details require an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Objective Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobian accuracy and smoothness of the inner map make the composite model agree with the objective to second order in radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\) and \(M_x(s)=h(c(x)+Js)+g(x+s)\). The model is first-order compatible with \(F\) on \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\) if \(J\) approximates \(
abla c(x)\) so that \(\|(J-
abla c(x))s\|\leq\kappa_J\Delta^2\), and if \(
abla c\) is Lipschitz near the ball. When \(h\) is Lipschitz there with constant \(L_h\), these conditions imply \[|F(x+s)-M_x(s)|\leq L_h igl(	frac12L_c+\kappa_J igr)\Delta^2\] for every feasible \(s\) satisfying \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\).
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L_h\) on the relevant image.
\(\nabla c\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L_c\) near the trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|F(x+s)-M_x(s)|\leq L_h(\tfrac12L_c+\kappa_J)\Delta^2\) for every feasible \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order consistency between a composite objective and its local trust-region model.

notation.meaning: model Jacobian for the inner mapping

review_flags: The compatibility estimate is standard but lacks a direct supplied source.
Feasibility ensures both objective and model values are finite.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the compatibility leaf, and the stated estimate follows the expected Lipschitz-composition scaling when all relevant values are finite. A cited source is still necessary to establish the exact compatibility definition, image neighborhood, feasibility requirements, and uniformity of its constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Convergence Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible composite models and sufficient predicted decrease yield termination or subsequential approach to composite first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the composite criticality measure \[\chi(x)=F(x)-\inf_{\|s\|\leq1}\{h(c(x)+
abla c(x)s)+g(x+s)\}.\] Suppose \(F=h\circ c+g\) is bounded below on the initial level set, \(
abla c\) is Lipschitz there, and the trust-region models are first-order compatible with \(F\). If each computed step attains a uniform fraction of model criticality decrease, acceptance uses actual-to-predicted reduction, and unsuccessful iterations contract the radius, then either the method terminates at \(x_k\) with \(\chi(x_k)=0\), or \(\liminf_{k	o\infty}\chi(x_k)=0\). For convex \(h\) and \(g\), \(\chi(x)=0\) implies \(0\in
abla c(x)^T\partial h(c(x))+\partial g(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is bounded below on the relevant level set and \(\nabla c\) is Lipschitz there.
Models have uniform first-order compatibility and steps provide a fixed fraction of criticality decrease.
The acceptance and radius-update rules satisfy standard trust-region safeguards.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either finite termination occurs with \(\chi(x_k)=0\), or \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global subsequential stationarity interface for a compatible composite trust-region scheme.
review_flags: A precise composite trust-region convergence theorem and its technical safeguards require an authoritative source.
The stationarity implication requires appropriate convex subdifferential chain and sum rules.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is appropriate for the convergence-interface leaf, but phrases such as standard trust-region safeguards and uniform fraction of model criticality decrease are not precise theorem hypotheses. The convergence alternative and the subdifferential stationarity implication require a specific authoritative theorem and applicable chain- and sum-rule qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Dimensional Trust-Region Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly accurate models, sufficient Cauchy decrease, and ratio-based radius updates extend trust-region stationarity guarantees to Hilbert spaces, with dual-norm criticality in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously Fréchet differentiable and bounded below on the initial level set, and let \(m_k:H\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\), \(m_k'(0)=f'(x_k)\), and a uniform quadratic model-error bound on \(\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\}\). If each computed step produces a fixed fraction of Cauchy decrease and the radius is updated by the usual actual-to-predicted reduction ratio, then every accumulation point \(x_*\) of the accepted iterates is stationary: \(f'(x_*)=0\). In a Banach space, the stationarity measure is the dual norm \(\|f'(x_k)\|_{H^*}\), and an analogous conclusion requires a suitable descent direction or duality map.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable and bounded below on the relevant level set.
Model errors are uniformly quadratic inside each trust region.
Trial steps achieve a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point \(x_*\) of accepted iterates satisfies \(f'(x_*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space first-order convergence under a norm trust region and uniformly adequate local models.

notation.meaning: Real Hilbert space; in the Banach-space variant, the ambient Banach space.
Local trust-region model at iteration k, expressed in step coordinates.

review_flags: A precise infinite-dimensional convergence theorem and its Banach-space hypotheses require an authoritative specialist source.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Hilbert-space convergence claim needs a specialist theorem with precise model-accuracy, step-decrease, radius-update, and compactness or accumulation hypotheses. The final sentence also blends a Banach-space variant into the Hilbert-space theorem and denotes its dual by H^* even though H was introduced as a Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal V\) be a real Banach space with dual \(\mathcal V'\), dual pairing \(\langle y,s\rangle=y(s)\), and norms \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal V}\) and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal V'}\). Let \(f:\mathcal V\to\mathbb R\) be Fréchet differentiable. At iteration \(k\), let \(x_k\in\mathcal V\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(m_k\) be a model defined on the closed ball \(\mathcal B_k=\{x_k+s:\|s\|_{\mathcal V}\leq\Delta_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers deterministic trust-region iterations on Banach spaces. In a Hilbert space, the Riesz identification \(\mathcal V'\simeq\mathcal V\) recovers the inner-product formulation. It does not assert convergence or existence of an exact model minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An infinite-dimensional trust-region method is an iteration which, for every \(k\), chooses \(s_k\in\mathcal V\) satisfying \(\|s_k\|_{\mathcal V}\leq\Delta_k\) and \(m_k(x_k+s_k)<m_k(x_k)\), forms the predicted reduction \(P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\), and, after evaluating \(f(x_k+s_k)\), forms \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/P_k\). Given \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\), it sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise, while contracting, retaining, or enlarging \(\Delta_k\) according to the agreement class of \(\rho_k\). The model derivative satisfies \(Dm_k(x_k)\in\mathcal V'\); for a quadratic model, \(m_k(x_k+s)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle H_ks,s\rangle\), where \(g_k\in\mathcal V'\) and \(H_k:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V'\) is bounded. Exact minimization is not required: the step may instead satisfy a prescribed Cauchy-type decrease on a one-dimensional segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method operates on a Banach space \(\mathcal V\). At each iteration it selects a step inside the norm ball of radius \(\Delta_k\), requires positive predicted model reduction, compares actual and predicted reductions through \(\rho_k\), accepts the step when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and updates the radius according to the agreement class. Derivatives belong to the dual space, and a quadratic Hessian is a bounded operator from \(\mathcal V\) to \(\mathcal V'\). A Cauchy-type step is permitted because an exact minimizer over an infinite-dimensional closed ball need not exist.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V\) is a real Banach space and \(f:\mathcal V\to\mathbb R\) is Fréchet differentiable on the region visited by the iteration.
For every \(k\), \(m_k\) is defined on \(\mathcal B_k\), satisfies \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), and admits a feasible step with positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|s_k\|_{\mathcal V}\leq\Delta_k,\quad P_k>0,\quad \rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{P_k},\quad x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&\rho_k\geq\eta_1,\\x_k,&\rho_k<\eta_1.\end{cases}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a Hilbert space, Riesz representation identifies \(Df(x)\in\mathcal V'\) with a gradient in \(\mathcal V\), so the dual pairing becomes the Hilbert inner product.
The trust-region subproblem may be written with an infimum, \(\inf_{\|s\|_{\mathcal V}\leq\Delta_k}m_k(x_k+s)\), without assuming that the infimum is attained.
special_cases_latex: For \(\mathcal V=\mathbb R^n\), the definition is the ordinary finite-dimensional trust-region iteration.
For a Hilbert space and self-adjoint \(H_k\), quadratic curvature is measured by \(\inf_{d\neq0}\langle d,H_kd\rangle/\langle d,d\rangle\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Strong convergence of first-order residuals is naturally measured by \(\|Df(x_k)\|_{\mathcal V'}\).
A Cauchy point remains well defined because its search is restricted to a finite-dimensional segment, even when the full ball is noncompact.
boundary_notes: Closed bounded balls need not be compact in an infinite-dimensional normed space, so an exact model minimizer is not part of the definition.
For a general Banach space, \(-Df(x_k)\) is not automatically a vector in \(\mathcal V\) or a steepest-descent direction; an appropriate duality map or additional regularity is needed.

notation.meaning: Continuous dual of the Banach space.
Ratio of actual to predicted reduction.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be partially separable: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x)\). For each element \(f_i\), let \(\mathcal N_i\neq\{0\}\) satisfy \(f_i(x+w)=f_i(x)\) for all \(x\) and \(w\in\mathcal N_i\), and set \(\mathcal R_i=\mathcal N_i^\perp\). Let \(P_i\) be the orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal R_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the componentwise, partially separable structured family. Each component has its own model and radius; this is distinct from using one scalar radius with a single scaling matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structure-exploiting trust-region method associates to every element \(f_i\), at every iteration \(k\), a model \(m_{i,k}\) and radius \(\Delta_{i,k}>0\). Its elemental region is \(\mathcal B_k^{(i)}=\{x_k+s:\|P_i s\|_k\leq\Delta_{i,k}\}\). The aggregate model and feasible region are \(m_k(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p m_{i,k}(x)\) and \(\mathcal B_k=\bigcap_{i=1}^p\mathcal B_k^{(i)}\). A trial step must satisfy \(x_k+s_k\in\mathcal B_k\) and a structured sufficient-decrease condition based at least on \(\Delta_k^{\min}=\min_i\Delta_{i,k}\). After evaluating the element reductions \(\delta f_{i,k}=f_i(x_k)-f_i(x_k+s_k)\) and \(\delta m_{i,k}=m_{i,k}(x_k)-m_{i,k}(x_k+s_k)\), the method may update each \(\Delta_{i,k}\) separately using its elementwise model-fit test, while overall acceptance is governed by the aggregate reductions \(\sum_i\delta f_{i,k}\) and \(\sum_i\delta m_{i,k}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family applies to an objective decomposed into partially separable element functions. Each element has a low-dimensional range space, its own local model, and its own radius. The overall model is the sum of element models, and the feasible step set is the intersection of the projected elemental trust regions. Component radii can therefore expand or contract independently, while the complete step must remain feasible for every element and provide sufficient aggregate model decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x)\), with invariant subspaces \(\mathcal N_i\) and \(\sum_i\mathcal R_i=\mathbb R^n\).
Each \(m_{i,k}\) depends only on \(P_i x\) and is defined on \(\mathcal B_k^{(i)}\).
The selected step satisfies \(x_k+s_k\in\bigcap_i\mathcal B_k^{(i)}\) and has strictly positive aggregate predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[m_k=\sum_{i=1}^p m_{i,k},\qquad \mathcal B_k=\bigcap_{i=1}^p\{x_k+s:\|P_i s\|_k\leq\Delta_{i,k}\},\qquad \Delta_k^{\min}=\min_i\Delta_{i,k}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When each \(f_i\) depends on a subset of coordinates, \(P_i s\) is the subvector of elemental variables and \(\mathcal B_k\) is an intersection of coordinate cylinders.
For quadratic elements, \(m_{i,k}(x_k+s)=f_i(x_k)+\langle g_{i,k},s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,H_{i,k}s\rangle\), with \(\mathcal N_i\subseteq\ker H_{i,k}\).
special_cases_latex: If the element variable sets are disjoint, the method reduces to independent trust-region iterations on the factors.
If \(p=1\), the construction reduces to a single-model trust-region method.
immediate_consequences_latex: A well-modelled element may retain a large radius even when a poorly modelled element is restricted to a small radius.
The aggregate feasible region contains exactly those steps satisfying every elemental model-validity restriction.
boundary_notes: Cancellation among element reductions prevents blindly interpreting every ratio \(\delta f_{i,k}/\delta m_{i,k}\) when \(\delta m_{i,k}\leq0\); sign-safe element-fit tests are required.
The definition presupposes a supplied partial-separability decomposition and does not prescribe how it is discovered.

notation.meaning: Range subspace containing the variables relevant to element \(i\).

source_refs.locator: Section 10.2.1, “Motivation and Basic Concepts,” equations (10.2.1)–(10.2.4), and Section 10.2.2, pp. 361–364

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured model approximates identified objective components separately while retaining their prescribed coupling and satisfying the required local consistency or accuracy bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\Phi(F_1(x),\ldots,F_q(x))\), where each \(F_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{p_i}\) represents a known component and \(\Phi\) is a known outer function. A structured trust-region model at \(x_k\) is a function \(m_k\) of the form \[m_k(s)=\widehat\Phi_k\bigl(M_{1,k}(s),\ldots,M_{q,k}(s)\bigr),\qquad \|s\|\leq\Delta_k,\] where \(M_{i,k}\) models \(F_i(x_k+s)\), \(\widehat\Phi_k\) preserves the prescribed outer coupling, and \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\). It is first-order consistent when \(m_k'(0)=f'(x_k)\), and fully linear when its value and gradient errors are uniformly \(O(\Delta_k^2)\) and \(O(\Delta_k)\), respectively, throughout the trust region.
assumptions_latex: All component models are defined on \(\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed composition defines a structured trust-region model; derivative matching gives first-order consistency.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a trust-region model that preserves an explicitly identified decomposition of the objective.

notation.meaning: Local model of component i at iteration k.

review_flags: The cited section is provisional and should be checked for this exact structured-model formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual least-squares trust-region model and agreement ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauss–Newton trust-region modeling for nonlinear residual equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a residual map $r$ with Jacobian $J$, let $f(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2$. At $x_k$, the Gauss--Newton trust-region model is
\[
m_k(p)=\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2=f_k+p^TJ_k^Tr_k+\tfrac12p^TJ_k^TJ_kp,
\]
with model Hessian $B_k=J_k^TJ_k$. A trial step approximately solves $\min_p m_k(p)$ subject to $\|p\|\leq\Delta_k$. Whenever the predicted reduction is nonzero, its actual-to-predicted reduction ratio is
\[
\rho_k=\frac{\|r(x_k)\|^2-\|r(x_k+p_k)\|^2}{\|r(x_k)\|^2-\|r(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|^2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonlinear residual equations, the Gauss–Newton trust-region model linearizes the residual and uses J_k^T J_k as model curvature. A trial step approximately minimizes this model within the trust region, and agreement is measured by the ratio of actual residual-norm reduction to the reduction predicted by the linearized residual model, provided that predicted reduction is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k=J_k^TJ_k,\quad p_k\approx\arg\min_{\|p\|\leq\Delta_k}\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2,\quad \rho_k=\frac{\|r_k\|^2-\|r(x_k+p_k)\|^2}{\|r_k\|^2-\|r_k+J_kp_k\|^2}.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Separable Trust Regions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partially separable trust-region model sums low-dimensional element models while enforcing one global step-radius constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) admit the partially separable representation \[f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(U_i x),\] where each linear map \(U_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) has \(n_i\ll n\). A partially separable trust-region model at \(x_k\) is \[m_k(s)=\sum_{i=1}^q m_{i,k}(U_i s),\qquad \|s\|\leq\Delta_k,\] with \(m_{i,k}(0)=f_i(U_i x_k)\). It is first-order consistent if \(m_{i,k}'(0)=f_i'(U_i x_k)\) for every component, in which case \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \(m_k'(0)=f'(x_k)\). The trust-region constraint remains global even though evaluation and derivative assembly are componentwise.
assumptions_latex: The objective has the stated finite partially separable representation.
Each element model is defined for every projected feasible step \(U_i s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise value and derivative consistency imply \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \(m_k'(0)=f'(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partially separable objectives modeled by low-dimensional element functions within one global trust region.

notation.meaning: Linear projection selecting variables used by element i.
Local model of element function i.

review_flags: The supplied inventory lacks a locator specifically supporting partially separable trust-region models.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for the stated partially separable trust-region formulation, component consistency conditions, and use of a single global trust region.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Model Assembly
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value and gradient error bounds add across component models, so controlled componentwise accuracy implies accuracy of the assembled model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(U_i x)\) and \(m_k(s)=\sum_{i=1}^q m_{i,k}(U_i s)\). If, for every \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\), the component errors satisfy \[|f_i(U_i(x_k+s))-m_{i,k}(U_i s)|\leq\kappa_{f,i}\Delta_k^2\] and \[\|U_i^{\mathsf T}(\nabla f_i(U_i(x_k+s))-\nabla m_{i,k}(U_i s))\|\leq\kappa_{g,i}\Delta_k,\] then the assembled model satisfies the corresponding bounds with \(\kappa_f=\sum_i\kappa_{f,i}\) and \(\kappa_g=\sum_i\kappa_{g,i}\). Thus uniform componentwise full linearity yields full linearity of the sum, provided these aggregate constants remain controlled.
assumptions_latex: The objective and model use matching finite-sum decompositions.
The displayed componentwise bounds hold uniformly throughout the global trust region.
The sums of component accuracy constants are finite and controlled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled model has value-error constant \(\sum_i\kappa_{f,i}\) and gradient-error constant \(\sum_i\kappa_{g,i}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of componentwise model-error bounds to an assembled partially separable objective model.
review_flags: The aggregation claim is mathematically direct, but the supplied inventory has no exact source locator for componentwise full-linearity bounds.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The aggregation inequalities follow directly from the triangle inequality and the content kind fits the leaf, but the nontrivial full-linearity interpretation has no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Exploitation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition is not automatically scalable: growing component counts, dense overlap, or uncontrolled aggregate errors can destroy uniform adequacy and computational savings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For assembled models \(m_k=\sum_{i=1}^{q_k}m_{i,k}\), uniformly bounded per-component errors do not by themselves imply a dimension-independent global adequacy constant. Indeed, if each component has value error at most \(\bar\kappa_f\Delta_k^2\), the only general bound is \[|f(x_k+s)-m_k(s)|\leq q_k\bar\kappa_f\Delta_k^2.\] Hence, when \(q_k\) grows and no sparsity, cancellation, weighting, or aggregate-error control is imposed, the full-linearity constant can diverge. Likewise, overlapping dense component supports can make assembly and subproblem solution as costly as an unstructured model. Structural decomposition yields scalable guarantees only when overlap, aggregate constants, and structured linear-algebra costs are controlled.
assumptions_latex: The global model is a finite sum of component models.
Only uniform per-component error bounds are assumed; no aggregate bound or cancellation is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global error constant may grow as \(q_k\), so dimension-independent model adequacy and computational savings need not hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: When decomposition alone fails to give dimension-independent model adequacy or computational savings.

notation.meaning: Number of active model components at iteration k.
Common upper bound on component value-error constants.

review_flags: A specialist source is needed for the broader scalability boundary and structured linear-algebra claim.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The additive error counter-bound is sound, but the broader assertions about dense overlap, subproblem cost, and scalable structured linear algebra require a specialist source. The failure-boundary content kind is appropriate.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\) be the current iterate, and let \(L_k\) be a finite ordered set of trial levels. A level \(\ell\in L_k\) supplies a model \(m_{k,\ell}\), radius \(\Delta_{k,\ell}>0\), feasible step \(s_{k,\ell}\), and evaluation cost \(c_{k,\ell}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This operational definition covers nested-radius searches and interfaces that compare several model or globalization levels. It does not require the models themselves to be nested functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hierarchical trust-region interface is a family of finite-level trial systems for which, at every outer iteration \(k\), each level \(\ell\) satisfies \(\|s_{k,\ell}\|_k\leq\Delta_{k,\ell}\) and has predicted reduction \(P_{k,\ell}=m_{k,\ell}(x_k)-m_{k,\ell}(x_k+s_{k,\ell})>0\). Levels are ordered so that moving upward represents a declared increase in radius, model fidelity, solution accuracy, or computational cost. Whenever the objective is evaluated, the interface forms \(\rho_{k,\ell}=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_{k,\ell})]/P_{k,\ell}\). A selector chooses a level \(\ell_k\) from the evaluated levels according to a fixed admissibility rule, such as \(\rho_{k,\ell}\geq\eta_1\), and returns \(s_k=s_{k,\ell_k}\) to the outer acceptance mechanism. In the nested-radius case, \(\Delta_{k,0}<\Delta_{k,1}<\cdots\), escalation continues only while agreement remains adequate and step lengths increase; otherwise the best admissible stored level is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface presents the outer iteration with several ordered trial levels. Each level has a model, radius, candidate step, predicted decrease, and possibly a different cost. A level is eligible only if its step is feasible and its predicted reduction is positive. Evaluated levels are compared through their actual-to-predicted ratios, and a fixed selector returns one admissible step. Internal radius enlargement is the special case in which the levels differ only by successively larger radii.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is finite and nonempty for each \(k\).
The selector and escalation rule are fixed before observing the current objective reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k=s_{k,\ell_k},\qquad \ell_k\in\{\ell\in L_k:\rho_{k,\ell}\geq\eta_1\},\qquad \rho_{k,\ell}=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_{k,\ell})}{P_{k,\ell}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The interface may be represented as a finite state machine whose state is the current level and whose transitions are escalation, fallback, acceptance, or rejection.
A nested-radius hierarchy is obtained by setting \(m_{k,\ell}=m_k\) and requiring \(\Delta_{k,\ell+1}\geq\gamma_3\Delta_{k,\ell}\) for some \(\gamma_3>1\).
special_cases_latex: Internal doubling is the case of one model and a hierarchy of increasing radii.
A two-branch interface may compare a descent trial and a negative-curvature trial before returning the one meeting the prescribed decrease test.
immediate_consequences_latex: The outer method receives a single step and agreement ratio even though several internal trials may have been generated.
A maximum number of evaluated levels makes the internal work per outer iteration explicitly bounded.
boundary_notes: The ordering may encode radius, fidelity, or cost, but the definition does not identify these distinct quantities.
Without a fixed selection rule, merely possessing several models is not a hierarchical trust-region interface.

notation.meaning: Finite ordered set of internal trial levels.
Declared cost of producing or evaluating level \(\ell\).

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Globalization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid interface first applies ratio-based trust-region acceptance, then uses a declared fallback decrease test if the trust-region proposal is rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), model \(m_k\), and thresholds \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), compute a trial step \(s_k\) with \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) and predicted reduction \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Evaluate \(\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k))/p_k\). Accept the trust-region step when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), updating \(\Delta_k\) from \(\rho_k\). Otherwise invoke a specified fallback globalization rule, such as backtracking along \(s_k\), and accept only a fallback point satisfying that rule's decrease test. If neither interface succeeds, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and reduce \(\Delta_k\). Output terminates when the chosen criticality test holds.
assumptions_latex: The trial step has positive predicted reduction.
The fallback rule has an explicit sufficient-decrease test and terminates or reports failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted iterate satisfies either the trust-region ratio test or the declared fallback globalization test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface combining trust-region acceptance with a fallback globalization mechanism.
review_flags: The source supports the trust-region interface provisionally; the hybrid fallback formulation needs a more specific locator.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the hybrid-interface leaf, but the cited basic trust-region algorithm does not specifically support the fallback globalization interface, its decrease test, or the combined failure policy. A hybrid trust-region/line-search source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Multilevel Trust-Region Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilevel interface prolongs a consistent coarse correction but accepts it only through reduction measured on the fine objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let level \(L\) be the finest level and choose a coarser level \(\ell<L\) with restriction \(R_\ell\) and prolongation \(P_\ell\). At fine iterate \(x_k\), construct a coarse model \(m_{\ell,k}\) whose value and restricted first derivative agree with the fine objective at the coarse origin. Approximately minimize \(m_{\ell,k}(d)\) subject to \(\|P_\ell d\|\leq\Delta_k\), and set \(s_k=P_\ell d_k\). Compute predicted reduction from the corrected model and actual reduction from the fine objective. Accept \(x_k+s_k\) only when their ratio exceeds the acceptance threshold; otherwise reject the correction and reduce the radius or return to a finer-level model. Stop using a fine-level criticality measure.
assumptions_latex: Restriction and prolongation operators map consistently between the selected levels.
The coarse model matches the fine value and restricted first derivative at the current point.
Acceptance uses the fine objective for actual reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted coarse correction is radius-feasible and passes a fine-objective actual-to-predicted reduction test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coarse-level correction embedded in a fine-level trust-region acceptance mechanism.

notation.meaning: Restriction from the fine level to level ell.
Prolongation from level ell to the fine level.

review_flags: A precise multilevel trust-region algorithm and consistency locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Multifidelity Trust-Region Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A corrected low-fidelity model must agree uniformly with the high-fidelity objective, while acceptance is decided from high-fidelity actual reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_H\) be the high-fidelity objective and let \(m_k^L\) be a corrected low-fidelity model on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\). The interface is fully linear when constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\), independent of \(k\), satisfy \[|f_H(x_k+s)-m_k^L(s)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\qquad \|\nabla f_H(x_k+s)-\nabla m_k^L(s)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\] for all \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\), with \(m_k^L(0)=f_H(x_k)\). A step proposed by \(m_k^L\) is accepted using \(f_H(x_k)-f_H(x_k+s_k)\) divided by the low-fidelity predicted reduction; low-fidelity reduction alone is not an acceptance certificate.
assumptions_latex: The high-fidelity objective is continuously differentiable on each trust region.
The corrected low-fidelity model and its gradient are available throughout that region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bounds define a fully linear multifidelity interface, and accepted steps are certified by high-fidelity reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement conditions allowing a low-fidelity model to propose steps accepted using high-fidelity evaluations.

notation.meaning: Corrected low-fidelity model at iteration k.

review_flags: A multifidelity trust-region source is required for the exact correction and fully-linear interface conditions.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The agreement conditions fit the interface leaf, but no source supports the exact correction, fully-linear bounds, or high-fidelity acceptance requirement. The record also combines a model-adequacy condition with an acceptance-policy assertion, so a specialist source is needed to confirm that formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Level Acceptance Coordination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-level steps require positive predicted decrease and a ratio comparing reference-level actual decrease with the proposing level's predicted decrease on a common scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a trial step \(s_k=P_\ell d_k\) proposed at level \(\ell\), define the level-\(\ell\) predicted reduction \(p_{\ell,k}=m_{\ell,k}(0)-m_{\ell,k}(d_k)\) and the reference-level actual reduction \(a_k=f_L(x_k)-f_L(x_k+s_k)\). Cross-level acceptance is admissible only if \(p_{\ell,k}>0\) and \[\rho_{\ell,k}=\frac{a_k}{p_{\ell,k}}\geq\eta,\] where \(0<\eta<1\). Radius enlargement may additionally require \(\rho_{\ell,k}\geq\eta_2>\eta\) and a nearly active trust-region constraint. If objective values from different fidelities are used in \(a_k\), they must first be mapped to a common corrected reference scale; otherwise the ratio has no valid acceptance interpretation.
assumptions_latex: The proposed step is mapped to the reference level by a specified prolongation.
Predicted and actual reductions refer to compatible corrected objective scales.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cross-level proposal is accepted only when \(p_{\ell,k}>0\) and \(\rho_{\ell,k}\geq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common acceptance ratio coordinates proposals and evaluations made at different hierarchy levels.

notation.meaning: Predicted reduction at the proposing level.
Actual reduction measured at the reference level.

review_flags: The common-scale requirement and cross-level radius policy need a dedicated hierarchical trust-region source.

children.top_down_role: Stopping, testing, scaling diagnostics, and coordination of outer and inner computational effort.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Numerical Methods for Unconstrained Optimization and Nonlinear Equations

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth unconstrained trust-region iteration, let \(x_k,s_k,m_k,\Delta_k\) be the current iterate, trial step, model, and radius. Define actual and predicted reductions \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\) and \(P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\). Let \(g_k=\nabla m_k(x_k)\), and let \(\varepsilon_M\) denote unit roundoff.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns deterministic runtime monitoring. Thresholds are user-specified diagnostic tolerances, not universal mathematical constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region execution diagnostic system is a map \(D_k=D(x_k,s_k,m_k,f,\Delta_k)\) whose components include: the agreement ratio \(\rho_k=A_k/P_k\); a criticality measure \(\chi_k=\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_{M_k^{-1}}\) for a positive-definite scaling \(M_k\); the feasibility margin \(v_k=\max\{0,\|s_k\|_k-\Delta_k\}\); a normalized model-decrease measure \(d_k=P_k/[\|g_k\|\min\{\|g_k\|/\beta_k,\Delta_k\}]\) when the denominator is positive; a resolution indicator \(r_k=\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}/[\varepsilon_M\max\{1,|f(x_k)|\}]\); and an effort counter \(e_k\) for inner work. A diagnostic event is any declared predicate on \(D_k\), such as termination, unreliable agreement, insufficient inner decrease, radius stagnation, or excessive inner work. The system is scale-aware when its criticality and step tests transform consistently under a declared variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagnostic system records mathematically defined quantities that explain an iteration: agreement, criticality, feasibility of the step, achieved model decrease relative to a Cauchy scale, numerical resolution of the reductions, and inner computational effort. A diagnostic is a threshold predicate on these quantities. This separates the observed symptoms from the acceptance and radius-update rules that act on them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D_k=(\rho_k,\chi_k,v_k,d_k,r_k,e_k),\qquad \rho_k=\frac{A_k}{P_k},\quad v_k=(\|s_k\|_k-\Delta_k)_+.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The diagnostic output may be represented as a labelled event set \(\mathcal E_k=\{j:\Phi_j(D_k)=\mathrm{true}\}\).
For Euclidean scaling \(M_k=I\), the criticality component reduces to \(\chi_k=\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: If both \(|A_k|\) and \(|P_k|\) are at the roundoff scale, \(r_k\) identifies an agreement ratio that should not be interpreted literally.
If \(v_k>0\), the returned step violates the trust-region constraint independently of its objective reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Agreement failure, insufficient model decrease, and numerical-resolution failure are distinguishable events.
Effort counters permit an oversolving diagnostic without changing the mathematical acceptance test.
boundary_notes: A diagnostic records conditions; it does not itself prove that a particular component caused poor progress.
The ratios are unsuitable when \(P_k\leq0\); that case must be reported as a model or subproblem failure.

source_refs.locator: Sections 17.4.1–17.4.4, especially “Computing the Value of rho_k,” “Stopping Conditions,” and “Noise and/or Expensive Function Evaluations,” pp. 825–831

children.title: Outer Termination-Criticality Diagnostic System
children.top_down_role: Termination and progress-diagnostic families for the outer trust-region iteration.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be smooth and let \(x_k,s_k,\Delta_k\) be an outer trust-region state. Let \(M_k\succ0\) be a scaling or preconditioning matrix, let \(x^{\mathrm{typ}}\) and \(M^{\mathrm{typ}}\succ0\) be reference scales, and choose tolerances \(\epsilon_g,\epsilon_x,\epsilon_\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition addresses smooth unconstrained outer iterations. Constraint feasibility and KKT residuals require the corresponding constrained variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An outer termination-criticality diagnostic system consists of the scaled criticality residual \(\chi_k=\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_{M_k^{-1}}\), its reference value \(\chi_{\mathrm{typ}}=\|\nabla f(x^{\mathrm{typ}})\|_{(M^{\mathrm{typ}})^{-1}}\), the radius-resolution residual \(u_k=\Delta_k/\max\{1,\|x_k\|\}\), and the componentwise step residual \(w_k=\max_i |(s_k)_i|/\max\{1,|(x_k)_i|\}\). It declares first-order termination when \(\chi_k\leq\epsilon_g\max\{1,\chi_{\mathrm{typ}}\}\). It declares resolution-limited termination when \(u_k\leq\epsilon_\Delta\) or \(w_k\leq\epsilon_x\), provided this exit is labelled separately from criticality. Optional resource limits, such as a maximum iteration or evaluation count, are also separate noncritical exits. Thus the system returns both a Boolean stop decision and a reason code distinguishing approximate stationarity from numerical or resource exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The outer diagnostic uses a scaled gradient norm to test approximate first-order stationarity. It separately monitors whether the trust-region radius or every step component is too small to change the represented iterate. The final output includes the stopping reason, so a numerically stalled run is not reported as a stationary solution.
assumptions_latex: All tolerances are positive and fixed independently of the current residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{stop}_k=\bigl[\chi_k\leq\epsilon_g\max\{1,\chi_{\mathrm{typ}}\}\bigr]\lor[ u_k\leq\epsilon_\Delta]\lor[w_k\leq\epsilon_x]\lor[\text{resource limit}],\] with mutually distinguishable exit labels.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(M_k=I\), the first-order test is a relative Euclidean gradient test.
A componentwise resolution test may use \(|(s_k)_i|<\varepsilon_M|(x_k)_i|\) for every nonzero component.
special_cases_latex: An absolute criticality test is obtained by taking the reference factor equal to one.
For a constrained problem, \(\chi_k\) is replaced by a scaled KKT, projected-gradient, or reduced-gradient residual and is accompanied by a feasibility residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: A criticality exit certifies only the stated tolerance, not exact stationarity.
A radius-resolution exit identifies stagnation without asserting that \(\nabla f(x_k)\) is small.
boundary_notes: The unscaled test \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\epsilon_g\) is sensitive to objective and variable scaling.
A small step caused by an inaccurate inner solve must not automatically be classified as outer criticality.

notation.meaning: Radius relative to the iterate scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer Iteration Stopping Criteria
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient tolerance certifies approximate first-order stationarity; small steps, small objective changes, or exhausted budgets require distinct stagnation or limit statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For continuously differentiable unconstrained minimization, terminate the outer iteration at \(x_k\) with first-order tolerance \(\varepsilon_g>0\) only when \[\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_g.\] If objective and step tolerances are also monitored, conditions such as \(|f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})|\leq\varepsilon_f(1+|f(x_k)|)\) or \(\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|\leq\varepsilon_x(1+\|x_k\|)\) are stagnation tests, not independent stationarity certificates. They may trigger termination only with an explicit stagnation status or together with the criticality test. Hitting an iteration, evaluation, or time limit returns a resource-limit status rather than convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable near the final iterate.
The reported gradient or criticality measure is evaluated with adequate numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence termination requires \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_g\); other exits must be labeled separately unless paired with this test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order termination test for unconstrained outer trust-region iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Measure Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model criticality certifies true stationarity only with derivative consistency or an explicit model-gradient error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For unconstrained minimization with differentiable model \(m_k\), define \(\chi_k=\|
abla m_k(0)\|\). If the model is first-order consistent, \(
abla m_k(0)=
abla f(x_k)\), then \(\chi_k\leq\varepsilon_g\) certifies \(\varepsilon_g\)-first-order stationarity. If only \(\|
abla f(x_k)-
abla m_k(0)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\) is known, then the verifiable implication is \[\|
abla f(x_k)\|\leq\chi_k+\kappa_g\Delta_k.\] Consequently, termination based on \(\chi_k\) is justified only when both \(\chi_k\) and the model-error term are below allocated tolerances. A diagnostic must flag nonfinite values, inconsistent scaling, or a criticality measure small solely because \(\Delta_k\) is small.
assumptions_latex: The objective and model are differentiable at the current iterate.
A derivative-matching identity or a certified model-gradient error bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The true gradient obeys \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\chi_k+\kappa_g\Delta_k\), yielding a checkable termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic consistency checks for a model-based first-order criticality measure.

knowledge_statements.title: False Termination Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tiny steps, tiny radii, or a zero gradient from an inaccurate model can occur far from stationarity and cannot alone justify convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Neither a small accepted step nor a small trust-region radius implies stationarity. For \(f(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), \(
abla f(x)=1\) everywhere, yet a radius sequence \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\) forces every feasible trial step to satisfy \(|s_k|\leq\Delta_k	o0\). Thus any rule terminating solely because \(\|s_k\|\leq\varepsilon_x\) or \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon_\Delta\) can declare convergence at a nonstationary point. Likewise, an inaccurate model with \(
abla m_k(0)=0\) may produce zero model criticality while \(
abla f(x_k)
eq0\). False termination is excluded only by checking a reliable objective criticality measure or a model measure accompanied by a certified derivative-error bound.
assumptions_latex: A stopping rule uses only step size, radius, or an uncertified model criticality measure.
No reliable objective-gradient or derivative-error check is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Such a stopping rule may terminate with \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|>0\), as shown by \(f(x)=x\) with \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Stagnation Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagnation occurs when accepted iterations produce negligible cumulative decrease over a fixed window while at least one recent criticality measure remains above tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For accepted iterates \(x_k\), define actual decrease \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\) and a first-order criticality measure \(\chi_k\ge 0\). Given a window length \(w\in\mathbb N\), progress tolerance \(\tau_f>0\), and stationarity tolerance \(\varepsilon_g>0\), declare progress stagnation at iteration \(k\ge w\) when
\[
\sum_{j=k-w}^{k-1}\max\{a_j,0\}\le \tau_f\max\{1,|f(x_{k-w})|\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{k-w\le j\le k}\chi_j>\varepsilon_g.
\]
The second inequality excludes legitimate termination: small accumulated decrease alone is not evidence of stagnation when every recent iterate is approximately stationary.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x_j)\) and \(\chi_j\) are finite for the inspected iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=k-w}^{k-1}\max\{a_j,0\}\le \tau_f\max\{1,|f(x_{k-w})|\}\) together with \(\max_{k-w\le j\le k}\chi_j>\varepsilon_g\) diagnoses nonstationary progress stagnation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic separating insufficient objective progress from approximate first-order termination.

notation.meaning: Actual objective decrease on accepted iteration k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The windowed decrease predicate and its particular normalization and thresholds are implementation-specific; the cited basic-algorithm section does not inspectably support this exact stagnation rule. The mathematical convention therefore requires a direct diagnostic or stopping-criteria source.
